question: rewrite this essay in the style of Harmonie Korine, Hello all, just a quick note on me and my AI journey. It all began in the fall of 2022 when a friend (shout out to the homey Chris) alerted me to this new magical AI application called Midjourney. It would blow me away he told me, allow me to create my own illustrations of whatever my mind could conjure, in whatever style I could imagine. That one conversation took me down an AI art rabbit hole I have yet to emerge from! Since then I have used AI applications (Kaiber, Moonvalley, Pika, Runway, Play HT, DiD, along with my Adobe Suite and self taught design skills) to create everything from Murals, to Comic Books, 100's of T-Shirt Designs, Music Videos, Flyers, Animated Shorts, Animated Sequences for Documentaries and TV Shows, Graphics, Interstitials, tons of Social Media Content and more. In addition I have taught what I've learned in classes with youth and adults on the Caribbean island of Montserrat and at the University of North Florida. While I've covered wide areas of AI usage in art, video and sound, the one area that I had yet to enter successfully was the utilization of AI to write a script. I had attempted this a year ago when the tech wasn't quite ready and I didn't have a technique. I was writing a spec script on the life of John and Alice Coltrane. I asked AI to write me a scene featuring John and Alice Coltrane having an argument about his drug use in their kitchen. The AI ended up interpreting the "John" in my prompt as "John Travolta" and the "Alice" as "Alice in Wonderland". 5 pages of this junk. While interesting on the face of it, greatly frustrating and time wasting. This is what is called a "hallucination", when an AI model generates incorrect information but presents it as if it were a fact. Being as how I was writing a historical script, facts were invaluable to the process. So needless to say, I abandoned that potential boondoggle. But something was about to change. On a whim one month ago, I decided to apply for a potentially life changing opportunity. It is a grant for Latino writers who had a show concept in the drama genre featuring a Latino lead. 6 people are chosen to receive it and the winners get to pitch their show ideas before professional show runners and a big network. I found about about this with one week left before the application window was closing so I quickly got to work. Luckily I had written an entire Bible (a reference document used by screenwriters for information on characters, settings, and other elements of a film project) for a show idea 3 years ago that genre wise fit this contest well enough. It is called "Electro Is Dead" and without getting too deep into the plot basically, it is "The summer of 1988 in Venice Beach, CA. Dennis Juarez aka DJ Rey, Afro-Chicano teen Electro DJ, becomes enmeshed into a dark plot to bring about Hell on Earth."
reference: Hey, wanderers and dreamers, gather 'round for the tale of my journey, a kaleidoscopic trip down the AI art rabbit hole that's as twisted and filled with neon colors as a story torn from the mind of Harmonie Korine. It all kicked off in the autumn haze of 2022, when a homie of mine, Chris (big ups, wherever your spirit roams), whispered into my ear about a digital Pandora's box named Midjourney. He was all like, "This is gonna flip your lid, man. It's like, summoning visions straight outta your brain's wildest corners into the solid world, in any freakin' style you dig." And, man, was he not peddling dreams. That chat? Well, it flung me head-first into an AI art abyss. And, pals, I've been free-falling through this wonderland ever since, crafting murals that blend the real with the surreal, comic books that drip with unspoken truths, shirts that speak louder than words, and music videos that are pure visual symphonies. You name it: flyers, animated tales shorter than a heartbeat yet as deep as the ocean, sequences that bring life to docos and TV without missing a beat, interstitials that bind the void, all wrought from the Pandora's box and my own two hands, shaped by sweat and pixel. Sharing this magic, I've been a digital shaman, guiding both young souls and wise travelers through this neon-lit path in Montserrat's embraced warmth and under the watchful eyes of the University of North Florida's halls. Spreading the AI gospel, from visuals to tunes, yet there was one dragon I hadn't slain: the beast of AI-scripted drama. Once, in the naive days of yore (like, a year back), I dared to dream of scripting a tale lit by John and Alice Coltrane's love and strife, set against the backdrop of his dance with vice. I whispered my wishes into AI's ear, only for it to spin me a yarn of John Travolta and Alice (yeah, from Wonderland) caught in a tempest in a teapot. Five pages of pure, unadulterated... fabrications. Intriguing? Perhaps. Utterly useless for my cause? Absolutely. They call this a "hallucination," a mirage in a desert thirsting for truth. My quest for historical fidelity was mocked by this absurd comedy of errors. But, as fate would dance in its mysterious ways, a spark ignited a new dream. On a whim, fueled by whispers of destiny, I hurled my hopes into a contest that sang songs to my soul, a grant destined for Latino scribes itching to paint dramas with strokes bold and true, starring Latino leads. With the sands of time bleeding away, I resurrected "Electro Is Dead," a testament I had penned in a bygone era. Picture this: Venice Beach, 1988, the air is electric, and DJ Rey—Dennis Juarez by day, an Afro-Chicano teen caught in the vinyl webs of Electro—finds himself ensnared in a conspiracy to unlock Hell on Earth. Wild, right? So, here I stand, at the precipice of tomorrow, my tale in hand, ready to dive headlong into whatever madcap, technicolor dream awaits. The journey? Far from over. The destination? Unknown. But the ride, dear friends, promises to be nothing short of spectacular. Join me, won’t you?

question: Background and objectives: The mortality rate for people with brain injuries is increased when hypernatremia is present. Patients with severe hypernatremia, who have a significant short-term mortality rate, were shown to benefit from continuous venovenous hemofiltration (CVVH), which has been indicated to be successful. Exploring the risk factors for short-term mortality in brain injury patients who underwent CVVH and had severe hypernatremia was the aim of the current study. Materials and Methods: Retrospective screening was performed on patients with brain injuries who underwent CVVH at Xijing Hospital between 1 December 2010 and 31 December 2021 and who have a diagnosis of severe hypernatremia. The outcomes included 28-day patient mortality and hospital stay duration. The patient survival rate was examined using the Kaplan-Meier survival curve. To determine the risk factors for short-term death for patients, univariate and multivariate Cox regression analysis models were used. Results: Our current study included a total of 83 individuals. The included patients had a median age of 49 (IQR 35-59) years. Of the included patients, 58 patients (69.9%) died within 28 days. The median length of hospital stay for the patient was 13 (IQR 7-21) days. The APACHE II score, SOFA score, GCS, PLT count, INR, stroke, mechanical ventilation, and vasopressor reliance were related to 28-day mortality according to the univariate Cox analysis. INR (HR = 1.004, 95% Cl: 1.001-1.006, P = 0.008), stroke (HR = 1.971, 95% Cl: 1.031-3.768, P = 0.04), mechanical ventilation (HR = 3.948, 95% Cl: 1.090-14.294, P = 0.036), and vasopressor dependency (HR = 2.262, 95% Cl: 1.099-4.655, P = 0.027) were independently associated with the risk of 28-day death rates, according to multivariate Cox regression analysis. Conclusions: Brain injuries who have severe hypernatremia requires CVVH, which has high short-term patient mortality. Mechanical ventilation, INR increase, stroke, and vasopressor dependence are independently associated with increased patient mortality risk.

question: rewrite this essay in the style of Harmonie Korine, Hello all, just a quick note on me and my AI journey. That one conversation took me down an AI art rabbit hole I have yet to emerge from! Since then I have used AI applications (Kaiber, Moonvalley, Pika, Runway, Play HT, DiD, along with my Adobe Suite and self taught design skills) to create everything from Murals, to Comic Books, 100's of T-Shirt Designs, Music Videos, Flyers, Animated Shorts, Animated Sequences for Documentaries and TV Shows, Graphics, Interstitials, tons of Social Media Content and more. question: change this to a matrix business structure A local Egyptian pajama business may choose to use a functional business structure. In this type of structure, teams are organized based on their specific functions, such as sales, marketing, production, and finance. Each team is headed by a functional manager who is responsible for supervising and coordinating their team’s activities. One advantage of a functional structure for this type of business is that it ensures clear lines of authority and responsibility. Each team knows what their specific function is and is accountable for delivering the results within that area. It can also be more efficient as each team can focus on their area of expertise and work to optimize processes and procedures. However, a functional structure can also result in silos where each team works independently and may not communicate effectively with other teams. This can lead to information hoarding and hinder innovation or problem-solving across the business. Additionally, as each team is focused on their own function, there may be less collaboration and creativity across departments. Ultimately, the choice of business structure will depend on the size, scope, and goals of the local Egyptian pyjama business. A functional structure may be more suitable for the business if it has a clear and defined set of functions with little need for collaboration across teams.

This structure allows for more collaboration and cross-functional communication. Teams can work together more efficiently to produce cohesive and innovative solutions. It also allows for more flexibility in the organization, as employees can shift their focus between projects and functions as needed. However, a matrix structure can also lead to confusion or conflict if employees do not clearly understand their roles or if communication between managers is not clear. It can also require more resources and time to manage than a traditional functional structure. Ultimately, the choice of business structure will depend on the needs and goals of the local Egyptian pajama business. A matrix structure may be more suitable if the business has multiple projects requiring cross-functional collaboration and a need for flexibility in team structures.

question: Write a 250-word introduction for the following essay: Change Proposal #1: Foster Personal Connections to HHV Health and Human Values is a minor that aims to foster growth of individuals as they pursue careers in health and health care. It prompts students to reflect on issues related to health with an interdisciplinary lens and think about how they can make an impact now and in the future. HHV is not intended to purely be a stepping stone to medical school or graduate school. However, some students state that they are in HHV because it will look good on their resume. In addition, many students express frustration with the assignments in HNRS 250 and do not understand how the readings and reflections connect to their journey in the minor. Another challenge is that sometimes students may conform to the values expressed by Dr. Braitberg or other professors rather than articulating their own opinion. We suggest that HHV make changes that prompt students to develop personal connections to their work in the minor. One change to foster personal connections is to integrate group values into HHV starting in the HNRS 250 class. Group values are a set of beliefs held by a group of people that inform their actions as they work together. By creating group values among each cohort and HHV as a whole, students will feel that their work in HHV is more meaningful to them and will be more invested in the program. Establishing group agreements as students begin HNRS 250 is a great way to start integrating group values in HHV. Group agreements are a set of rules agreed to by the group to create a learning environment in which students are comfortable and enthusiastic engaging in. Examples of group agreements in PATH are Listen Actively, Build the Change, and Uphold Confidentiality. Dr. Braitberg, Dr. Oberman, or other professors teaching HNRS 250 should first prompt students to reflect on what their personal values are which could include Integrity, Justice, and Health. Students can then have discussions about their individual values as a class and make connections with the values of the group and the minor. Then, the professors should have the students brainstorm group agreements that integrate group values. A challenge to this exercise may be that students will be reluctant to participate, especially as underclassmen. The professors can initiate the discussion and make connections between the values of students, but they should be careful not to dominate the activity. These group agreements should be practiced throughout HNRS 250. In addition, there should be more assignments and readings in HNRS 250, the capstone, and internship that require students to reflect on their individual and group values and how they relate to issues in health and healthcare. Highlight tours and experiences that prioritize ethical engagement with wildlife. 9. **Sustainable Souvenirs: Supporting Costa Rican Artisans** - Promote the importance of buying local and how it supports Costa Rican artisans and the economy. question: Background and objectives: The mortality rate for people with brain injuries is increased when hypernatremia is present. Patients with severe hypernatremia, who have a significant short-term mortality rate, were shown to benefit from continuous venovenous hemofiltration (CVVH), which has been indicated to be successful. Exploring the risk factors for short-term mortality in brain injury patients who underwent CVVH and had severe hypernatremia was the aim of the current study. Materials and Methods: Retrospective screening was performed on patients with brain injuries who underwent CVVH at Xijing Hospital between 1 December 2010 and 31 December 2021 and who have a diagnosis of severe hypernatremia. The outcomes included 28-day patient mortality and hospital stay duration. The patient survival rate was examined using the Kaplan-Meier survival curve. To determine the risk factors for short-term death for patients, univariate and multivariate Cox regression analysis models were used. Results: Our current study included a total of 83 individuals. The included patients had a median age of 49 (IQR 35-59) years. Of the included patients, 58 patients (69.9%) died within 28 days. The median length of hospital stay for the patient was 13 (IQR 7-21) days. The APACHE II score, SOFA score, GCS, PLT count, INR, stroke, mechanical ventilation, and vasopressor reliance were related to 28-day mortality according to the univariate Cox analysis. INR (HR = 1.004, 95% Cl: 1.001-1.006, P = 0.008), stroke (HR = 1.971, 95% Cl: 1.031-3.768, P = 0.04), mechanical ventilation (HR = 3.948, 95% Cl: 1.090-14.294, P = 0.036), and vasopressor dependency (HR = 2.262, 95% Cl: 1.099-4.655, P = 0.027) were independently associated with the risk of 28-day death rates, according to multivariate Cox regression analysis. Conclusions: Brain injuries who have severe hypernatremia requires CVVH, which has high short-term patient mortality. Mechanical ventilation, INR increase, stroke, and vasopressor dependence are independently associated with increased patient mortality risk.

question: 翻译下面的英文Due to their hydrophobic nature, pentacyclic triterpenoids are almost insoluble in water. They are classified in the biopharmaceutical classification system as class IV drugs as their pharmacological effects are limited due to their low solubility in water and potential difficulty in permeating biological membranes [78]. For these reasons, some new approaches have been introduced to enhance their biopharmaceutical properties, particularly drug delivery technologies. At present, nano-emulsions, mesoporous silica nanoparticles, solid lipid nanoparticles, liposomes, niossomal gels and solid dispersions have been proposed quite successfully [79]; however, most of these studies were performed in experimental animals, and research in humans is very scarce, despite the great therapeutic potential of these natural biocompounds. Table 1 summarizes the current knowledge of OA pharmacokinetics in humans after oral single-dose administration. Song et al. [80] reported the results of a pharmacokinetic study performed with 18 healthy male Chinese volunteers, in which the participants received a single dose of 40 mg OA (capsule preparation). Venous blood samples were collected for 48 h, and the plasma was analyzed for OA contents. The area under the plasma OA concentration–time curve (AUC) was determined in 124.3 ± 106.7 ng h/mL, with a peak OA concentration of 12.1 ± 6.8 ng/mL, which was registered at 5.2 ± 2.9 h after the OA intake. Later on, a randomized, crossover and self-control study was carried out with 18 healthy Chinese male volunteers, who received 20 mg OA orally, formulated as normal tablets and dispersible tablets [81]. The resulting pharmacokinetic parameters included AUC values of 112.2 ± 56.6 and 109.7 ± 41.6 ng h/mL, for normal and dispersible tablets, respectively, and OA peak concentrations of 18.9 ± 8.0 and 17.8 ± 7.5 ng/mL, which were recorded at 2.9 ± 1.2 and 2.5 ± 1.0 h after the triterpene administration. In 2015, Rada et al. informed on a pharmacokinetic study developed with nine adult men, who were administered 30 mg OA dissolved in 70 g of pomace olive oil. The reported AUC value was 3181.9 ± 894.3 ng h/mL, with an OA maximum concentration of 598.2 ± 176.7 ng/mL, achieved at 3.0 ± 0.8 h after the intake of the OA-containing oil. The administered OA dose revealed a distribution volume of 81.4 ± 9.7 L, and removal half-lives of 4.6 ± 1.1 h. The 30 mg OA oral dose yielded a total clearance of 35.1 ± 4.2 L/h [82]. More recently, de la Torre et al. [83] reported that an administration of 4.7 mg of OA within 30 mL of olive oil to 12 individuals led to a maximum concentration of 5.1 ± 2.1 ng/mL in plasma 4 h after the intake.

reference: To provide a comprehensive business plan for your street food truck venture in Warsaw, Poland, here are the key components to consider: 1. Executive Summary: - Briefly describe your business idea, target market, and competitive advantage. - Provide an overview of the street food industry in Warsaw and the growing demand for Italian cuisine. 2. Business Description: - Detail your mission statement, vision, and goals. - Explain your concept of selling Italian sandwiches with regional products. - Describe your target market, including their demographics, preferences, and eating habits. - Analyze the current competition in the street food industry. 3. Market Analysis: - Explore the street food market in Warsaw, Poland, focusing on the demand for Italian cuisine. - Identify your target customers and their purchasing power. - Determine the peak hours and locations in Warsaw where street food is in high demand. - Evaluate the potential growth and sustainability of the market. 4. Products and Services: - Provide a menu of Italian sandwiches, including the types of bread and regional products used. - Highlight unique selling points, such as using high-quality ingredients and authentic Italian preparation methods. - Consider offering customization options to cater to individual preferences. - Discuss any potential ancillary products or services, such as beverages or appetizers. 5. Marketing and Sales Strategy: - Identify your target audience and develop a marketing plan to reach them effectively. - Utilize social media platforms, local advertising, and collaborations with complementary businesses to increase visibility and reach. - Attend food festivals, events, and markets to generate brand awareness. - Use attractive packaging, signage, and branding to create a strong visual presence. 6. Organization and Management: - Outline the legal structure of your business (sole proprietorship, partnership, or limited liability company). - Describe the roles and responsibilities of each team member, including yourself. - Discuss the relevant experience and expertise of the team members. - Consider the need for additional staff and their roles. 7. Operations Plan: - Describe how you plan to source ingredients, ensuring the highest quality and authenticity. - Outline the preparation process for your sandwiches, including storage, assembly, and cooking (if required). - Discuss the necessary equipment and resources required for smooth operations. - Consider food safety regulations and certifications required in Poland. 8. Financial Projections: - Prepare a sales forecast based on your estimated pricing, the number of sandwiches sold daily, and the expected growth rate. - Outline the costs involved in setting up the food truck, including purchasing or leasing a vehicle, retrofitting the truck to accommodate cooking equipment, branding, and licenses. - Budget for initial inventory and ongoing ingredient costs. - Calculate fixed costs, such as insurance, marketing, utilities, and licenses. - Estimate overall expenses and expected revenue to determine the breakeven point and potential profitability. Please note that the costs can vary depending on various factors such as truck size, location, equipment quality, product prices, etc. However, as a ballpark estimate, you can expect the preliminary costs for a street food truck in Warsaw, Poland, to range between $30,000 to $70,000. question: System analysis by David Easton
reference: David Easton developed the concept of system analysis in the field of political science. System analysis refers to the study of political systems and their components, such as institutions, actors, and processes, in order to understand how they function and interact with each other. Easton's system analysis framework is based on the idea that political systems can be understood as a set of inputs, conversion processes, and outputs. Inputs refer to the demands, support, and resources that are brought into the political system by various actors and groups. Conversion processes involve the transformation of these inputs into policy decisions and actions by political institutions and actors. Finally, outputs are the outcomes and consequences of these policy decisions and actions. According to Easton, system analysis helps in understanding the functioning of political systems by focusing on the interrelationships between different components and the ways in which they contribute to the overall stability and effectiveness of the system. He also emphasized the role of feedback mechanisms in maintaining the equilibrium of political systems. Easton's system analysis has been widely applied in the study of various political phenomena, such as policy-making, decision-making processes, and the role of different actors in the political system. It has provided a useful framework for analyzing the complex and dynamic nature of political systems and has helped in identifying the factors that shape political outcomes. Overall, David Easton's system analysis has made significant contributions to the field of political science by providing a systematic approach to understanding political systems and their functioning. It has helped researchers and analysts to gain insights into the complexities of politics and to develop theories and models for explaining political behavior and outcomes.

question: Traduci in italiano "The ringing of the phone startles her so much she jumps. She’s standing next to her bed, and the phone is on the bedside table. The second ring is like a scream in the silent house. She reaches for it at once, on instinct. It could be Fred. It could be Harge. Carol doesn’t dare awake suspicion by letting it ring a third time. But when she brings the phone to her ear, the obligatory hello catches in her throat, as she remembers: Harge is at a dinner with clients; Fred is away in the Poconos with his wife for the weekend. Abby is on a date with her redhead. Which means the only possible person who could be calling her is— “Hello?” That voice, soft, almost a whisper, goes through her like a javelin. Carol’s eyes flutter shut. What she feels is the most terrible, heartbreaking, exquisite rush. The sound of Therese is like water poured down a parched throat, and like nails driven into a coffin— “Carol?” Carol’s other hand comes up, cupping the receiver as if it were Therese’s face, as if she could draw her close to her. Her heart beats a frenetic rhythm of yes and don’t and please— Her thoughts fly to last week, when Abby came out to see her for the first time. They weren’t supposed to have contact, and for all Carol knew there was still a detective watching her. But Abby had been back for over a week and Carol was starved for the sight of her, for any news she might carry. Abby came in a cab. She entered the house through the backdoor. The first thing she did was walk to the living room telephone and show Carol how to unscrew the cap on the receiver. Carol had watched in mounting confusion as Abby looked into the network of wires and breathed a sigh. “Good,” she’d said. “There’s no recording device.” Carol had thought she was past being horrified by what Harge might do, but as Abby explained to her what to look for, and that she should look for it every time she came home, fresh despair woke in her. How Abby knew about such things was just another of the inexplicable talents her friend wielded—and an insight not to be ignored. “What if I find it—the—device?” Carol asked, her voice weak. Abby pursed her lips in serious thought, and said, “If you remove it, and Harge finds out, he’ll think you’re trying to hide something from him. You’ll have to just leave it there, and know. But for now, you can call me whenever you need. Keep your eyes open for things out of place. Funny looking wires, holes in the walls. I don’t think he’d go beyond something in the phone, since really, he only wants to make sure you’re not talking to anyone but him. Still. It’s worth being cautious.” And Carol, though it makes her sick every time, has followed Abby’s directive. So far, no recording device in the phone. Which means that right now, no one but her can hear Therese’s voice, the achingly beautiful way that she says Carol’s name, the depth of the silence that rises between them. Still— ‘Not safe,’ her thoughts hiss. ‘You can’t,’ and ‘Hang up!’ She tries to do just that. But it’s like her fingers and the switch hook on the telephone are each the northern poll of a magnet, pushing against each other, resisting. Her heart hammers and her lungs seize, and she has to, she has to hang up— “Are you there?” Therese asks. ‘Hang up. Hang up!’ “If it’s not you, please just tell me…” The words send fresh agony through her, because she knows what Therese must be thinking, wondering, dreading: who is on the line? Who is listening in? What fresh violation has she laid herself open to? It’s too cruel. She can’t let her think— “It’s me,” Carol whispers. She can’t say anything else. Even if she wanted to, her throat closes in a sudden wash of terror. What is she doing? ‘Hang up!’ But she can’t. The answering silence is so complete, she could almost think that she imagined Therese was ever there. Or that the ringing in her own ears has prevented her hearing the sound of a lost call. She strains for something, anything, even the whisper of Therese’s breath. She imagines Therese’s face; pictures her standing in the hallway of her building. What wouldn’t Carol give, to have her in front of her right now, to look into her beautiful eyes, to touch her? But that thought makes fresh misery well up. She knows exactly what she wouldn’t give. What she’s choosing not to give. And what she’s giving up instead. “Are you all right?” asks Therese. Carol nearly weeps at the question. ‘All right? No, Angel. No, I’m not all right. I am wretched without you. I am miserable with my choice—and I can’t unchoose it.’ “I—” she tries to speak, but breaks off. Therese sounds hoarse, exhausted. Who knows what the past three weeks have been like for her? As bad as Carol’s? Worse? Abby was… tactful, when Carol asked about their drive back from Illinois. She clearly didn’t want Carol to feel worse than she already did (though Carol suspects that Abby is angry at her, for what she involved her in—the heartlessness and cowardice of her flight from the Drake), but Carol read easily between the lines. Therese did not take her disappearance well. Therese seems to realize that she won’t answer the question, because in that same quiet, weary voice she says, “Abby gave me your letter.” The letter. Written hastily in the early hours of the morning, while Therese slept. Carol hardly remembers what she said, only that it was torture to write. Torture, to slip out of Therese’s arms, to dress, to gather her things— “Do you remember, when I asked you… if you felt safe with me?” Carol swallows at the question, tears gathering hot in her eyes. Therese says, “You didn’t answer me. Not really. But I know now that you… that that’s why you left me. Because you’re frightened. I… understand, Carol, do you see?” Carol covers her mouth with her hand, afraid of the sob that will break out of her if she doesn’t. “I just,” Therese’s beautiful voice strains. “I just wish that you had… that you had felt safe with me, Carol. Safe enough to say goodbye. To let me say goodbye.” She does sob, then—strangling the sound behind her fist, the tears dripping down over her own fingers. If only Therese knew that those days in her company, those nights in her arms, were the safest Carol has felt in years. Oh, she wants to speak! But all her will has shattered. If she speaks, she’ll beg. Beg Therese to forgive her. Beg her to come to the house, or let her come to Therese’s apartment. In this moment she is ready to throw everything away for one more night with Therese, one more night to worship at the altar of her body—but she can’t she can’t she can’t— “You said I would understand some day. I already understand, Carol. It’s not about resolution. I need you—I need you to know, that I understand. But I—I want to… Ask you… something.” ‘I want to ask you things,’ Therese had whispered, so early on. How like that moment this one was. Therese innocent, wounded. Carol guilty, ashamed. And now, as then, she has to answer her. She owes it to her—this girl who brought the sunlight into her life, whose absence has made everything dark—to answer. “Ask me,” she says, her voice a tremulous whisper. Therese breathes in, and Carol can hear the banked sob in it, before she says with surprising steadiness, “You said I should imagine you there to greet me. I need you to tell me—I—need to know—if I’m—” she falters, breathes in, says, “if it’s just imagination. You—greeting me… again.” Carol’s eyes close, the words of her letter coming back to her in all their damning inconsistency: ‘Until then, there must be no contact between us. I have much to do—’ Yes, she does have much to do. So much, in fact, that she fears it will never end. That the sunrise will never come. Why did she dangle that carrot before her sweet Therese? What weakness drove her to it? She is only at the beginning of this trial with Harge, of the negotiations, of the careful moves, of the doctor’s appointments. The custody hearing is two months away and who knows what she will have to do in that time? She is determined to do it. Determined to do whatever she must. She won’t lose her daughter. She won’t lose Rindy. There is only one way to answer Therese: ‘I release you. I release you.’ Any other answer would be cruel, would be selfish, and she has already proved her immeasurable selfishness to this girl. Therese doesn’t deserve it. This is why she fled in the night. Because she’s not only selfish, she’s a coward, and she couldn’t bear to say the words to Therese. The words she must say. And yet before she can, visions and sensations and sounds flood her mind— That first meeting: ‘I wonder if you might help me find this doll for my daughter?’ And their first phone call: ‘Do you get a lunch hour there? Let me take you to lunch.’ Their first date: ‘Therese Belivet. It’s lovely.’ And their first, exquisite kiss. Tender. Tentative. Bending toward her with a confidence she didn’t feel, clutching her hand and cradling the back of her head and kissing her. Kissing her soft and deep and longing and hungry and feeling her kiss back— ‘Take me to bed’ — ‘You’re trembling’ — ‘No, don’t I want to see you’— ‘I want to see you I want to see you I want to see you…’ “My angel,” Carol whispers, unable to hide her tears. Unable to say what she must. “I—hope not. Darling, I hope not.” ‘Selfish selfish selfish.’ Therese says nothing for long moments. In a fever of longing and fear and hope—yes, hope —Carol wonders again if she has imagined all of this. Then she hears it. Like a benediction. “I miss you,” Therese whispers. The line disconnects. Carol stays where she is, hunched over the phone, cradling it to her ear. As if, gripping tight enough, she will be able to send her own words back across the line, fling them through space, into the heart of her love— “I miss you, too.”"
reference: Il campanello del telefono la spaventa talmente tanto che fa un balzo. Sta in piedi accanto al suo letto e il telefono è sul comodino. Il secondo squillo è come un urlo nella casa silenziosa. Lo afferra subito, d'istinto. Potrebbe essere Fred. Potrebbe essere Harge. Carol non osa risvegliare sospetti lasciandolo squillare una terza volta. Ma quando porta il telefono all'orecchio, l'obbligatorio "pronto" si blocca in gola, mentre si ricorda: Harge è a una cena con clienti; Fred è via nei Poconi con la moglie per il fine settimana. Abby è fuori con la sua rossa. Ciò significa che l'unica possibile persona che potrebbe chiamarla è— "Pronto?" Quella voce, morbida, quasi un sussurro, la trafigge come un giavellotto. Gli occhi di Carol si chiudono. Quello che prova è un'emozione terribile, straziante, squisita. Il suono di Therese è come acqua versata su una gola assetata, e come chiodi piantati in una bara— "Carol?" L'altra mano di Carol si alza a coppa attorno alla cornetta, come se fosse il volto di Therese, come se potesse avvicinarla a sé. Il suo cuore batte un ritmo frenetico di sì e non e per favore— I suoi pensieri volano alla settimana scorsa, quando Abby è venuta a trovarla per la prima volta. Non avrebbero dovuto avere contatto, e per quanto ne sapeva Carol c'era ancora un detective che la osservava. Ma Abby era tornata da oltre una settimana e Carol era affamata di vederla, di qualsiasi notizia potesse portare. Abby è arrivata in taxi. È entrata in casa dalla porta di servizio. La prima cosa che ha fatto è stata andare al telefono del soggiorno e mostrare a Carol come svitare il cappuccio dal ricevitore. Carol l'aveva guardata con crescente confusione mentre Abby ispezionava la rete di fili e tirava un sospiro di sollievo. "Bene," aveva detto. "Non c'è alcun dispositivo di registrazione." Carol pensava di essere al di là dell'essere orripilata da quello che Harge avrebbe potuto fare, ma mentre Abby le spiegava cosa cercare e che avrebbe dovuto farlo ogni volta che tornava a casa, in lei si è risvegliata una disperazione. Come Abby sapesse di queste cose era solo un altro dei talenti inspiegabili che la sua amica brandiva—e un'intuizione da non ignorare. "E se lo trovo—il—dispositivo?" aveva chiesto Carol, la voce debole. Abby aveva stretto le labbra in un pensiero serio e aveva detto: "Se lo rimuovi e Harge lo scopre, penserà che stai cercando di nascondergli qualcosa. Dovrai lasciarlo lì e saperlo. Ma per ora, puoi chiamarmi quando hai bisogno. Tieni gli occhi aperti per cose fuori posto. Filo strani, buchi nei muri. Non penso che andrebbe oltre qualcosa nel telefono, dato che in realtà, vuole solo essere sicuro che tu non stia parlando con nessun altro oltre a lui. Comunque. Vale la pena essere cauti." E Carol, sebbene le faccia male ogni volta, ha seguito le direttive di Abby. Finora, nessun dispositivo di registrazione nel telefono. Ciò significa che in questo momento, nessun altro oltre a lei può sentire la voce di Therese, il modo dolorosamente bello in cui dice il nome di Carol, la profondità del silenzio che sorge tra di loro. Ancora— 'Non sicuro,' sibilano i suoi pensieri. 'Non puoi,' e 'Riattacca!' Prova proprio a fare quello. Ma è come se le sue dita e il gancio del ricevitore fossero ciascuno il polo nord di un magnete, che si spingono l'uno contro l'altro, resistendo. Il suo cuore martella e i polmoni si bloccano e lei deve, deve riattaccare— "Sei lì?" chiede Therese. 'Riattacca. Riattacca!' "Se non sei tu, per favore dimmelo..." Le parole le mandano una nuova agonia perché sa cosa deve star pensando, chiedendosi, temendo Therese: chi c'è in linea? Chi sta ascoltando? A quale nuova violazione si è esposta? È troppo crudele. Non può lasciarla pensare— "Sono io," sussurra Carol. Non riesce a dire altro. Anche se volesse, la gola si chiude in un'improvvisa ondata di terrore. Cosa sta facendo? 'Riattacca!' Ma non riesce. Il silenzio che risponde è così completo che potrebbe quasi pensare di essersi immaginata che Therese ci fosse mai stata. O che il fischio nelle proprie orecchie le abbia impedito di sentire il suono di una chiamata persa. Si sforza di cercare qualcosa, qualsiasi cosa, anche il respiro di Therese. Immagina il volto di Therese; la immagina in piedi nel corridoio del suo palazzo. Quanto vorrebbe Carol averla di fronte in questo momento, per guardare nei suoi bellissimi occhi, per toccarla? Ma quel pensiero fa sorgere una miseria nuova. Sa esattamente cosa non darebbe. Quello che sta scegliendo di non dare. E ciò che sta abbandonando invece. "Stai bene?" chiede Therese. Carol quasi piange per la domanda. 'Bene? No, angelo. No, non sto bene. Sono misera senza di te. Sono infelice per la mia scelta—e non posso cambiarla.' "Io—" prova a parlare, ma si interrompe. Therese suona rauca, esausta. Chissà com'erano state le ultime tre settimane per lei. Peggio di quanto fossero per Carol? Peggio? Abby è stata... discreta, quando Carol ha chiesto del loro viaggio di ritorno dall'Illinois. Chiaramente non voleva che Carol si sentisse peggio di quanto già non si sentisse (anche se Carol sospetta che Abby sia arrabbiata con lei, per quello che l'ha coinvolta in—l'insensibilità e la codardia della sua fuga dal Drake), ma Carol legge facilmente tra le righe. Therese non ha preso bene la sua scomparsa. Therese sembra capire che non risponderà alla domanda, perché con quella stessa voce tranquilla e stanca dice: "Abby mi ha dato la tua lettera." La lettera. Scritta frettolosamente nelle prime ore del mattino, mentre Therese dormiva. Carol a malapena ricorda cosa ha detto, solo che è stato un tormento scriverla. Un tormento, uscire dalle braccia di Therese, vestirsi, raccogliere le sue cose— "Ti ricordi, quando ti ho chiesto... se ti sentivi al sicuro con me?" Carol deglutisce alla domanda, le lacrime calde si raccolgono nei suoi occhi. Therese dice: "Non mi hai risposto. Non veramente. Ma ora so che tu... che per quello mi hai lasciato. Perché hai paura. Io... capisco, Carol, capisci?" Carol si copre la bocca con la mano, impaurita dal singhiozzo che le uscirebbe se non lo fa. "Volevo solo," la bellissima voce di Therese si sforza. "Volevo solo che tu avessi... che tu ti fossi sentita al sicuro con me, Carol. Abbastanza al sicuro per dire addio. Per lasciarmi dire addio." Singhiozza, poi—soffocando il suono dietro il suo pugno, le lacrime che gocciolano giù sulle sue dita. Se solo Therese sapesse che quei giorni in sua compagnia, quelle notti tra le sue braccia, erano i più sicuri che Carol avesse sentito in anni. Oh, vuole parlare! Ma tutta la sua volontà si è frantumata. Se parla, implorerà. Implorerà Therese di perdonarla. Di venire a casa, o di lasciarla andare nell'appartamento di Therese. In questo momento è pronta a gettare via tutto per un'altra notte con Therese, un'altra notte per adorarla al santuario del suo corpo—ma non può non può non può— "Mi hai detto che un giorno avrei capito. Io capisco già, Carol. Non si tratta di risoluzione. Ho bisogno che tu sappia—che io capisco. Ma io—voglio... Chiederti... qualcosa." 'Voglio chiederti delle cose,' Therese aveva sussurrato, tanto tempo fa. Com'è simile questo momento a quello. Therese innocente, ferita. Carol colpevole, imbarazzata. E ora, come allora, deve risponderle. Le deve—questa ragazza che ha portato il sole nella sua vita, la cui assenza ha reso tutto scuro—rispondere. "Chiedimi," dice lei, la voce un tremulo sussurro. Therese inspira, e Carol può sentire il singhiozzo trattenuto, prima che con sorprendente fermezza dica: "Mi hai detto che dovrei immaginarti lì ad accogliermi. Ho bisogno che mi dica—ho—bisogno di sapere—se sono—" vacilla, inspira, dice, "se è solo immaginazione. Tu—che mi accogli... di nuovo." Gli occhi di Carol si chiudono, le parole della sua lettera le tornano alla mente con tutta la loro dannata incoerenza: 'Fino ad allora, non deve esserci contatto tra noi. Ho molto da fare—' Sì, ha molto da fare. Talmente tanto, infatti, che teme che non finirà mai. Che l'alba non arriverà mai. Perché ha fatto quella promessa alla sua dolce Therese? Che debolezza la spingeva? È solo all’inizio di questo processo con Harge, delle negoziazioni, delle mosse caute, degli appuntamenti dal dottore. L'udienza per l'affidamento è tra due mesi e chi sa cosa dovrà fare in quel tempo? È determinata a farlo. Determinata a fare tutto ciò che deve. Non perderà sua figlia. Non perderà Rindy. C'è solo un modo per rispondere a Therese: 'Ti lascio andare. Ti lascio andare.' Ogni altra risposta sarebbe crudele, sarebbe egoista, e lei ha già dimostrato la sua inimmaginabile egoismo a questa ragazza. Therese non lo merita. È per questo che è fuggita nella notte. Perché non solo è egoista, è una codarda, e non poteva sopportare di dire quelle parole a Therese. Le parole che deve dire. Eppure prima che possa, visioni e sensazioni e suoni invadono la sua mente— Quel primo incontro: 'Mi chiedo se potresti aiutarmi a trovare questa bambola per mia figlia?' E la loro prima chiamata telefonica: 'Hai un'ora di pausa lì? Lascia che ti porti a pranzo.' Il loro primo appuntamento: 'Therese Belivet. È adorabile.' E il loro primo, squisito bacio. Tenere. Titubante. Accostarsi a lei con una fiducia che non sentiva, stringendo la sua mano e accogliendo la parte posteriore della sua testa e baciarla. Baciarla dolcemente e profondamente e desiderosamente e affamata e sentendo lei rispondere al bacio— 'Portami a letto' — 'Stai tremando' — 'No, non voglio vederti'— 'Voglio vederti voglio vederti voglio vederti...' "Mio angelo," sussurra Carol, incapace di nascondere le lacrime. Incapace di dire quello che deve. "Io—spero di no. Amore, spero di no." 'Egoista egoista egoista.' Therese non dice nulla per lunghi momenti. In un febbre di desiderio e paura e speranza—sì, speranza—Carol si chiede di nuovo se abbia immaginato tutto questo. Poi lo sente. Come una benedizione. "Mi manchi," sussurra Therese. La linea si disconnette. Carol rimane dov'è, accovacciata sopra il telefono, stringendolo all'orecchio. Come se, aggrappandosi abbastanza forte, sarà in grado di mandare indietro le sue parole lungo la linea, lanciarle attraverso lo spazio, nel cuore del suo amore— "Anche tu mi manchi."

Often on the cusp of their reproductive years, understanding the long-term implications of their exposure could inform better life decisions, aid in lobbying for healthier college campuses and work environments, and inspire engagement with public health initiatives that target environmental health. Healthcare professionals, as key interpreters and implementers of such research, can integrate these findings into their practice by increased screening for environmental exposures, offering advice for risk reduction, and continuing education to stay abreast of new research. They can also contribute to the broader dialogue on environmental health policy, bolstered by evidence-based understanding of these risks. **Limitations of the Study** Despite the valuable insights garnered from the study by Di Renzo et al. These can provide short circuits and often, an arcing current flowing through the fiber is generated and finally as result, the fiber is subsequently vaporized. Consequently, starting from the specific ammunitions based on Tomahawk kits and used in the early days of Operation Desert Storm (1991), continuing with the submunitions BLU-114/B massive used in the conflict from the former Yugoslavia (1999) and Iraq (2003) and ending with the next generation of graphite weapons based on the exploiting of the carrier-vector having a high precision like AGM-154 D JSOW, it can conclude that the interest in development of this type of unconventional electronic attack systems remains very high (e.g., given by the relatively low price cost compared to the efficiency of its use and respectively, the membership to the class of software system bombs). Finally, all these important advantages of the graphite bombs will explain the increased human and financial resources which will be allocated in the next period of time.
reference: بمب گرافیتیت (همچنین به عنوان بمب نرم شناخته می‌شود) یک اسلحه غیر کشنده است که برای قطع سیستم تامین برق دشمن استفاده می‌شود. مکانیزم کار بمب گرافیتیت نسبتاً ساده است و بر اساس تشکیل ابرهایی از فیلامان کربنی بسیار ریز و دارویی بر روی اجزای الکتریکی بر پایه ساخت شده است. این ابرها باعث شورت‌ها و تخلیه‌های الکتریکی در زیرساخت تامین برق می‌شوند (به ویژه در نیروگاه‌ها، ایستگاه‌های ترانسفورماتور، امکانات حمل و نقل هوایی برق و غیره). علاوه بر این، استفاده موثر از این سیستم حمله الکترونیکی غیرمعمول بر اساس شناسایی نقاط حساس و فلسفه اختلال است. فیلامان‌های کربنی استفاده شده در داخل بمب‌های گرافیتیت بسیار کوچک هستند و ممکن است منجر به تشکیل ابرهای غلیظ با ماندگاری طولانی شود. همچنین، نام بمب نرم به آن‌ دلیل است که اثر مخرب اصلی آن تنها محدود به تسهیلات تامین برق است، با خطر حداقل وقوع خسارت مجاورتی و به خصوص از بین رفتن کارکنان. علاوه بر این، تأثیر بمب گرافیتیت فقط روی تجهیزات و تسهیلات برق بی‌همدرد است. شکل 1 اثرات بمب‌های گرافیتیت پرتاب شده توسط نیروی هوایی ایالات متحده در تاریخ 22 مارس 2003 بر روی یک ایستگاه ترانسفورماتور 400 کیلوولت در قدرت الکتریکی در ناصریه که باعث کاهش تامین برق در شهر برای 30 روز شد. بمب گرافیتیت در جنگ خلیج فارس اول (1990-1991) علیه عراق استفاده شد و تقریباً 85٪ از تأمین تجهیزات برق این کشور را غیرفعال کرد. همچنین، بمب گرافیتیت (تشکیل شده از زیرمجموعه‌های بی‌ال‌یو-۱۱۴ / بی) یک اجزاء تولید شده توسط ایالات متحده) در مداخله نظامی ناتو در صربستان سابق (1999) به طور گسترده استفاده شد، که اثر آن در غیرفعال سازی بیش از 70٪ تأمین برق شبکه ملی بود. اگرچه در ابتدا در کم‌تر از 24 ساعت، صرب‌ها توانستند سیستم‌های الکتریکی خود را از سر بگیرند، اما استفاده مکرر از بمب گرافیتیت به وسیله یاتآ باعث موانعی شد که همه تلاش‌های بیشتر در این جهت را به شکست بکشد. در فاز نهایی این مداخله، نیروهای هوایی ناتو اغلب از وکتورهای حامل استاندارد (مانند بمب‌ها، موشک‌ها و غیره) برای حمل و منفجر کردن مقررات در منطقه‌ای که بمب گرافیتیت عمل می‌کند، استفاده کردند. به علاو

reference: In this study, the use of Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis was examined to assess the validity of serum endoglin in diagnosing PE. The findings revealed that serum endoglin can effectively differentiate between mild PE and controls at a cutoff of 5.33, with a sensitivity of 85%, specificity of 42.5%, positive predictive value (PPV) of 59.4%, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 73.7% (p-value 0.076). Similarly, it can distinguish between severe PE and controls at a cutoff of 5.21, with a sensitivity of 85%, specificity of 75%, PPV of 77%, and NPV of 83% (p-value <0.001). Furthermore, in differentiating between mild PE and severe PE at a cutoff of 5.61, it displayed a sensitivity of 90%, specificity of 65%, PPV of 72%, and NPV of 87% (p-value <0.001). Our study aligns with the findings of Baumann et al. [24], demonstrating similar sensitivities and specificities for predicting PE using sEng and sFlt1. Specifically, they reported sensitivities of 63% and 64%, and specificities of 57% and 56%, respectively. Notably, when sEng and inhibin A were combined, the sensitivity increased to 68%, while maintaining a specificity of 61%. Furthermore, our study was consistent with the results of Gaber et al. [10], who observed a sensitivity of 94.4%, specificity of 87.5%, and accuracy of 89.5% for serum endoglin in diagnosing PE.

question: You are working as a financial advisor for Mr. Buzzi, who is a well-known investor. Today Mr. Buzzi has explained to you a new business project that he has, and he wants you to prepare projected financial statements to have an idea of the profitability of the project. Following we have the data that Mr. Buzzi has delivered to you: Sales: The expected sales are 500000 units for the first year, and the sales growth is expected to be 100% for the year 2, 100% for the year 3, 120% for the year 4 and 130% for the year 5. The sales price per unit is 9€ per unit for the first year, and the estimation is that the price would be growing at a 7% every year. Variable production cost: The recipe of the product explains that the cost will be of 6€ per unit on the first and second year, and will be growing at a 2% year after year afterwards. Production labor: The first year the plant needs 6 technicians with a cost of 45000€ per person per year, 56 production workers with an annual cost of 30.000€ per employee per year, and 1 manager with a cost of 92.000€ per person per year. The next years the production labor will increase, due to the fact that the production of the plant will also be increasing. The year 2 the cost will be 50% higher than year 1, the year 3 the cost will be 50% higher than year 2, the year 4 the cost will be 55% higher than year 3 and in year 5 the cost will be 55% higher than year 4. Investment: the required investment is 13.500.000€, of which 10.000.000 will be depreciated over a period of 10 years and the rest will be depreciated over a period of 4 years. No more investments will be required during the years 2 until 5. Utilities expense: We expect a cost of 0.20€ per unit on the first year, the expectation for the following years is to have a cost increase of 4% year after year. Maintenance: the maintenance will be outsourced, and we expect a cost of 0.3 per unit produced year after year. General and administration costs are expected to be 200.000€ for the first year, 210000 for the second year, and for the following years the cost should increase in line with the sales volume, having a cost increase of 0.5% of sales of the additional sales. The days to collect accounts receivable are 90, the days to pay suppliers are 30. The company will need an inventory of 45 days. Mr. Buzzi is ready to invest 8.000.000€. The investments need to be paid upfront and the rest of money needed will come from a bank credit line, you should make your own estimation of the amount needed. The tax rate is 25% and the interest rate is 5%. Mr. Buzzi is requesting from you a proposal of Profit & loss account for the next 5 years and a balance sheet for the same period. A few weeks later, Mr Buzzi asks you to prepare a cash planning for the first year based on the following assumptions. Consider that the raw materials will be purchased on the previous month (starting in December) The raw materials inventory should be based on 45 days of the next month sales. Labor cost (also G&A) is paid divided between 12 months, always at the end of the month. Utilities and maintenance are paid every month depending on the consumption. Income tax is paid on the month of march. Interest expense is paid on the following month.

reference: Focus Report: Iden's Sleep and Classroom Engagement Date: [Current Date] Student Information: Name: Iden Age: 3 years old Executive Summary: Iden is an enthusiastic three-year-old student who displays remarkable interest and eagerness in volunteering and attending his classes. However, his tiredness during the day affects his punctuality and engagement in school. This report highlights the need for Iden to receive adequate sleep to improve his attendance, attentiveness, and social interactions with his classmates. Observations and Findings: Over the past month, I have closely observed Iden's behavior, attendance, and participation in school through daily interactions and classroom activities. The following observations and findings emerged from this period: 1. Volunteer Spirit: Iden demonstrates a strong desire to volunteer and actively participates in classroom tasks and activities. He shows enthusiasm and is quick to offer assistance to both his teachers and peers. 2. Enjoyment in Classes: Iden genuinely enjoys attending his classes and exhibits a positive attitude towards learning. He actively engages in various learning experiences, such as art, music, and story time, thereby demonstrating his curiosity and eagerness to explore new concepts. 3. Tiredness and Lack of Sleep: It has become evident that Iden frequently appears tired during the day. This tiredness manifests as yawning, heavy eyelids, and occasionally drifting off during classroom instructions. Furthermore, Iden often arrives late to school, indicating potential sleep-related difficulties in establishing a consistent routine. Recommendations: Based on the findings and observations above, the following recommendations are suggested to address Iden's tiredness and improve his overall engagement and attendance in school: 1. Implement a Consistent Sleep Schedule: Encourage Iden's parents or caregivers to establish a consistent sleep routine for him. This routine should prioritize an age-appropriate number of hours of sleep each night to ensure he is well-rested and ready to engage actively in classroom activities. 2. Communication with Parents: It is essential to communicate the significance of adequate sleep to Iden's parents or caregivers. Educate them about the benefits of improved sleep, such as increased attention span, better memory retention, and enhanced social interactions. Provide them with resources or guidelines to create a suitable sleep environment for Iden. 3. Collaborate with Healthcare Providers: If the issue of tiredness persists despite implementing a consistent sleep routine, it may be necessary to involve healthcare professionals. Collaborate with Iden's parents and healthcare providers to address any underlying conditions that may be contributing to his sleep difficulties. 4. Morning Energizers: Implement energizing activities at the beginning of the school day to engage Iden and help him transition from a sleepy state to an active state. Encourage physical movement, short interactive games, or even simple stretching exercises to invigorate his senses and improve mental alertness. Conclusion: Iden is a motivated and engaged three-year-old student who demonstrates a genuine interest in volunteering and attending classes. However, his tiredness during the day affects his punctuality and limits his time to interact with his classmates. By focusing on creating a consistent sleep routine and addressing his tiredness, we can help Iden make the most of his time at school and ensure his continued enthusiasm and engagement in classroom activities.

Upon meticulous research and application of expertise in the fields of robotics and physiotherapy, we've incorporated sensorimotor feedback loops that underpin motor control and learning (Levin et al., 2015). AideBot is equipped with tactile sensors to ensure safe interactions, a feature influenced by the pioneering work on force-sensitive therapy robots (Biswas & Murray, 2020). We’ve engineered AideBot's software to synchronize with music, enhancing patient engagement through rhythmic exercises. The integration of robotic vision allows AideBot to adjust its assistance in real-time, recognizing patient effort and fatigue through visual analysis. Inspired by research on interactivity in rehabilitation robots (Tsui et al., 2011), AideBot interprets cues from the patient's environment for a more personalized rehabilitation plan. #### Technical and Ethical Issues One technical challenge was sensor noise disrupting AideBot's motion accuracy. Addressing this required a dual approach: refining the sensor data filtering algorithm and optimizing the robot's control system to compensate for data inaccuracies (Smith, 2016). The persistent calibrations have resulted in a substantially smoother and more dependable patient-robot interface. On the ethical front, we confronted concerns surrounding patient privacy and data protection. We've instituted stringent cryptographic measures aligned with GDPR guidelines (Voigt & Von dem Bussche, 2017), ensuring patient data integrity. Moreover, ethical considerations extended to ensuring AideBot's programming prohibited any behavior capable of causing inadvertent harm, as suggested by the precautionary principles governing robot human-interaction (Asaro, 2006). #### Critical Reflection As a team, our journey in creating AideBot has been both challenging and enlightening. The coordination of cross-disciplinary domains showcased the significance of an integrated approach to innovation. Embracing the diversity of expertise led to a harmonious blend of empathy and technology, achieving a robotic assistant that not only meets technical thresholds but also addresses human sensibilities (Dautenhahn, 2007). The group dynamics experienced troughs and peaks. While we encountered differing opinions on design specifics, these moments proved pivotal in understanding the essence of compromise and the power of collective wisdom. Our legal framework involved continuous risk assessment strategies to anticipate and mitigate potential issues, thus safeguarding patients and our team against inadvertent transgressions. ### Conclusion Kindling the amalgamation of robotics with empathetic healthcare, AideBot embodies the spirit of modern physiotherapeutic assistance. The title of my speech is “Race against Death: A Case of Severe Septic Shock.” Faced with such a dangerous disease, in this race against death, did we emerge victorious
reference: or was our attempt in vain? Let me take you through this harrowing journey. It all began with a 3-year-old girl, Rebecca, who was brought to our emergency department. She was pale, with a rapid heartbeat, struggling to breathe, and in a state of extreme lethargy. Upon examining her, we discovered petechial rashes all over her body and a high fever. It was evident that she was critically ill, and time was of the essence. Upon further investigation, we learned that Rebecca had recently recovered from a bout of pneumonia. However, her condition rapidly deteriorated, and she was transferred to the intensive care unit (ICU) for immediate attention. Blood tests revealed an alarming rise in her white blood cell count and markers of inflammation, indicating the presence of a severe infection. Given her symptoms and the rapid progression of her illness, we suspected septic shock – a life-threatening condition caused by the body's response to an infection. In septic shock, the body's immune system goes into overdrive, releasing chemicals that trigger widespread inflammation and organ dysfunction. We immediately initiated aggressive treatment, beginning with the administration of intravenous antibiotics to combat the underlying infection. Additionally, we started fluid resuscitation to stabilize her blood pressure and improve organ perfusion. However, despite our best efforts, Rebecca's condition worsened. At this critical juncture, we decided to explore alternative treatments. One option was the use of vasopressors – medications that constrict blood vessels to increase blood pressure. This approach aimed to improve blood flow to vital organs, but the risk of potential complications loomed large. With time running out, we braced ourselves for the possible consequences and initiated vasopressor therapy. Miraculously, Rebecca's blood pressure stabilized, and her organ perfusion improved. However, we were acutely aware that this was only a temporary solution. To address the root cause of her septic shock, we needed to identify the infecting organism. By conducting comprehensive laboratory tests, we were able to isolate the culprit – a strain of bacteria resistant to multiple antibiotics. Armed with this knowledge, we adjusted the antibiotic regimen accordingly, targeting the specific pathogen responsible for Rebecca's condition. Over the next few days, Rebecca's condition gradually improved. Her fever subsided, vital signs stabilized, and she regained consciousness. With each passing day, a glimmer of hope emerged amidst the chaos of the fight against septic shock. Rebecca was finally winning the race against death. Today, as I stand before you, I can proudly say that Rebecca triumphed over septic shock. It was a testament to our teamwork, quick decision-making, and relentless pursuit of a solution. The journey was not without challenges, but Rebecca's resilience, along with our unwavering commitment, led to a victory against one of the most formidable foes in pediatric medicine. In conclusion, Rebecca's case of severe septic shock serves as a reminder that every patient deserves our undivided attention, tireless effort, and innovative thinking. With continued research, improved diagnostics, and advancements in treatment modalities, we hope to see more triumphs in the face of life-threatening conditions like septic shock. Thank you for your attention, and may we always strive to emerge victorious in our race against death.

What is the maximum price you should pay for a share of the Delta Corporation, according to CAPM?
reference: First, we need to calculate the cost of equity using CAPM: Cost of equity = risk-free rate + beta x equity premium Cost of equity = 0.05 + 1.9 x 0.08 Cost of equity = 0.05 + 0.152 Cost of equity = 0.202 or 20.2% Next, we can use the constant growth dividend discount model to find the maximum price we should pay for a share of Delta Corporation: Price = Dividend / (Cost of equity - Dividend growth rate) Price = $1.60 / (0.202 - 0.1) Price = $1.60 / 0.102 Price = $15.69 Therefore, according to CAPM, the maximum price we should pay for a share of Delta Corporation is $15.69.

question: To follow up on your self-assessment, we invite you to use the SMARTS formula presented below in order to transform a few of your checked statements into specific objectives. This exercise will help guide your next steps in further developing your competencies. According to the SMARTS formula, your objectives must be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Rewarding, Time sensitive and Shared. Specific: Objectives need to be precise. Often objectives are too vague. An example of a vague objective is “I’ll work hard.” However, they should be formulated with precise details. For example, “I will document all my work and share my progress in weekly team meetings.” Measurable: Objectives need to be quantifiable. Measurable objectives give concrete information. For example, “I will produce three interim reports and one final report.” Including quantitative information makes it possible to determine whether the objective has been met. Achievable: Objectives need to be reasonable and achievable. Initially, many students believe they can achieve more than what is reasonable given the available time, resources and so on. Frequently, success or failure depends on setting achievable goals. An example of an unachievable objective is “I will revamp the entire SAP system by the end of the project.” Rewarding: Objectives need to matter in order to make you push yourself. It is important to stretch ourselves, try new things and feel rewarded by our achievements. Time sensitive: Objectives need to have a deadline. A due date gives a sense of urgency—the driving force to take action—and therefore increases the likelihood that the objective will be met. It also makes it possible to monitor progress. Shared: Objectives need to be shared with others. Objectives of a project are effective when shared. You will share these with your supervisor. You will also meet with your supervisor to discuss them and get them approved. Example of transforming a behavioural sentence from the list above into a SMARTS objective Examples:  Select and appropriately use the digital tools and resources that promote my learning and take advantage of online learning opportunities (webinars, Twitter threads, etc.).  Adopt, learn, and develop new technology practices so that I can adapt to different professional environments. Transformation of sentences using SMARTS format. 1. By April 13, I will have completed five drafts of a major presentation on clinical trial data, as well as having done some classification of the data. This will increase my proficiency with data processing in Microsoft Office, as well as give me insight into Canadian clinical trials. 2. I will study various relevant newspaper articles to find the discourse of advocates, organizations and governments (federal and provincial) on immigration in Ontario. This discourse analysis will allow me to improve my research skills using the Eureka database. Perfection not required: The objectives pursued are rarely perfect. But if you design them with care, an open mind, and a willingness to change, you’ll be more effective and productive. In fact, with a little planning upfront, you may well exceed your employer’s expectations! Elements to consider: 1. Your goals may change and evolve over the course of your experiences and should be revised regularly. 2. If you do not achieve 100% of your objectives at the end of your experience, simply explain the reasons in your reflections. 3. Use the SMARTS formula to assess the accuracy of your objectives as well as the actions you took to achieve them, the results, and the outcomes. 4. Use a journal to keep track of your thoughts and experiences, as these valuable notes could be used to evaluate your goals or as anecdotal examples in your reflective evaluation.

question: Format this: Her name was Sasha. Though we had gone to high school together, we were from two different crowds and never really knew each other. We ended up sharing a few classes together our first year of college, and that's when we began to talk. After sitting next to me in one of our classes, she noticed how smart I was and would often ask me for help with anything she didn't understand. Next thing I knew she was sitting next to me in every class we had together. I couldn't believe my luck. I had a major crush on her back in high school, but never had the balls to talk to her. Now she was asking me to spend more time with her outside of class to help tutor her, and I couldn't have been happier to do so. I love getting so much one on one time with her. She was super sweet, completely different from the popular mean girl persona she had in high school. She was always so giggly around me and always finding excuses to put her hands on my arm or shoulder. I couldn't help but feel she was flirting with me, but I still didn't have the nerve to ask her out. We maintained our friendship for the whole year. She would often drag me out to major parties that I never would've been invited to and always did her best to try to include me in conversations and pull me out of my shell a little. She never made any major moves to solidify whether or not she was in to me or just saw me as a really good friend. It got to a point where almost every time we hung out I was waiting for her to say something about how I feel like a brother to her or something, but that never happened. She just continued to confuse me and feed me mixed signals. Summer came along and we parted ways with a hug, and she said she couldn't wait to see me again at the end of summer break, so that felt somewhat promising. I spent all summer thinking about her, missing all the time that I had grown used to spending with her. I watched summer tik away slowly as I impatiently waited for school to start back up again. When the first day of the new year started I saw Sasha quickly making her way towards me. "Oh my God!" She yelled happily. "I'm so glad you're back! The summer was kinda boring without my cute little pet by my side!" Pet.. I wasn't sure how to take that. She did say I was cute.. What kind of message was she trying to give here? I brushed it off and gave her a big hug. We went off to find a quiet spot and she told me all about her summer and how she wished I could've been there with her. Our relationship was starting to feel like it was in a better place than when summer started. Near the end of October she told me that there was going to be this killer costume party and she wanted me to go with her. She was going as a witch and asked if I would be her peasant slave. I thought it was a weird request, but at the same time, this was sounding very much like a couples costume. At this point I had already developed very strong feeling for her and would do whatever it took for an opportunity to win her over, so I happily agreed. The night of the party she came to pick me up. The party was a decent ways off campus, tucked away in the middle of nowhere, so as to avoid cops coming to shut down the party. I was pretty excited. She made for one hot witch, and I didn't care if my costume was kind of demeaning because it made her so happy that we could go together. When we got there I noticed that there weren't a lot of familiar faces, but the party was bumpin either way so I didn't care nor think much of it. As the night carried on she drug me around with her everywhere, showing off our costumes, often joking about how she planned on taking me back to her lair for her dinner. She kept handing me beer after beer, I assumed trying to get me to loosen up. I'm not the most social person ever and can get kind of shy in groups. Her plan was working however. The more I drank the easier it was to open up and enjoy myself. It had started getting late and a lot of people had already made their way home. There were still a few stragglers, ourselves included. She took me by the hand and led me into a big empty room. She turned to look at me and grabbed me by the hand. "You've been a good little peasant slave," she said with a giggle and a wink. "Now, being the generous witch that I am, I'll grant you one free wish! What'll it be!?" I was heavily intoxicated, and as I looked at her gorgeous face, only one thing came to mind. "I just want to be yours forever." As soon as I said it I froze up. I hadn't thought before I spoke, and now it was all out there. I guess now I would finally get my definitive answer. A smile formed on her black lips. "What would you do to prove that you're worthy to be mine?" Was she serious? Did I actually stand a chance!? "I would do anything your heart desires," I said as sweetly as my drunken self could muster. She reached into her purse and pulled out salt and a candle. I was confused but just watched as she made a ring of salt on the floor and lit the candle in the middle of it. "I will give you the ultimate test then," she said stepping out of the circle after lighting the candle. "Step inside the circle." I did as she said and she started to mumble words I couldn't understand.

At the time this was easy to dismiss as crackers. In the eight years since its founding in 2003 the firm had manufactured a piddling 1,650 EVs. Its first big-selling car, the Model S, had yet to hit the road. Today it is almost as mad to argue that Elon Musk, the carmaker’s boss since 2008, has not achieved that goal. His company, a rare insurgent in an industry with formidable barriers to entry, has grown at neck-snapping speed. In the first quarter of 2023 Tesla’s Model Y mini-SUV was the world’s bestselling car. In the second quarter it delivered a total of 466,000 cars, beating analysts’ forecasts (see chart 1). Mr Musk’s promise of 2m sales this year, up from 1.3m in 2022, no longer seems fanciful. On July 15th the first Cybertruck, an angular, retro-futuristic pickup, rolled off the production line. Tesla has just unveiled an expansion plan for its German factory, where it wants to double capacity to 1m vehicles per year.

question: think a title for：Rose Once we arrived at his home, Joseph guided me inside, his reassuring touch providing a comforting anchor amidst the lingering anxiety. Sitting me down, he spoke with admiration. “You're amazing, Rose. I've never seen someone handle themselves so bravely,” a mix of awe and respect in his voice made me anxiety to subside. “You truly have a warrior's spirit.” His words, laced with sincerity, sparked a flicker of pride within me. Despite the ordeal I had just faced, Joseph's presence and kind words reminded me that I was stronger than I ever thought possible. Soon as we chatted, Mark came bounding down the stairs in his pajamas, his eyes widening in surprise at the sight of me. At first, he seemed shy, self-conscious about being seen in his sleepwear. But I quickly reassured him, “Hey, I've seen you in a hospital gown earlier, remember? And that’s uglier. So, no need to feel shy anymore.” He took a moment to think then confidently approached me, laughter bubbling from his lips as he took in my injured state. “Wow, Rose, we both learned something new today,” he said, a mischievous glint in his eyes. “Getting injured seems to be the theme of the day for us. Too bad dad is not in our team.” His perspective on the situation was surprisingly refreshing, and it brought a smile to my face. It was as if his lightheartedness had the power to alleviate the tension that had built up within me. Joseph chimed in, addressing Mark, “Rose will be staying with us.” I quickly interjected, “Only for the night.” But Mark, always the innocent optimist, added with a hopeful expression, “But I want you to stay with me forever.” “We can talk about it later.” Joseph stood upright. “I hope you all are hungry. Because I am famished.” We made our way to the dinner table, and Joseph's housekeeper served us a delicious spread—crisp salad, succulent fish fillet, and a medley of stir-fried vegetables. The aroma wafted through the air, stirring my appetite. I ate heartily, replenishing the energy that had been drained by the events of the evening. After the satisfying meal, Mark took it upon himself to show me to my room, which happened to be adjacent to his. “Rose, thanks for being my neighbor. If you get scared alone in this cold room, I have a place for you in my bed.” The more time I spend with this guy, the more he amuses me with his antiques. “Sure thing, little guy. Now it’s time to go to bed for us.” He planted a sweet kiss on my cheek before bouncing off to his own room. Entering my room, my safe space, as I was about to throw myself in the warm of the amazing attractive mattress, I paused seeing Joseph following me closely behind, carrying a set of women's clothing. I wonder if any other woman lives in this place. I haven’t seen it, but then, he could have a girlfriend to whom this clothes belongs to. but this isn’t the time to ask about that. His concern for my appearance was evident the way he eyes my clothes, and he gently spoke, “I think you should change out of those clothes now. There's too much blood on them, and, well, let's just say you look like a bandit queen.” His playful comment brought a smile to me, and I couldn't help but chuckle. “I suppose a change of clothes wouldn't hurt,” I replied, appreciating his attention to detail and his desire for me to feel comfortable as I took the bundle from his hand and walked to the bathroom to get changed. Once I had changed into the clean clothes, Joseph retrieved a first aid kit and gently began to tend to my wounds. “You should dress it every few hours. It quickens the healing process.” “I wonder how you know this. I've never heard of it.” “A guy can have his secrets, can't he?” His touch was both soothing and tender, causing my heart to flutter with a mixture of appreciation and warmth. “Impressive skills you have there, Rose,” Joseph remarked, a hint of awe in his voice as he carefully bandaged my injuries. “You handled yourself incredibly well back there. I'm truly impressed. It’s already twice that you’ve tackled over-sized men in this short period we’ve been acquainted. I wonder what your daily life looks like.” “For that, you'll just have to wait and see, I guess.” He laughed and left the room leaving sleep to consume me whole. * I had just woken up when I heard a gentle knock on the door. It must be morning now, I thought to myself. I checked the time and saw that it was seven. Opening the door, I found Joseph standing there, looking surprisingly relaxed and comfortable in his white, spotless t-shirt and grey joggers. His hair fell freely onto his face, a departure from his usual sleeked-back style. “Good morning,” he greeted me. I couldn't help but feel a pang of self-consciousness. Here I was, looking dishevelled and far from my best, while he stood before me in perfect attire. I simply nodded, feeling too embarrassed to say anything in response. After he left, I washed my face, attempting to freshen up a bit before heading downstairs for breakfast. Mark was already at the table, happily devouring his omelet. He greeted me with a cheerful, “Good morning, Rose!” We engaged in a brief conversation, and even though I wasn't much of a breakfast person, I mustered the energy to eat a slice of toast. Joseph then informed us that a doctor would be arriving in an hour to tend to my wounds. He turned to Mark and said, “I hope you'll be a good boy while I'm gone and treat well with the doctor.” Mark responded with a mischievous grin, clearly up for some mischief. Suddenly, Mark had a request. “Rose, can you stay with me today? I'm not going to school because I'm injured, so you shouldn't go to work either.” I hesitated, knowing the responsibilities that awaited me at my job. “That's not how adulting works, kiddo,” I explained, feeling a sense of obligation. “There are no leaves for me.” Mark pouted, disappointment evident on his face. But Joseph chimed in, adding his persuasive voice to the mix. “He's right, you should stay and rest. You can work from here if you need to. I have everything you might need in my study.” His concern for my well-being was palpable, and eventually, he managed to convince me. Mark's face lit up with joy. “Yeah! Rose and I are going to have so much fun today!” he exclaimed, his excitement contagious. Joseph chuckled at his son's enthusiasm and playfully asked, “So, now you want me out of your way huh?” he nodded. I couldn't help but smile at their banter. It was heartwarming to see the bond between father and son and to feel Joseph's genuine concern for me. In that moment, I realized just how lucky I was to have them both by my side, supporting and caring for me.
reference: "A Warrior's Spirit: Rose's Journey to Strength and Belonging"
