question: Ledbury Poetry (UK) has announced that Donegal poet Annemarie Ní Churreáin is among the poets shortlisted for the fourth Ledbury Hellens Poetry Prize for best second collection published in Britain or Ireland in 2021 or 2022. The prize aims to support and encourage poets at the mid-career stage, with a prize of £5000 for the winning second collection. Speaking of Ní Churreáin’s nominated work, judges Togara Muzanenhamo and Penelope Shuttle said: “Drawing inspiration from the concept of restorative justice – Annemarie Ní Churreáin’s The Poison Glen entwines legend from the Gaeltacht landscape with moments from history to depict the systematic mistreatment of unmarried or abandoned mothers and the children born to these women. Ní Churreáin revisits locations of state care institutions in Ireland over the past hundred years and beyond with an inquisitive lens that requires us to ask what the left-behind sites remember or what sense of the child remains after trauma. The Poison Glen stands as a literary monument to silenced voices”. ADVERTISEMENT - CONTINUE READING BELOW Originally from Cloich Cheann Fhaola, Ní Churreáin's books include Bloodroot, Doire Press, 2017, Town, The Salvage Press, 2018, and The Poison Glen, The Gallery Press, 2021. She is a recipient of the Irish Arts Council’s Next Generation Artist Award and a co-recipient of The Markievicz Award. She is Poetry Editor at The Stinging Fly Magazine. Her most recent literary project, a limited edition poetry pamphlet titled Ghostgirl, explores the Stranorlar Workhouse and Stranorlar County Home, also known as Stranorlar Mother and Baby Home. The project was a commission of the Donegal Archives Service as part of the Donegal Decade of Centenaries Programme. Co-judge Togara Muzanenhamo said: “The award is particularly special because it celebrates the accomplishment of what can be an artistic hurdle for some poets – compiling a second collection. There are numerous prizes for first collections and best collections but few focus on the pivotal role of a poets’ second book – a book that may highlight a poet’s maturing voice or solidify their career. I am excited at the prospect of reading work that will confidently explore and freely navigate language and introduce us to voices that will shape the future of poetry”. ADVERTISEMENT - CONTINUE READING BELOW The other collections and poets shortlisted for the prize are; Kaveh Akbar (Chatto) Pilgrim Bell; All the Names Given, Raymond Antrobus (Picador); A Blood Condition, Kayo Chingonyi (Chatto); England’s Green, Zaffar Kunial (Faber); Bloom, Sarah Westcott (Pavilion Poetry). The winner of the fourth Ledbury Hellens Poetry Prize will be announced on December 4 at 7pm at an online prize giving ceremony hosted by the Ledbury Centre.

question: In the Molecular Structure and Vapor Pressure lab, Peter added 2.0 mL of air containing 0.000086 moles of air at 753.5 torr total pressure at 298.6 K into the graduated cylinder. Then he added hexane and placed the graduated cylinder in a water bath at 329 K. The volume in the sample chamber became 8.4 mL. What is the partial pressure, in torr, of the air in the sample chamber now? Report the answer to one place after the decimal point. Do not include the unit. Helpful value: R = 62.36 L• torr / mol • K Helpful equation: PV = nRT

question: WeDriveAnywhere is a taxi company in a major city. At present their taxis are available at the railway station and at large retail centres. Customers can also book a taxi by phone. Ali, the owner and manager, are investigating the introduction of new technology to make booking and paying for a taxi more efficient and easier for the customer. (a) Explain three ways in which technology could be used to improve booking and payment.
reference: 1) Mobile App: The company can develop a mobile application that allows customers to easily book a taxi from their smartphones. The app can provide real-time information on the availability and location of taxis, allowing users to select the nearest available vehicle. It can also allow customers to track the location of their booked taxi, estimate arrival time, and communicate with the driver if needed. Additionally, the app can provide various payment options, including cashless transactions, making the payment process more convenient for customers. 2) Online Booking System: Implementing an online booking system on the company's website can streamline the booking process. Customers can quickly enter their pickup and drop-off locations, select their desired vehicle type, and specify any additional requirements. The system can provide instant confirmation of the booking, along with estimated fare and arrival time. Customers can also choose payment options and securely input their payment details. 3) Advanced Payment Methods: Introducing contactless payment methods, such as NFC (Near Field Communication) or QR code scanning, can expedite the payment process. reference: To calculate the standard error of a sample proportion, we can use the formula: Standard error = sqrt((p̂ * (1 - p̂)) / n) Where: - p̂ is the sample proportion - n is the sample size In this case, the sample proportion is 73% or 0.73, and the sample size is 100. Standard error = sqrt((0.73 * (1 - 0.73)) / 100) Calculating this expression: Standard error = sqrt((0.5329) / 100) = sqrt(0.005329) ≈ 0.073 Therefore, the standard error of the sample proportion is approximately 0.073, which is equivalent to 0.063 when rounded to two decimal places.

question: Think a title for :Rose Alex was in my cabin, talking about the overall idea that I might be expecting from him. I told him all I have and he noted it down in a notepad when Sarah came to my office to call me for the outfit trials. I'm so glad to have her work for my secretory. Joseph was the one to recommend her for her efficient skills and poised demeanour as she talks with people. I have reasons to believe they’ve worked together in the past. Walking towards the trial rooms, I couldn't help but notice the tension radiating from Joseph as he watched Alex and I coming through. His irritated expression perplexed me, considering he had been the one to choose Alex as the director. He was even thankful earlier when Alex confirmed to give us dates for the shoots, as it deemed to me like a big deal. Why wouldn’t it be, Alex is known to be the best in the field. It seemed now that there was some unspoken history between them. Entering the room on the first floor, I observed racks of costumes neatly arranged on hangers, waiting to be tried on. The walls were adorned with sketches and fabric swatches, adding an artistic touch to the space. A full-length mirror stood in one corner, ready to reflect the transformation of the actors. Sean, the designer approached us, his tone slightly curt. “Rose, glad you could make it. We need your opinion on the costumes. The actors are waiting.” I nodded, acknowledging his request. “I'm eager to see the outfits myself. Let's get started.” The actors began trying on their costumes as Sean suggested. The first apparels they came out wearing formal patterns, shirts and long pants. “Light cotton fabrics with detailed embroidery and flowy patterns should suit more to the theme.” I observed.” Sean nodded, picking out the types of outfits I suggested from the hanger. Alex leaned in closer to me, a mischievous glimmer in his eyes. “Rose, you have a way of making even costume trials exciting. I can't help but admire your attention to detail.” I chuckled, feeling a slight blush creep onto my cheeks. “Well, it's all about creating the perfect look, isn't it? Every little detail matters.” Meanwhile, Joseph sat nearby, his crossed arms and furrowed brows indicating his displeasure. Alex, seemingly unfazed, couldn't resist teasing him. “Joseph, don't worry. I won't steal your spotlight. I'm just here to bring Rose's vision to life.” Joseph's response was curt. “Just make sure you do your job, Alex. That’s what we are paying you for.” I laughed awkwardly. “Let’s focus on work.” The tension between them was palpable, and I couldn't help but feel caught in the middle, like literally. If it wasn’t for work, I don’t think I will ever be able to handle them together. So, I focused on the actors, offering feedback on the costumes and engaging in lighthearted banter to lighten the mood. Oh completely, utterly useless. Emma twirled in her vibrant floral maxi dress, her eyes sparkling with excitement. “Rose, what do you think? Does this costume capture your vision of my character?” I examined her outfit, considering its fit and overall aesthetic. “Emma, you look stunning. The costume perfectly embodies your character. It's elegant yet approachable but I think there is something missing here. what do you think Alex?” “Yeah!” he nodded. Jake joined in, a mischievous grin on his face. “Rose, do you think this costume will make me look dashing enough to win over hearts?” I playfully rolled my eyes. “Jake, with your charm, you don't need a costume to win hearts. But yes, this one adds an extra touch of charisma.” As the actors continued trying on different outfits, Alex took the opportunity to talk playfully with me. “Rose, it really doesn’t seem like your first project. You seem to have a great foresight.” I blushed, trying to hide my smile, proud of what I've accomplished thanks to Joseph. But he is farther to happiness as he can be. He is sitting brooding for some reason. “Alex, you know how to charm a girl, don't you?” Sean teased. “But let's focus on the task at hand, shall we? There is a lot of work and much less time.” “Yes, Alex let’s work now. we can talk about other things later.” Joseph, seemingly unable to ignore our interaction, interjected. “We're here to work, not flirt, Alex.” Alex smirked, undeterred. “Joseph, no need to be jealous. You had your chance with Rose. It's my turn now.” My eyes widened in surprise, and I quickly redirected the conversation. “Alright, enough banter, gentlemen. Let's get back to the costumes. We need to ensure that every detail is perfect.” The costume trial continued amidst the playful exchanges and occasional jabs between Alex and Joseph. As we narrowed down the options and made final decisions, a sense of excitement and satisfaction filled inside me. Despite the underlying tension, I couldn't help but find the situation amusing. There was something comical about the contrasting personalities and their playful rivalry. One can't help but smile, other is sitting on the chair like a sulking child. While everyone else are talking and sharing opinions. The actors began trying on the chosen outfits, one after the other, swirling around to give us a good look. Sean carefully observed their fits, making minor adjustments here and there. Tweaking one safety pin behind or another on the side. Emma raised her concerns about the length of her dress, while Jake argued that his shirt felt too tight around the collar. There are many more adjustments that is gonna be needed for Sean to complete in a few days. In the midst of their debates, Joseph and Alex chimed in with their opinions. Joseph, ever the advocate for bold choices, insisted, “We need some vibrant shades to bring out the characters' personalities. We have very little time to showcase a story. it will be better if they can use the help of their outfits.” He is not wrong, but that would make them contrasted. We need to follow a color theme. Alex, on the other hand, countered, “I believe pastels and fresh colors are more in line with the current trends. It will give the production a modern touch.” Observing the two men on either side of me, I couldn't help but feel caught in the middle. I carefully considered their opinions before voicing my own. “I think Alex has a point. Pastels would indeed give a refreshing and contemporary vibe to the costumes. And since we are following a summer vibe, I think that should be considered.” A proud smile formed on Alex's lips, while Joseph's irritation was evident. However, before Joseph could express his dissent, his phone rang, and he excused himself to take the call. His sudden departure left an awkward silence in the room. Everyone adjust to the little awkwardness that still remained and started again with the work. Taking advantage of the moment, Alex leaned closer to me, a playful glimmer in his eyes. “Rose, I must say, your taste in fashion aligns perfectly with mine. I'm glad we're on the same page.” I chuckled, feeling a mixture of excitement and confusion. “It seems we have a shared aesthetic, Alex. Let's hope it translates well into the production.” Just as we were conversing, Joseph returned unexpectedly, his eyes narrowing as he witnessed us talking. A surge of anger flashed across his face before he abruptly turned and stormed back to his office, leaving us puzzled. The costume designer, sensing the tension, tried to diffuse the situation. “Well, Rose, Alex, the fittings are almost complete. Overall, I believe the costumes are shaping up wonderfully. The colors and styles complement the characters' personalities perfectly.” I nodded, grateful for the designer's input. “Thank you for your hard work. Please get started with the fittings. We’ll start filming from next week.” As the actors continued changing outfits to their clothes when Alex added, “how about we share contacts, I'll call you soon as my assistant confirm the location?” I hesitated for a moment, glancing around to ensure no prying eyes were watching, before sharing my contact information with him. Our exchange didn't go unnoticed by Joseph, who had returned to the room, his eyes fixed on us. His anger was palpable as he silently observed Alex's demeanor. His reaction perplexed me. I couldn't understand why he was acting so mad, especially considering he had chosen Alex as the director. His sudden withdrawal, retreating to his room for the rest of the discussion only added to my confusion. Despite the underlying tension, I tried to maintain a sense of professionalism. I engaged in discussions with the actors, providing feedback on the costumes and offering encouragement. However, the absence of Joseph's presence weighed heavily on the atmosphere. Done for the day, I couldn't help but feel a mixture of excitement and apprehension for the upcoming production. The dynamic between Alex and Joseph had certainly added an unexpected twist to the process. I could only hope that their differences would ultimately contribute to the success of the project, rather than hinder it. Everyone already went home when I walked into Joseph's office, holding the photographs of the chosen outfits and makeup styles in my hands. His reaction was far from what I expected. He simply nodded and took the photos without saying anything other than, “I'll see it.” Concern etched across my face, I couldn't help but wonder if he was sick. So, I asked, “Joseph, is something wrong? Are you feeling unwell?” He shook his head dismissively. “No, I'm fine. Just a bit preoccupied with work, that's all.” I sighed relief. I've been in the mistake of thinking that I've done something to annoy him. but if it isn’t for me, it must have something to do with Alex. Sensing his distance, I mustered up the courage to extend an invitation. “You know, Joseph, I've been meaning to thank you for everything you've done. How about I take you and Mark out for dinner? It'll be my treat.” He waved his hand, brushing off my offer. “No need to bother. You can go ahead with your plans for the date you've set up with Alex.” His response caught me off guard. Confusion clouded my thoughts as I searched for an explanation. “Joseph, I don't understand. Why are you acting this way? What do you mean by 'the date you’ve set up'? I'm not going on any date.” With mounting frustration, he unleashed his pent-up anger. His words cut through me like a sharp blade. “We are here for work, Rose! Not to indulge in romantic entanglements. Don't you get that? I've begged everyone because I saw potential in you, but for some days I'm seeing you are more occupied with something else.” His outburst left me speechless, my emotions teetering on the edge. I've been working even after leaving office. Still planning everything meticulously. How can his accusatory tone make me feel so disappointed. “Fine! If you are going to do this, I'll better leave you alone.” Unable to bear his accusations any longer, I quietly left his office and retreated to my own. The weight of his words lingered, leaving me with a sense of hurt and confusion. As I closed the door behind me, I sank into my chair, struggling to make sense of Joseph's sudden anger. What had I done to deserve such treatment? I had simply been trying to foster a positive working environment and extend my gratitude for all his help. The room felt suffocating, and I longed for answers. I couldn't help but question why Joseph's frustrations were being directed at me. Had I unknowingly crossed a boundary? The more I pondered, the more frustrated and disheartened I became. Feeling a mix of emotions, I resolved to give Joseph some space, hoping that he would eventually explain his outburst. It was clear that tensions were running high, and I had no desire to exacerbate the situation further. The silence enveloping me, I couldn't shake off the nagging feeling of confusion and disappointment. This unexpected turn of events had cast a shadow over our once harmonious working relationship, leaving me yearning for resolution and understanding. But for the day, I'm going to go home and not think about it anymore.
reference: Title: Unspoken Tension in the Costume Fitting Room: Rose's Confusion and Disappointment.

question: Mr Chan started his trading business on 1 January 2007. On that date, the company bought a computer for office use, costing $12,000. The computer was expected to be used for three years before it would be replaced by a more advanced model. As at 31 December 2007, Mr Chan decided that the computer be carried at its original cost of $12,000 on the balance sheet, without providing for depreciation. State the accounting principle or concept that has been violated and provide an explanation.
reference: Mr. Chan's decision to carry the computer at its original cost of $12,000 without providing for depreciation violates the **Matching Principle** and the **Depreciation Accounting Principle** (part of the Accrual Accounting Concept). **Matching Principle:** The matching principle is a fundamental accounting concept that requires expenses to be matched with the revenues they help generate, in the same accounting period. This means that the cost of an asset should be spread over its useful life in order to properly match the cost of the asset with the benefits (revenues) it generates each year. By not depreciating the computer, Mr. Chan fails to allocate the cost of the computer over its expected useful life of three years, thus not reflecting the actual use and economic contribution of the computer to the business for that year. **Depreciation Accounting Principle:** This principle dictates that the cost of a fixed asset should be allocated over its useful life in order to represent its consumption and wear and tear over time. Depreciation is the method used to allocate the cost of tangible assets over their useful lives systematically. Since the computer is expected to be replaced after three years, it should be depreciated over that period to reflect the reduction in value as the asset is used. Mr. Chan's treatment of the computer's cost also impacts the **Going Concern Principle** by not showing ongoing expenses related to fixed assets properly, which may mislead users of the financial statements regarding the company's periodic income and financial position. As a corrective measure, Mr. Chan should provide for the depreciation expense of the computer starting from the date of purchase up to the reporting date (31 December 2007). Assuming straight-line depreciation with no residual value, the annual depreciation expense would be $12,000 divided by 3 years, which is $4,000 per year. Therefore, for the year 2007, Mr. Chan should recognize a depreciation expense of $4,000 and reduce the carrying amount of the computer to $8,000 on the balance sheet as of 31 December 2007.

GARCH models have been widely used for modeling and forecasting financial time series data, including stock prices. However, the accuracy of forecasting using GARCH models can be improved by integrating machine learning techniques, which are capable of capturing complex relationships and patterns in the data. One such technique is stacking machine learning models, which combine several machine learning algorithms to minimize errors and increase accuracy. Therefore, the proposed research aims to develop a hybrid GARCH and stacking machine learning model to forecast the volatility of the Tehran Stock Exchange. This will provide a basis for developing the research hypotheses and objectives. 2. GARCH models: This will involve a review of the different types of GARCH models and their applications in financial time series forecasting. The research will focus on selecting the appropriate GARCH model that can accurately capture the volatility of the TSE. 3. Machine learning models: This will involve a review of the different machine learning techniques that can be applied to financial time series forecasting, including stacking models. The research will focus on examining the strengths and weaknesses of different machine learning models and selecting the most appropriate models for the proposed framework. 4. Hybrid model: This will involve developing the hybrid GARCH and stacking machine learning model for forecasting the volatility of the TSE. The research will test the model using historical data and evaluate its forecasting performance using statistical measures such as Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). In summary, the proposed research will contribute to the literature on financial forecasting by developing a hybrid GARCH and stacking machine learning model for volatility forecasting of the TSE. This framework will allow investors to make informed investment decisions and reduce the impact of volatility on their portfolios.

question: Explain this to me: Introduction API Root Endpoint United States https://www.site24x7.com/api Europe https://www.site24x7.eu/api China https://www.site24x7.cn/api India https://www.site24x7.in/api Australia https://www.site24x7.net.au/api Japan https://app.site24x7.jp/api The Site24x7 API helps you achieve all the operations that can be performed on our web client. The API requires OAuthtoken as an account identifier. This API is built using the REST principles which ensures predictable URLs that make writing applications easy. This API follows HTTP rules, where a wide range of HTTP clients can be used to interact with the API. Every resource is exposed as a URL. The URL of each resource can be obtained by accessing the API Root Endpoint. We have multiple data centers in Site24x7: United States - .com Europe - .eu China - .cn India - .in Australia - .net.au All examples in the document, except Japan, are based on COM domain. You can change the DC Root endpoint of any example from COM to any DC you want to access. For Japan DC, the API Root Endpoint would be https://app.site24x7.jp Getting Started Example $ curl https://www.site24x7.com/api/monitors \ -H 'Accept: application/json; version=2.0' \ -H 'Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken 1000.41d9f2cfbd1b7a8f9e314b7aff7ab2d1.8fcc9810810a216793f385b9dd6e125f' \ All Site24x7 APIs require a Authorization request header for authentication. Authentication Zoho Accounts Root Endpoint United States https://accounts.zoho.com Europe https://accounts.zoho.eu China https://accounts.zoho.com.cn India https://accounts.zoho.in Australia https://accounts.zoho.com.au Japan https://accounts.zoho.jp Site24x7 REST APIs uses the OAuth 2.0 protocol to authorize and authenticate calls. The OAuth protocol provides a more secure access to protect resources, thereby reducing the hassle of asking for a username and password every time a user logs in. We have multiple data centers in Zoho: United States - .com Europe - .eu China - .com.cn India - .in Australia - .com.au Japan - .jp All examples in PART 1 - 4 are based on COM domain. You can change the DC Root endpoint of any example from COM to any DC you want to access. Please follow the steps below to access Site24x7’s APIs using OAuth 2.0: PART 1: REGISTERING NEW CLIENT APPLICATION Register your application with Site24x7 to get your Client ID and Client Secret. For script-based API calls, the Self Client option in the Zoho Developer Console is preferrable or check out the other options based on your client types. To register your application using the Self Client option, Go to Zoho Developer Console and click on Get Started Now > Self Client > Create Now. United States Europe China India Australia Japan Click on Create. Confirm the process. On successful registration, you will be provided with a set of OAuth 2.0 credentials such as Client ID and Client Secret, that are known to both Zoho and your application. Note: Do not share these credentials to anyone. PART 2: GENERATING GRANT TOKEN Once you have successfully registered the client application, generate a grant token to obtain authorization to use the APIs based on your requirement. If you have generated the OAuth 2.0 credentials using the Self Client option, then please follow the steps below: Go to Zoho Developer Console and click on the created Self Client. Navigate to the Generate Code tab and provide the Scope List of scopes (based on the API calls that you are going to use), Description, and the Time Duration for its validity (from 3 minutes to 10 minutes). Get the scopes for the APIs from their respective API document and separate multiple scopes with commas. Click Generate. Copy the code for the mentioned scope. For other client types (such as web-based), refer here. Note: Generating a Grant Token is a one-time process. It cannot be generated via API call. Once the Grant Token is generated, refer Part 3 to create a Refresh Token immediately before the former expires. Please note that the Refresh Token is permanent and has no expiry. PART 3: GENERATE ACCESS AND REFRESH TOKEN POST https://accounts.zoho.com/oauth/v2/token?client_id={client_id}&client_secret={client_secret}&code={code}&grant_type=authorization_code After getting the grant token from the above step, make a POST request for the following URL with the given params to generate the access_token: Request Example $ curl https://accounts.zoho.com/oauth/v2/token \ -X POST \ -d "client_id=1000.0SRSZSY37WMZ69405H3TMYI2239V" \ -d "client_secret=fb0196010f2b70df8db2a173ca2cf59388798abf"\ -d "code=1000.dd7e47321d48b8a7e312e3d6eb1a9bb8.b6c07ac766ec11da98bf6a261e24dca4"\ -d "grant_type=authorization_code" \ Response Example { "access_token":"1000.2deaf8d0c268e3c85daa2a013a843b10.703adef2bb337b 8ca36cfc5d7b83cf24", "refresh_token":"1000.18e983526f0ca8575ea9c53b0cd5bb58.1bd83a6f2e22c3a7e1309d96ae439cc1", "expires_in":3600, "api_domain":"https://www.zohoapis.com", "token_type":"Bearer" } Parameter Description client_id Mandatory Client ID obtained during Client Registration. client_secret Mandatory Client Secret obtained during Client Registration. code Mandatory The grant token that is obtained in the above step. grant_type Mandatory Value must be authorization_code In the response, you will get both access_token and refresh_token. The access_token will expire after some specified seconds (represented by expires_in param in the response). You can regenerate a new access_token using the refresh_token (Refer Part 5: Generate Access Token from Refresh Token). The refresh_token is permanent. To revoke a refresh_token, refer Part 6: Revoking a Refresh Token. Note: Each time a re-consent page is accepted, a new refresh token is generated. The maximum limit is 20 refresh tokens per user. If this limit is crossed, the first refresh token is automatically deleted to accommodate the latest one. This is done irrespective of whether the first refresh token is in use or not. You can generate a maximum of 20 refresh tokens in a span of 10 minutes per client ID. Each refresh token can have a maximum of 10 active access tokens (non expired). When the user creates the 11th access token, the first created access token is automatically deleted to accommodate the latest one. You can also refer to sample scripts in the community post. Read the kbase article to know about the common OAuth Errors. PART 4: CALLING AN API Once the access and the refresh tokens are generated, API calls can be made by passing the access token in the header. Header name should be Authorization Header value should be Zoho-oauthtoken {access_token} To access an MSP Customer or a BU’s data you need to pass their ZAAID in the header. For more information. Header name should be Cookie Header value should be zaaid={zaaid of the customer/bu} Note: Access tokens cannot be passed in the request param. Example $ curl https://www.site24x7.com/api/monitors \ -H 'Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken 1000.41d9f2cfbd1b7a8f9e314b7aff7ab2d1.8fcc9810810a216793f385b9dd6e125f' \ List of scopes available in Site24x7: Scope Description account To access, add, edit, delete users and license related data. Availabe types: Site24x7.Account.Read, Site24x7.Account.Create, Site24x7.Account.Update, Site24x7.Account.Delete, Site24x7.Account.All admin To access, add, edit, delete monitors, configuration profiles, third party integrations etc. Availabe types: Site24x7.Admin.Read, Site24x7.Admin.Create, Site24x7.Admin.Update, Site24x7.Admin.Delete, Site24x7.Admin.All reports To access, add, edit, delete reports and monitor status. Availabe types: Site24x7.Reports.Read, Site24x7.Reports.Create, Site24x7.Reports.Update, Site24x7.Reports.Delete, Site24x7.Reports.All operations To access, add, edit, delete operation related data such as IT Automation, maintenance, status page announcements etc. Availabe types: Site24x7.Operations.Read, Site24x7.Operations.Create, Site24x7.Operations.Update, Site24x7.Operations.Delete, Site24x7.Operations.All msp To access, add, edit, delete MSP related data. Availabe types: Site24x7.Msp.Read, Site24x7.Msp.Create, Site24x7.Msp.Update, Site24x7.Msp.Delete, Site24x7.Msp.All bu To access, add, edit, delete Business Units related data. Availabe types: Site24x7.Bu.Read, Site24x7.Bu.Create, Site24x7.Bu.Update, Site24x7.Bu.Delete, Site24x7.Bu.All PART 5: GENERATE ACCESS TOKEN FROM REFRESH TOKEN POST https://accounts.zoho.com/oauth/v2/token?client_id={client_id}&client_secret={client_secret}&refresh_token={refresh_token}&grant_type=refresh_token Access tokens have limited validity. In most of the cases, the access tokens expire in one hour. Until then, the access token has unlimited usage. Once it expires, your app will have to use the refresh token to request for a new access token. Note: You can generate a maximum of 10 access tokens in a span of 10 minutes. Make the following POST request with the given params to get a new access token: Request Example $ curl https://accounts.zoho.com/oauth/v2/token \ -X POST \ -d "client_id=1000.0SRSZSY37WMZ69405H3TMYI2239V" \ -d "client_secret=fb0196010f2b70df8db2a173ca2cf59388798abf" \ -d "refresh_token=1000.8ecd474019e31d52d2f94aad6c5cb7.4638677ebc14f2f2ee0b6dfb6cebdc"\ -d "grant_type=refresh_token" \ Response Example { "access_token":"1000.2deaf8d0c268e3c85daa2a013a843b10.703adef2bb337b 8ca36cfc5d7b83cf24", "expires_in":3600, "api_domain":"https://www.zohoapis.com", "token_type":"Bearer" } Parameter Description client_id Mandatory Client ID obtained during Client Registration. client_secret Mandatory Client Secret obtained during Client Registration. refresh_token Mandatory REFRESH TOKEN using which a new access token has to be generated. grant_type Mandatory Value must be refresh_token.

question: 1. Position Information Title: Consultancy for supporting Karnali PA for Public Hearing, Oversight, and Promoting Open Parliamentary Practices Department/Unit: Parliament Support Project Reports to: National Project Manager Coordination with: Project Team Lead Implementation Area: Provincial Assembly Expected Places of Travel (if applicable): NA Duration of Assignment: 01 June to 30 August Provision of support services: Office space Yes □ No x Equipment (laptop etc.) Yes □ No x Secretarial Services Yes □ No x 2. Background Information Since 2018, UNDP through parliament support (PSP) project is supporting the parliaments and secretariats in PAs to strengthen their capacities for effective operation of parliamentary functions including institutional capacity building. PSP’s support to the PAs are focused primarily towards strengthening parliamentary core functions; oversight, law making, and enhancing the representation. PSP, over the years has invested in the parliament outreach and openness through various initiation such as: introducing Meet the Speaker in Karnali and Sudurpaschim Provinces, connecting the PAs with the District through virtual mode, development of Outreach plan of action, supporting the parliaments for the public hearing through the media and CSOs to count few. Some of the initiations of previous years have been adopted by the PA secretariats in some ways however, there are still many areas where the Parliament secretariat has limited engagement such as engaging with the public and thematic independent CSOs in the oversight of pertinent issues. Though there are examples of some openness activities initiated by the PA secretariat, but these are not always consistent. Likewise, the engagement with the citizens through public hearing and open interaction is another aspect through which the parliament Secretariat can enhance their outreach and openness where the secretariat will get the opportunities to respond to the queries from the citizen while sharing about the activities of the Parliament secretariat. Planning and organizing an event where citizen forums could be engaged through the consultation, dialogues, sharing, and other side activities could be another method of promoting parliament openness by engaging with the public, youth, and students in larger scale. Additionally, engaging with the CSOs for supporting the parliament secretariat in planning and organizing the events related to the parliamentary openness not only help the secretariat in swift management but it will also contribute towards wider stakeholder engagement in the parliamentary affairs and better understanding and awareness on the overall legislative development and oversight mechanism. In this backdrop, PSP plans to engage with a competent service provider organization to support the Karnali PA secretariat in the oversight on relevant emerging issues, including the public hearing and a mega event on the parliamentary openness. Through these programs the PA secretariats are expected to enhance their collaboration with the relevant CSOs and experts while also inspiring the PA towards making the parliament more open and accessible to the public. Thus the project plans to hire service from a consulting firm/organisation that can provide the service as per the scope of this ToR. 3. Objectives of Assignment The overall objective of the proposed assignment is: To conduct dialogues/interaction through public hearing to make parliament accountable to the citizens To support the PA committees in their oversight works to engage with relevant thematic CSOs. To support the PA secretariat in planning and organizing a package event as part of the parliamentary openness 4. Scope of work Expected Results/Deliverables/Final Products Expected The service provider will work in close coordination with the Project to complete the following duties and responsibilities. Scope of Work: The service provider will establish coordination with the PSP, PA secretariat and relevant stakeholders to to facilitate the said activities relating to conducting 2 public hearing, 2 events with Committees on their oversight work, and conduct one package-based Event for Parliamentary Openness in Karnali Province. In addition, the service provider will accomplish the following: Planning and Implementation Activity1: Support PA to Conduct Public Hearing-2 events Service provider will identify key issues and develop a plan for the public hearing Coordinate with the PA secretariat, relevant thematic committees for planning and organization Identify the key issues and venue for public hearing with the Committee on various issues within its jurisdiction, and it will be done in consultation with the Committee secretariat and PSP. Collect pertinent questions and concerns form the selected community on the issue in advance so that it could be raised during the hearing programme. Research some evidence on the key issues of the community so that the moderator could help the community raise/complement their concerns. Select the Chairs/MPs (at least 4) representing at least 2 thematic committees of the PA and at least one MP from that constituency. Select a spot related to selected issues that must be accessible and feasible for a one-day event. Organize and facilitate2 events of public hearing program between the parliamentarians of the PA of the Province and the citizens on the selected issue. The interaction will take place at the community level which is accessible in terms of proximity from the provincial capital. Make sure that media persons are also engaged in the event and the news of the same is covered by the local media. Prepare a detailed report with the major issues raised, response/commitment made, and ways forward. Activity 2: Support PA secretariat to engage with Research institutions and CSOs in oversight work-2 events Service provider will prepare plan of engagement with the CSOs Coordination with PA Secretariat, committees and relevant CSOs for the engagement in committees works Conduct a half day interaction/ sharing event among the PA secretariat, Committees and lead representative from the CSOs to inform the committees on their thematic areas of engagement, and sensitize to identify the pertinent areas for the oversight. Facilitate evidence-based presentations from the CSOs so that committees could make informed choices about their oversight agenda. Such engagement could be with different committees such as women and social dev committees with focus on women and social justice, Public Accounts Committee with CSOs and media active on public financial governance , Agriculture and Environment committee with the CSOs working on Environment, Climate and forestry etc.) Document the major discussion, way forward and future engagement plan, if any Provide the committees with the roster of the CSOs/research institutions for the use of the committees Activity 3: Support PA secretariat to promote open parliamentary practices-1 packaged event Service provider will develop an event plan to organize the event for promoting the parliamentary openness. Coordinate and share with the Parliament Secretariat, leadership, and PSP the event plan and finalizee event accordingly. Organize a package-based event on parliament openness in the PA in consultation with the PA secretariat ( the openness event could be a good mix of at least 5 activities such as Visit Your Parliament visit, documentary show, photo or video shows, exhibition on democracy and parliaments/ quiz or elocution shows/Meet the Speaker for elderly citizen, Youths/Students Q and A with MPs, Know your Lawmaking Corner, Women and Marginalized Groups in Parliament Corner, and other talk series relating to parliament openness or any other events as identified in consultation with the PA secretariat ) Engage at least 250 people directly in these activities and reach out t at least 10 thousand people via social media tools Prepare event report on major achievements, outreach, and outcome of the program Methodology: The Service provider will be responsible for all the logistics associated with organizing and conducting the said events/activities. The public hearing program will be more participative, interactive, and practical where all the stakeholders will be given the chance to share their queries unopposed. The moderation of the public hearing program will be managed by a moderator to bind the program in a standard format and save the time The event on the engagement with the CSOs/Research Institutions will be expert led for the better understanding of Parliamentarians followed by a moderated open discussion. The eservice provider must mobilize an independent expert with exemplary expertise and experience in parliamentary affairs, oversight issues and collaboration who can share his/her findings without any prejudice. The parliament openness event will be planned based on the discussion and agreement with the PA secretariat and in consultation with PSP. The service provider will ensure all public communication via relevant media to invite the public and engage the partners such as university and media, and disseminate the programme and so on. The service provider must document all the events and its output/outcome appropriately along with the report, pictures, and videos. Points of Consideration for the service Provider The service provider must coordinate with the PA secretariat appropriately for the participative program planning and to ensure the engagement of the PA secretariat in every step of program implementation. The service provider should have to be flexible enough to plan the events as per the availability of the Parliament and Committee leadership The service provider team /moderator should avoid any issues/ discussion that may cause political conflict during the events. The service provider must ensure the Gender balanced participation in each event. Report Submission Prepare and submit the event completion report with a precise Executive summary followed by activity wise chapters (1 chapter for Public hearing, one for Engagement with the CSOs in Oversight, and one on Openness event) . The Report will include key achievements and observations, points of discussion, key anecdotes/remarks of the participants, parliamentarians, lessons learnt, ways forward, and necessary annexes relating thereof to UNDP/PSP. Time Frame: The time frame for the completion of the assignment is within 01 June 30 August 2023 Expected Results/Final Products/Deliverables: Completion of 2 public hearing events on key issue with the parliament and Committee leadership in the Karnali Province where at least 100 public (including some from LGBTIQ and Persons with Disabilities groups) interact with the committee leadership. Completion of 2 events with the CSOs/Research Institution on parliamentary Oversight where 10 -15 thematic CSOs will get the opportunity to discuss about the issues with Committee leadership as stated above. Completion of 1 packaged event on promoting the parliamentary openness where at least 250 public get the opportunity to directly participate and reach out to at least 10 thousand people via social media tools A report based on the findings and outcomes of these 3 events and possible ways forward. Good photos and a small (2-3minutes) video featuring the summary of all three events and feedbacks of the participants. Make two different bids ( Two different organization) for this TOR

Problem ten sprowadza się do wyczerpania dostępnego miejsca na urządzeniu, na którym działał proces executora Sparka. Poniżej wyjaśniam poszczególne komponenty tej wiadomości oraz ogólny kontekst, w jakim taki błąd może wystąpić w środowisku Sparka. 1. **Job aborted due to stage failure**: Oznacza, że zadanie (job) zostało przerwane z powodu błędu na etapie (stage) jego realizacji. Spark dzieli zadania na etapy w zależności od operacji, które wymagają przesłania danych między węzłami. Błąd na jakimkolwiek etapie może spowodować przerwanie całego zadania. 2. **Task 5016 in stage 189.0 failed 4 times**: Wskazuje to na to, że zadanie o numerze 5016 w etapie 189.0 nie powiodło się cztery razy. Spark ma mechanizm ponawiania zadań, które się nie powiodły, często do określonej liczby prób, zanim ostatecznie uzna zadanie za nieudane. 3. **most recent failure: Lost task 5016.3 in stage 189.0 (TID 67443) (bisw87.misc.t-mobile.pl executor 16)**: Najnowsza próba wykonania zadania (w tym przypadku trzecia próba tego zadania w etapie) również się nie powiodła. Może to skutkować błędami odczytu/zapisu, ponieważ Spark (lub konkretnej jego zadania) najprawdopodobniej próbował zapisać dane na dysku (na przykład w ramach procesu shuffle, tworzenia partycji danych, zapisywania wyników itd.) i nie było gdzie ich pomieścić. question: 翻译下面的英文Due to their hydrophobic nature, pentacyclic triterpenoids are almost insoluble in water. They are classified in the biopharmaceutical classification system as class IV drugs as their pharmacological effects are limited due to their low solubility in water and potential difficulty in permeating biological membranes [78]. For these reasons, some new approaches have been introduced to enhance their biopharmaceutical properties, particularly drug delivery technologies. At present, nano-emulsions, mesoporous silica nanoparticles, solid lipid nanoparticles, liposomes, niossomal gels and solid dispersions have been proposed quite successfully [79]; however, most of these studies were performed in experimental animals, and research in humans is very scarce, despite the great therapeutic potential of these natural biocompounds. Table 1 summarizes the current knowledge of OA pharmacokinetics in humans after oral single-dose administration. Song et al. [80] reported the results of a pharmacokinetic study performed with 18 healthy male Chinese volunteers, in which the participants received a single dose of 40 mg OA (capsule preparation). Venous blood samples were collected for 48 h, and the plasma was analyzed for OA contents. The area under the plasma OA concentration–time curve (AUC) was determined in 124.3 ± 106.7 ng h/mL, with a peak OA concentration of 12.1 ± 6.8 ng/mL, which was registered at 5.2 ± 2.9 h after the OA intake. Later on, a randomized, crossover and self-control study was carried out with 18 healthy Chinese male volunteers, who received 20 mg OA orally, formulated as normal tablets and dispersible tablets [81]. The resulting pharmacokinetic parameters included AUC values of 112.2 ± 56.6 and 109.7 ± 41.6 ng h/mL, for normal and dispersible tablets, respectively, and OA peak concentrations of 18.9 ± 8.0 and 17.8 ± 7.5 ng/mL, which were recorded at 2.9 ± 1.2 and 2.5 ± 1.0 h after the triterpene administration. In 2015, Rada et al. informed on a pharmacokinetic study developed with nine adult men, who were administered 30 mg OA dissolved in 70 g of pomace olive oil. The reported AUC value was 3181.9 ± 894.3 ng h/mL, with an OA maximum concentration of 598.2 ± 176.7 ng/mL, achieved at 3.0 ± 0.8 h after the intake of the OA-containing oil. The administered OA dose revealed a distribution volume of 81.4 ± 9.7 L, and removal half-lives of 4.6 ± 1.1 h. The 30 mg OA oral dose yielded a total clearance of 35.1 ± 4.2 L/h [82]. More recently, de la Torre et al. [83] reported that an administration of 4.7 mg of OA within 30 mL of olive oil to 12 individuals led to a maximum concentration of 5.1 ± 2.1 ng/mL in plasma 4 h after the intake.

question: Story prompt: 13-year-old Max was headed to a friend’s house. As someone who can’t drive yet, he uses a ride-sharing app to get from one place to another. On this day, however, he ended up sharing a ride with a stranger. 13 years old as well, she was dressed fashionably and had an air of popularity to her. Someone who definitely went out with friends more often than others. According to the app, her destination was a large shopping mall, closer than Max’s friend’s house, thought pretty far away. It would take about 30 minutes to get to the mall. In the meantime, Max, who was never one to initiate conversation, kept to himself. Still, 30 minutes was gonna take a while. “So… mall, huh?”, awkwardly asked Max to start a conversation. “Yeah.”, was the response she gave him. Doesn’t seem like she was interested. Why would she? Everyone’s a stranger in the car. This was gonna be a long ride. Still, it didn’t seem like she was completely cold and distant. After a few minutes had passed, Max opened up with, “Hanging out with a friend today. Thinking you’re doing the same?” The girl responded, “Yeah. Probably just gonna go window shopping.”, while on her phone. “Got any other plans after that?”, asked Max. Even she was surprised to answer him so casually, saying, “We got basketball practice today at 4.” Max replied, “Oh, cool. I had a feeling you were the sporty type too.” It didn’t take long for the seemingly awkward boy and the seemingly disinterested girl to actually engage in long conversations. It didn’t even register to them that they were already at the mall. “I’m Max, by the way.” The girl replied, “My name’s Suzanna. Or Suzie, but whatever. It was nice talkin’ to you, Max.”, just before closing the door and going inside the mall. As the car began to head to his friend’s house, Max couldn’t help but think to himself, “I just had a good conversation with a stranger. Pretty, too.”
reference: As Max watched Suzanna disappear into the bustling crowd at the entrance of the mall, a small grin spread across his face. He couldn’t help but chuckle inwardly, realizing just how odd it was for him to strike up a conversation like that, and even odder that he enjoyed it. Delighted by the unexpected interaction, Max settled back into the car seat, his initial unease evaporating. The remainder of the ride felt shorter than he expected. Max was lost in thought, analyzing every part of the conversation, wondering if maybe he had seemed too curious, too eager, or just plain awkward. Yet, something about Suzanna’s casual demeanor felt refreshing. He wasn't used to this—making a connection so effortlessly. Max's friend greeted him with a wave from the front porch as the car pulled up to the curb. After thanking the driver, he hopped out and jogged up to the house, all the while recounting the ride to his waiting friend. Dusk approached as Max and his friend wrapped up a day filled with video games and laughter. While walking home, Max's thoughts wandered back to Suzanna. The way she talked about basketball practice with such passion, how she switched from a detached stranger to an engaging conversationalist—it sparked something within Max, a newfound confidence that maybe he could be that person, too. From that day on, Max no longer dreaded the ride-sharing trips to his friend's house or back home. He found himself more open to chatting with drivers or passengers, and his circle of acquaintances started to grow. At school, he became less of the quiet kid in the corner and more of the friendly face in the crowd, even striking up a conversation with a few of Suzanna's friends who recognized him from the ride share. As fate would have it, several weeks later, Max found himself in the same car with Suzanna once more. This time, the conversation started instantly, as if they were old friends catching up. They shared a laugh over the coincidence of their paths crossing again in such a busy city. “Looks like the universe has a weird sense of humor, huh?” Max said with an easy smile, as the car pulled away, blending into the city’s traffic. Suzanna grinned back. “I guess it does, Max. Maybe this should be a regular thing, shared ride buddies?” Max’s heart skipped a beat, not just at the suggestion, but at the realization that simple twists of fate could lead to such unexpected friendships, and maybe, in time, to even more.

question: In 2016, the City of Sontse, Florida, installed porcelain tile in 45 of the neighborhood community centers in the city. City managers wanted to upgrade the facilities' quality to rent them out for private functions. Designers working on the renovations selected Porcelain tile manufactured by Anato Porcelain for all floors because of its upscale appearance, durability, and slip-resistant properties. However, city leaders were concerned about users slipping on these floors due to the likelihood of wet floors from spills, plumbing issues, and water blowing in during heavy rainfall. Because of this, designers required that the new porcelain tile floors meet the American National Standards Institute ANSI B101.3 test method for measuring the wet dynamic coefficient of friction (DCOF) of Hard Surface Walkways. This test requires the floor to meet a dynamic coefficient of friction measurement equal to or greater than 0.42 under prescribed wet testing conditions. The quantity of tile ordered from Anato required a 5% overage on the tile needed for the initial installation to be delivered to each location as part of the installation process. This overage was stored at each location to be available for replacement of porcelain that might be needed over the life of the installation. The tiles for the testing were taken from these boxes so that there would be no chance of sealer or cleaning chemicals being on them. However, since installers completed the new porcelain flooring installation, slip-and-fall accidents in these community centers have increased substantially. A report on the local news made residents aware of the extent of the problem, prompting the city to sue Anato Porcelain, claiming the porcelain tile manufacturer provided does not meet the required standard for slip resistance. They are requesting that the manufacturer provide new porcelain tile, pay for testing it before installation, and pay for removal and reinstallation of the new porcelain tile. The manufacturer claims their product did meet the test standards, suggesting that the installers’ application of unapproved sealers or maintenance staff using incorrect cleaning materials post-installation can also cause the problem. The judge overseeing the case had an independent investigation company, Floor Testing Inc., measure a sample from the extra tiles for each community center to evaluate the claim. You have also been hired as an independent expert witness to evaluate if the porcelain tile provided by the manufacturer likely met or failed to meet the required standard. Your contract is for services as an ordinary fact witness. In conclusion, the decision to prioritize the Aboriginal community by the police in Australia is grounded in the recognition of their historically disadvantaged circumstances, high rates of crime, and the urgent need for targeted support. question: Write a 250-word introduction for the following essay: Change Proposal #1: Foster Personal Connections to HHV Health and Human Values is a minor that aims to foster growth of individuals as they pursue careers in health and health care. It prompts students to reflect on issues related to health with an interdisciplinary lens and think about how they can make an impact now and in the future. HHV is not intended to purely be a stepping stone to medical school or graduate school. However, some students state that they are in HHV because it will look good on their resume. In addition, many students express frustration with the assignments in HNRS 250 and do not understand how the readings and reflections connect to their journey in the minor. Another challenge is that sometimes students may conform to the values expressed by Dr. Braitberg or other professors rather than articulating their own opinion. We suggest that HHV make changes that prompt students to develop personal connections to their work in the minor. One change to foster personal connections is to integrate group values into HHV starting in the HNRS 250 class. Group values are a set of beliefs held by a group of people that inform their actions as they work together. By creating group values among each cohort and HHV as a whole, students will feel that their work in HHV is more meaningful to them and will be more invested in the program. Establishing group agreements as students begin HNRS 250 is a great way to start integrating group values in HHV. Group agreements are a set of rules agreed to by the group to create a learning environment in which students are comfortable and enthusiastic engaging in. Examples of group agreements in PATH are Listen Actively, Build the Change, and Uphold Confidentiality. Dr. Braitberg, Dr. Oberman, or other professors teaching HNRS 250 should first prompt students to reflect on what their personal values are which could include Integrity, Justice, and Health. Students can then have discussions about their individual values as a class and make connections with the values of the group and the minor. Then, the professors should have the students brainstorm group agreements that integrate group values. A challenge to this exercise may be that students will be reluctant to participate, especially as underclassmen. The professors can initiate the discussion and make connections between the values of students, but they should be careful not to dominate the activity. These group agreements should be practiced throughout HNRS 250. In addition, there should be more assignments and readings in HNRS 250, the capstone, and internship that require students to reflect on their individual and group values and how they relate to issues in health and healthcare. If students find their own values integrated more in HHV, they will be more invested and engaged as well as find value in the program beyond being a stepping stone. Change Proposal #2: Create More Experiential Learning Opportunities in the Minor The HHV minor places a focus on understanding the social, ethical, cultural, political, and structural factors shape health, disease, and health care. Such an understanding, especially that of an interdisciplinary nature, requires students to be able to critically think about different social issues related to health care. However, one of the concerns with regard to the HHV minor is that there is less student engagement, and one of the reasons for this decreased engagement may be that students sometimes may struggle to understand how the content they are learning in their HHV classes applies directly to their future careers or the communities, institutions, and other settings they are part of in the real-world. Such confusion or lack of understanding can also decrease student engagement. One of the ways to foster critical thinking as well as increase student engagement is through creating more experiential learning opportunities in the minor. Students really value the opportunity to speak with people from different community organizations that address different issues like poverty, homelessness, disability justice, etc that are discussed in the HHV classes. Having an opportunity to speak to more guest speakers can enable students to more clearly see how the content they discuss in class can be applied to the real-world and thus engage with the minor and peers more often. Through experiential learning opportunities such as volunteering and service learning, students will also have the chance to interact with different people and communities that experience the social and health issues discussed in class. This will increase students’ empathy and understanding as well as foster a passion for justice and creating change. Ultimately, experiential learning can increase students’ feelings of citizenship in the minor and ability to think about creating organic change within their own communities. Additionally, students may sometimes feel overwhelmed with too many readings and the same class structure for every class, which can also lead to decreased engagement. One way to potentially address this issue is to prioritize quality over quantity. For instance, organizing field trips to different community organizations (especially for the 250 class) in place of some regular class readings and discussions can allow students to engage with class content in a different learning environment, which can also help increase engagement and allow for a deeper understanding and connection to course material. Furthermore, creating opportunities for meaningful reflections after such experiences can enable students to reflect on their personal growth and consider numerous other career opportunities both in and outside of healthcare to address the issues they are most passionate about. Change Proposal #3: Improve Organization and Structure of HHV Classes We would like to propose an increase in overall structure and organization of the Health and Human Values classes. Establishing a clear structure that is well organized gives students peace of mind and helps them succeed academically. An essential part of any relationship is setting clear expectations of each party. In the context of a student-teacher relationship, a teacher needs to establish their expectations of the student for their class. We would recommend that a syllabus is established by the first day of class. This way, the student is able to fully understand what is expected of them from the beginning. The student can plan accordingly and ensure that the class is the right fit for them and their schedule. We also recommend that the syllabus remain relatively consistent throughout the semester and within cohorts. This would provide students with a sense of stability in addition to clear expectations. Regarding the organization of classes, we recommend that classes follow a similar structure between cohorts. Something that we have noted as mentors is that when talking with mentees, it seems that the class structure has changed since we have taken the class. Although the core values of the HHV minor are always present, it may help give students peace of mind if they knew what to expect of the introduction and the capstone course. Developing a framework that each class follows could still allow for changes from year to year, but the framework would be able to give the class some consistency. The framework could be used by other professors in the future as well. Anonymous student feedback surveys may help Dr. Braitberg to learn more about what students would like to see from the organization and structure of the HHV minor. Although there is a university wide end of semester student course survey, we believe that Dr. Braitberg should have students fill out an anonymous survey that is more specific to the organization and structure of the class. This could provide Dr. Braitberg with more helpful insight into what students would like to see with regards to structure and organization. Change Proposal #4: Increase Inter-Cohort and Alumni Support/Connection The Health and Human values minor has a diverse group of majors, internships, and various opportunities that are available to the community. However, there are rarely settings where these are shared across cohorts. The first time that we were able to share our own opportunities/experiences in depth was as mentors in the 250 course. A potential way to enrich participation in the minor is through events where sharing these opportunities is celebrated and encouraged. Thus, HHV social events one or two every semester, where HHV students in the internship, capstone, and core introductory course are required to attend would start the spread of information about unique opportunities that are available in the healthcare space. Another method to increase the inter-cohort support by other undergraduate mentors would be an HHV preceptorship for the 250 course in the spring. A preceptorship encourages dialogue between more HHV seniors and newer students in the minor. A peer mentor has the advantage of being more approachable, the shared experience of being a student in the course, and could reduce the grading workload for faculty (for smaller assignments like discussion posts). When most people enter their internship, most talk to Dr. Braitberg and the person who previously was in the internship before them, but rarely get the opportunity to see presentations about internships that are available to them. Therefore, there should be a database of posters/recorded presentations that students can watch if they are unable to come to the peer capstone/internship academic poster session. The HHV minor has multiple graduating classes, but there seems to be a lack of alumni support from those that are outside of the minor. Therefore, it is imperative that alumni offer advice and support to students that are trying to find their path through the HHV minor and beyond. There should be a form/spreadsheet with the contact information of graduated HHV students along with a note (if possible) of what their plans were immediately after graduation. This would allow HHV mentors to start connecting with alumni near graduation and could become something that could be advertised to increase the amount of people that apply to HHV. HHV is an Honors minor, but there seems to be a limited connection between it and the remainder of the Honors College. An idea that should be discussed further is offering interdisciplinary approaches to problems by offering collaborative work sessions or seminars between HHV students and other Honors minors.

question: what happens if a magnitude 10 earthquake hits China? How much money would be the damages estimated?
reference: A magnitude 10 earthquake has never been recorded in human history and would represent an event of almost unimaginable power. The highest magnitude earthquake ever recorded was the Great Chilean Earthquake of May 22, 1960, which measured 9.5. The scale used to measure earthquakes, the Moment Magnitude Scale (Mw), is logarithmic, so a magnitude 10 earthquake would release approximately 32 times more energy than a 9.5 quake. If a magnitude 10 earthquake were to occur, the effects would be catastrophic and would vary greatly depending on several factors such as the depth of the quake, the geography and geology of the affected area, population density, and the quality of infrastructure and building standards in the region. In China: 1. Tremendous Loss of Life: The potential fatality count would likely be in the millions, particularly if the quake struck a densely populated area. 2. Massive Infrastructure Damage: Cities and towns could be leveled, with buildings, roads, bridges, and other infrastructure suffering severe damage or destruction across a vast area, possibly affecting large portions of the country or even neighboring countries. 3. Economic Impact: The economic impact would be staggering, likely amounting to hundreds of billions or even trillions of US dollars. The cost would encompass the immediate impacts of destruction, the loss of life and livelihoods, and the long-term effects on the national and regional economies. It would take many years, even decades, to recover fully. 4. Humanitarian Crisis: The displacement of populations would lead to a humanitarian crisis, with a need for immediate international aid for shelter, medical care, food, and water. 5. Environmental Consequences: A quake of this magnitude could also lead to secondary disasters, such as landslides, tsunamis (if the epicenter were offshore), and flooding, which would compound the damage. 6. Global Impact: The economic aftershocks would be felt worldwide due to disruptions in supply chains and markets, especially considering China's significant role in global trade. It's important to note that the Moment Magnitude Scale is not capped at 10, but rather, a magnitude 10 earthquake is generally considered highly unlikely because it is not certain that the Earth’s crust could accumulate and then release that amount of energy. Current understanding suggests that plate tectonics would likely release accumulated stress before it could reach a magnitude 10 level. Predicting the exact amount in economic damages for such a hypothetical and unprecedented event is difficult and speculative. It would depend on the specific characteristics of the earthquake and the resilience of the infrastructure affected. For context, the 2008 Sichuan earthquake in China had a magnitude of 7.9 and caused an estimated $85 billion in damages; an earthquake more than a thousand times more powerful would lead to exponentially greater destruction and costs. In reality, it is more productive for regions at risk of earthquakes to focus on preparedness measures, such as enforcing strict building codes, developing robust early warning systems, and planning for emergency responses to mitigate the effects of high-magnitude earthquakes that are within the range of what has been historically observed.

question: Story prompt: 13-year-old Max was headed to a friend’s house. As someone who can’t drive yet, he uses a ride-sharing app to get from one place to another. On this day, however, he ended up sharing a ride with a stranger. 13 years old as well, she was dressed fashionably and had an air of popularity to her. Someone who definitely went out with friends more often than others. According to the app, her destination was a large shopping mall, closer than Max’s friend’s house, thought pretty far away. It would take about 30 minutes to get to the mall. In the meantime, Max, who was never one to initiate conversation, kept to himself. Still, 30 minutes was gonna take a while. “So… mall, huh?”, awkwardly asked Max to start a conversation. “Yeah.”, was the response she gave him. Doesn’t seem like she was interested. Why would she? Everyone’s a stranger in the car. This was gonna be a long ride. Still, it didn’t seem like she was completely cold and distant. After a few minutes had passed, Max opened up with, “Hanging out with a friend today. Thinking you’re doing the same?” The girl responded, “Yeah. Probably just gonna go window shopping.”, while on her phone. “Got any other plans after that?”, asked Max. Even she was surprised to answer him so casually, saying, “We got basketball practice today at 4.” Max replied, “Oh, cool. I had a feeling you were the sporty type too.” It didn’t take long for the seemingly awkward boy and the seemingly disinterested girl to actually engage in long conversations. It didn’t even register to them that they were already at the mall. “I’m Max, by the way.” The girl replied, “My name’s Suzanna. Or Suzie, but whatever. It was nice talkin’ to you, Max.”, just before closing the door and going inside the mall. As the car began to head to his friend’s house, Max couldn’t help but think to himself, “I just had a good conversation with a stranger. Pretty, too.”
reference: As Max watched Suzanna disappear into the bustling crowd at the entrance of the mall, a small grin spread across his face. He couldn’t help but chuckle inwardly, realizing just how odd it was for him to strike up a conversation like that, and even odder that he enjoyed it. Delighted by the unexpected interaction, Max settled back into the car seat, his initial unease evaporating. The remainder of the ride felt shorter than he expected. Max was lost in thought, analyzing every part of the conversation, wondering if maybe he had seemed too curious, too eager, or just plain awkward. Yet, something about Suzanna’s casual demeanor felt refreshing. He wasn't used to this—making a connection so effortlessly. Max's friend greeted him with a wave from the front porch as the car pulled up to the curb. After thanking the driver, he hopped out and jogged up to the house, all the while recounting the ride to his waiting friend. Dusk approached as Max and his friend wrapped up a day filled with video games and laughter. While walking home, Max's thoughts wandered back to Suzanna. The way she talked about basketball practice with such passion, how she switched from a detached stranger to an engaging conversationalist—it sparked something within Max, a newfound confidence that maybe he could be that person, too. From that day on, Max no longer dreaded the ride-sharing trips to his friend's house or back home. He found himself more open to chatting with drivers or passengers, and his circle of acquaintances started to grow. At school, he became less of the quiet kid in the corner and more of the friendly face in the crowd, even striking up a conversation with a few of Suzanna's friends who recognized him from the ride share. As fate would have it, several weeks later, Max found himself in the same car with Suzanna once more. This time, the conversation started instantly, as if they were old friends catching up. They shared a laugh over the coincidence of their paths crossing again in such a busy city. “Looks like the universe has a weird sense of humor, huh?” Max said with an easy smile, as the car pulled away, blending into the city’s traffic. Suzanna grinned back. “I guess it does, Max. Maybe this should be a regular thing, shared ride buddies?” Max’s heart skipped a beat, not just at the suggestion, but at the realization that simple twists of fate could lead to such unexpected friendships, and maybe, in time, to even more.

question: EmbedDataInBMP[bmpFile_, dataFile_, outputFile_] := Module[{imageData, dataToEmbed, extendedData, modifiedImageData, outputStream, success, dataSizeBytes}, imageData = BinaryReadList[bmpFile]; dataToEmbed = Import[dataFile, “Text”, CharacterEncoding -> “WindowsCyrillic”]; dataToEmbed = ToCharacterCode[dataToEmbed, “WindowsCyrillic”]; If[Length[dataToEmbed] == 0, MessageDialog[“Нет данных для встраивания.”]; Return[False]]; dataSizeBytes = IntegerDigits[Length[dataToEmbed], 256, 4]; extendedData = Join[dataToEmbed, ConstantArray[0, 16 - Mod[Length[dataToEmbed], 16]]]; modifiedImageData = Join[Take[imageData, 54], dataSizeBytes, extendedData, Drop[imageData, 58 + Length[extendedData]]]; outputStream = OpenWrite[outputFile, BinaryFormat -> True]; BinaryWrite[outputStream, modifiedImageData, “Byte”]; Close[outputStream]; success = FileExistsQ[outputFile]; If[success, MessageDialog[“Внедрение данных выполнено успешно.”]; True, MessageDialog[“Не удалось встроить данные.”]; False]] ;; bmpPath = “C:\Users\Я\Pictures\stego.bmp”; dataPath = “C:\Users\Я\Documents\data.txt”; outputBmpPath = “C:\Users\Я\Pictures\stego+эцп.bmp”; If[FileExistsQ[bmpPath] && FileExistsQ[dataPath], If[EmbedDataInBMP[bmpPath, dataPath, outputBmpPath], If[FileExistsQ[outputBmpPath], extractedFilePath = ExtractDataFromBMP[outputBmpPath]; MessageDialog["Данные извлечены в: " <> extractedFilePath]], MessageDialog[“Не удалось встроить.”] ] ]; обьясни алгоритм кода

Вот пошаговое объяснение алгоритма, который реализован в коде: 1. Функция `EmbedDataInBMP` принимает три аргумента: `bmpFile_` - путь к исходному BMP-изображению, `dataFile_` - путь к текстовому файлу с данными для встраивания, и `outputFile_` - путь к выходному файлу, который будет содержать встроенные данные. 2. `imageData` считывает бинарные данные BMP-изображения. 3. `dataToEmbed` импортирует данные из файла, который нужно встроить (`dataFile_`), с использованием кодировки “WindowsCyrillic” и преобразует их в список чисел, соответствующих кодам символов текста. 4. Проверка на наличие данных для встраивания: если `dataToEmbed` пуст, выводится сообщение о том, что нет данных для встраивания, и функция возвращает значение `False`. 5. `dataSizeBytes` представляет размер данных для встраивания в виде списка из 4 байтов, который будет в использован для записи размера вставляемых данных в изображение. 6. `extendedData` дополняет данные до кратного 16 путем добавления нулевых байтов, если это необходимо. 7. `modifiedImageData` объединяет исходные бинарные данные изображения (исключая первые 54 байта, которые обычно представляют заголовок BMP-файла), добавляет размер данных и непосредственно встраиваемые данные. Остаток изображения (начиная со следующего байта после вставленных данных) копируется без изменений. 8. С помощью функции `OpenWrite` создается поток для записи в выходной файл в бинарном режиме. С помощью `BinaryWrite` модифицированные данные записываются в этот файл, а затем поток закрывается функцией `Close`. 9. Проверяется успешность создания выходного файла. Если файл создан, выводится сообщение о том, что встраивание данных выполнено успешно, и функция возвращает значение `True`. В противном случае выводится сообщение об ошибке, и функция возвращает `False`. 10. Затем, этот кусок кода создает пути к файлам BMP-изображения и к текстовому файлу с данными для встраивания и вызывает функцию `EmbedDataInBMP`, чтобы выполнить процесс встраивания. 11. После встраивания (если оно было успешным), код должен был бы извлекать данные из BMP-изображения с помощью `ExtractDataFromBMP`, однако определение этой функции отсутствует в предоставленном фрагменте кода. Если функция `ExtractDataFromBMP` работает корректно и извлекает данные, путь к извлеченным данным должен выводиться в диалоговое окно с сообщением о том, где сохранены данные.
