question: 请将“At that time, regular merchant voyages linked trading centres in the Arab world, the eastern coast of Africa, India and the ‘Far East’. And this commercial world system was marked by many of the characteristics that are usually taken as indicators for the development of the capitalist world market - mature seafaring and shipbuilding, techniques of monetary transactions and exchange as well as the creation of companies in which financiers and merchants worked hand in hand. European merchants also participated in this worldwide trade. Although they played a more or less marginal role, merchants from Flanders and Champagne, Venice and Lombardy made use of these connections. They imported spices, textiles, jewels, ebony and sometimes slaves. They, by contrast, had relatively little to offer. Back then, the overall balance of trade with trading partners in the Far East was already negative, leading to a drain on silver. At the time, the world was also anything but peaceful. However, the ‘guardians’ of the trading routes guaranteed the flow of goods in exchange for toll. If from time to time the flow of goods was jeopardised, it was still possible to switch from the southern to the northern ‘silk route’ and vice versa (Abu- Lughod 1989, p. 361). And it was possible to reach India either from the Persian Gulf or the Red Sea by ship. As long as supply and demand remained intact in the three sub-systems of this trading system, world trade functioned. The decline of this world trade system was not triggered by commercial and technological backwardness or the disinterest of local rulers in trade,1 as so often suspected. But because the link was primarily a link between cities, the decline in urbanisation following the massive dying out of populations during the Black Death in the fourteenth century had a fundamental and sustained negative impact upon established relations.2 In some regions, the world trade that was to start out from Europe in the sixteenth century took up where earlier trading relations had left off.3 But on the whole, it was a new system. Because merchants of various origins were no longer prepared to allow one another to make use of the infrastructures of the trading routes of their region without hindrance, the age of monopolies had been born, and thus that of armed competition (as shown by Braudel 1979/1986). That competition was manifest in sea battles and raids on trading bases. And it was this practice of armed competition for trading monopolies which distinguished the world trade emerging from the end of the fifteenth century onwards from the world trade of the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries. If there had been attacks on the property and possibly even the lives of traders earlier, the era of armed trade first came to prevail systematically when European merchant warriors sailed the world’s seas. According to Kirti N. Chaudhuri, who conducted research on the development of trade and culture in the region of the Indian Ocean up until 1750, it is less the new development in trade relations that required explanation than the development of thoroughly armed trade (1985, p. 14). Armed trade emerged from governmental practice in the countries of origin of the merchant warriors, where in early modernity one European ruler after the other developed a practice of conferring privileges. Trading companies hoped that by acquiring a privilege, they would have the support of rulers in eliminating competition, and this was only possible if the prince announced his claim over a trading monopoly in a certain region of the world. In exchange for such privileges, the princes had themselves paid and awarded shares of expected profits. Even if the profits were not always forthcoming, appropriation through trade was thus closely tied to appropriation by princes, and thus to the use of violence. The increased presence of Europeans furthered the decline in long-term trading relations between partners. Instead, violence was often employed to earn short-term and often predatory profits. Consequently, merchants aimed at establishing trading bases that were secured and defended with the use of arms. Thus, the growing participation of European merchant warriors altered the practice of international trade.4 Robbery and Regulations While most merchants acting overseas aimed at gaining acceptance in their mother countries as members of the upper and possibly even aristocratic classes, they were less troubled by their reputation when they were overseas. Wherever they saw an opportunity, they appropriated the riches of peoples when they were overseas without bothering with the niceties of trade. An early example of this practice is to be seen in the first Iberian adventurers in South America. When they realised that Amerindians did not have the kind of merchandise they had hoped for, they plundered whatever seemed worth plundering. But they especially went for gold. ‘They were as greedy for gold as hungry pigs’, Aztecs are reported to have said of them.5 In the early stage of the ‘world market’ which had its origins in Europe, European merchant warriors not only plundered what they found abroad. Instead, wherever it appeared possible, they found shortcuts for the process of appropriation by attacking the ships loaded by their European competitors. Historical accounts read like reports on fights between bands of robbers.6 And that is precisely what they were.7 But because equipping ships was costly and princes wanted their share of the booty, many of those who participated in raids on the high seas were commissioned by or at least acted with the tacit assent of the princes of the mother countries. Even if these silent or even official partners in raids on the high seas thought the violent appropriation of wealth in every part of the world was par-ticularly desirable, they had to take account of the potential negative effects on their rule. In other words, robbing one’s European competitors had to bear at least the appearance of legitimacy. Just as on land, legitimacy for such raids was created by claiming territorial rights over parts of the seas. Much later the argument was put forward to do away with such claims because territorial rights over certain regions of the seas could not really be successfully defended. But that had not really been the point throughout the period in which such arguments were put forward as valid. For whosoever claimed territorial rights over an entire region of the sea gave himself the right to impound any ship found in the region without requiring the permission of whoever exercised sovereign jurisdiction over the vessel, to confiscate its cargo and to pass sentence on its crew as pirates. There was no court in which the legality of such a procedure could be challenged; therefore, the publication of a claim to the dominion over a certain part of the world seas included the claim to decide what was right and wrong in that territory. Letus start out by following, if only very roughly, the carving up of the world’s seas in territories. This began in 1493 when Columbus and his crew returned from their first major voyage. It had started the great race for wealth overseas. Initially, only the Crowns of Spain and Portugal seemed to have the prospect of competing successfully in this race. In order to not destabilise their rule in Europe, both powers turned to the Pope so that he could carve up the New World for them. The fact that the demarcation line chosen was changed again the following year shows clearly that negotiations prior to the conclusion of the treaty had been tough.8 Be that as it may, the ‘world’ outside Europe was split up between Spain and Portugal on 7 June 1494 under the aegis of Pope Alexander vi in the Treaty of Tordesillas. Whatever was to be found further than 370 nautical miles west of the Cape Verde Islands went to the Kingdom of Spain, while everything to the east of this imaginary line belonged to the Kingdom of Portugal. Since the end of the fifteenth century, the high sea between Europe and the Americas had thus been formally broken up into territories.9 To be precise, the Pope did not determine which part of the New World both kingdoms could rightly appropriate, but merely distributed territories in which they were allowed to do missionary work.10 Of course, this specific detail played no role in practice. Further demarcations followed. In 1526, the Treaty of Zaragoza established how the Pacific was split up. The so-called Moluccas antemeridian corresponded to today’s 135th meridian. It is possible that these lines kept Portuguese and Spanish ships from entering each other’s territories in the high seas, as laid down in the treaty, but for the French corsairs and English ‘discoverers’ sailing the seas for booty from the sixteenth century onwards, these treaties only consisted of a risk if they were defeated on the seas. To reduce this risk and thereby enhance their chances of getting a share of said booty, the rulers of the new sea powers challenged the legitimacy of the lines and demanded that their subjects should have the right to sail through the sea regions claimed by Portugal and Spain.n In Câteau-Cambrésis, negotiations were conducted for a peace treaty between Spain and France in 1559.12 It was said that there had been an additional, oral agreement amending the published text of the treaty. In any case, it was reported time and again that the peace treaty was limited to Europe and that armed conflicts beyond this ‘line of friendship’ would not be interpreted as a breach of the treaty. Although the issue of whether the treaty had this additional clause alongside the official version is still open to debate/3 it played a considerable role in academic debates over the past decades, triggered by a publication by Carl Schmitt in 1950, which in turn referred to a publication by Gustav Adolf Rein from 1930. According to Schmitt, bracketing out an area of combat outside Europe served war in Europe (1950, p. 66).14 More recent research on the treaty negotiations have shown that Spain offered to reduce its claim on territories, hitherto based on the Treaty of Tordesillas. But ultimately, Spain did not give up its claims (Kempe 2010, p. 57). They continued to apply to everyone who continued to run the risk of being attacked as pirates when violating the maritime territory to which Spain laid claim.”翻译为中文
reference: 在那个时期，定期的商船航行连接着阿拉伯世界、非洲东海岸、印度以及“远东”的贸易中心。这个商业世界体系被许多通常被视为资本主义世界市场发展指标的特征所标记——成熟的航海和造船技术、货币交易和交换技术以及金融家和商人合作的公司的创建。 欧洲商人也参与了这一全球贸易。尽管他们扮演了或多或少边缘性的角色，来自佛兰德、香槟、威尼斯和伦巴第的商人利用了这些联系。他们进口香料、纺织品、珠宝、乌木，有时也有奴隶。与之相比，他们几乎没有什么可以提供的。当时，与远东贸易伙伴的总体贸易平衡已经是负的，导致银行流失。 当时，世界也远非和平。然而，贸易路线的“守护者”通过收取过路费来保证货物的流通。如果货物流动偶尔受到威胁，仍然可以从南方的“丝绸之路”切换到北方，反之亦然（Abu-Lughod 1989，第361页）。而且还可以从波斯湾或红海乘船抵达印度。只要这个贸易系统的三个子系统中的供需保持完整，世界贸易就能运作。这个世界贸易体系的衰退并非由商业和技术的落后或地方统治者对贸易的不感兴趣触发，正如人们经常怀疑的那样。但是因为这个联系主要是城市之间的联系，因此14世纪黑死病期间人口的大量死亡对城市化的下降造成了根本性和持续的负面影响，对既有关系产生了根本性和持续的负面影响。 在某些地区，16世纪从欧洲开始的世界贸易接替了之前的贸易关系。但总体上，它是一个新系统。因为来自不同来源的商人不再愿意彼此无障碍地使用彼此地区的贸易路线的基础设施，垄断时代已经诞生，因此武装竞争时代（如Braudel 1979/1986所示）已经诞生。这种竞争表现在海上战斗和对贸易基地的袭击上。正是这种对贸易垄断权的武装竞争实践，区别于13和14世纪的世界贸易，标志着从15世纪末开始出现的世界贸易。 如果说之前对贸易商的财产甚至生命的攻击也曾存在，当欧洲的商业战士航行世界各海时，武装贸易的时代才首次系统性地盛行。根据Kirti N. Chaudhuri的研究，他研究了直到1750年印度洋地区贸易和文化的发展，不是贸易关系的新发展需要解释，而是彻底的武装贸易的发展（1985年，第14页）。 武装贸易源于商业战士的原籍国的政府实践，在那里，一个又一个的欧洲统治者在早期现代性逐渐形成了授予权利的实践。贸易公司希望通过获得特权，他们将得到统治者的支持，以消除竞争，这只有在某地区的世界宣布对贸易垄断的主张时才可能实现。为了获得这样的特权，王侯们让自己得到了报酬，并获得了预期利润的份额。即使利润并不总是如期而至，通过贸易的占有从而与王侯的占有紧密联系起来，因此与使用暴力紧密联系起来。 欧洲人的增加促进了长期贸易关系的下降。相反，往往使用暴力来获得短期和经常是掠夺性的利润。因此，商人们旨在建立用武器保护和防御的贸易基地。因此，欧洲商业战士的日益参与改变了国际贸易的实践。 掠夺与规范 虽然大多数在海外行事的商人都希望在母国被接纳为上层甚至可能是贵族阶层的成员，但当他们在海外时，他们对自己的声誉不太在意。在他们看到机会的地方，他们不顾贸易的规矩，侵占了当地人民的财富。 这种做法的一个早期例子可以在南美的第一批伊比利亚冒险家中看到。当他们意识到美洲土著没有他们希望的那种商品时，他们掠夺了看似值得掠夺的一切。但他们尤其追求黄金。“他们像饥饿的猪一样渴望黄金”，据说阿兹特克人这样说过他们。 在欧洲起源的“世界市场”的早期阶段，欧洲的商业战士不仅掠夺了他们在国外发现的东西。相反，只要有可能，他们就通过攻击欧洲竞争对手装载的船只，为占有过程找到捷径。历史记录读起来就像是抢劫团伙之间战斗的报道。而这正是它们的本质。 但是因为装备船只成本高昂，王侯们想要分得战利品的份额，许多参与高海上突袭的人士是受到母国王侯的委托，或至少是在王侯的默许下行动的。即使这些在高海上突袭中的沉默或官方合作者认为在世界每个角落通过暴力占有财富是特别理想的，他们也必须考虑到其对统治的潜在负面影响。换句话说，抢劫欧洲竞争对手至少必须具有合法性的外观。就像在陆地上一样，通过声称对海域部分地区的领土权来为这种突袭创造合法性。直到很久以后，才提出废除这种主张的论点，因为海域的某些地区的领土权真的无法成功维护。但这并不是在提出这些论点为有效期间的真正要点。 无论谁宣称对整个海域地区的领土权，给了自己在该区域发现的任何船只进行扣押的权力，无需获得对船只行使主权管辖权的人的许可，没收其货物并对其船员判定为海盗的权力。没有法院可以挑战这种程序的合法性；因此，宣称对世界海域某个部分拥有统治权的声明包括了决定该领土上什么是对与错的权力。 让我们开始跟踪，即使非常粗略地，对世界海域进行领土划分。这始于1493年，当哥伦布和他的船员从他们的第一次大航行返回时。这开启了海外财富的伟大竞赛。最初，只有西班牙和葡萄牙的王室似乎有成功竞争的前景。为了不破坏他们在欧洲的统治，两国都向教皇求助，以便他为他们划分新世界。明显的是，次年选择的分界线再次被改变，清楚地表明先前的条约谈判非常艰难。但无论如何，在教皇亚历山大六世的庇护下，1494年6月7日签订了托尔德西拉斯条约，将“世界”以外的欧洲分割给了西班牙和葡萄牙。凡是从佛得角群岛向西370海里以外的区域归西班牙王国所有，而这条想象线东侧的一切都属于葡萄牙王国。从15世纪末开始，欧洲与美洲之间的公海因此被正式划分成了领土。要精确地说，教皇并未决定两个王国可以正当地占有新世界的哪个部分，而仅仅是分配了他们被允许进行传教工作的领土。当然，这个具体细节在实践中没有任何作用。 进一步的领土划分随之而来。1526年的萨拉戈萨条约确定了太平洋的分割。所谓的摩鹿加群岛对跖点对应今天的第135经线。可能这些线阻止了葡萄牙和西班牙的船只进入高海上条约中规定的彼此领土，但对于从16世纪开始在海上寻找战利品的法国私掠船和英国“探险家”来说，这些条约只有在他们在海上被击败时才构成风险。 为了减少这种风险，从而增加获取战利品的机会，新的海上大国的统治者挑战了这些线的合法性，并要求他们的臣民有权通过葡萄牙和西班牙声称的海域。在1559年西班牙和法国之间为了一项和平条约进行的卡托-坎布雷西斯谈判中，据说有一个额外的口头协议修订了公布的条约文本。无论如何，一直有报道称和平条约仅限于欧洲，超出这个“友谊线”的武装冲突不会被解释为违反条约。虽然关于条约是否有这样一个额外的条款与官方版本并行的问题仍然存在争议，但在过去几十年的学术辩论中，这在很大程度上是由卡尔·施密特于1950年发表的出版物引发的，该出版物又参考了古斯塔夫·阿道夫·莱因1930年的出版物。根据施密特的说法，在欧洲之外排除一个战斗区域有助于欧洲的战争（1950年，第66页）。近期关于条约谈判的研究表明，西班牙提出减少其基于托尔德西拉斯条约的领土要求。但最终，西班牙并未放弃其主张。它们继续适用于所有继续冒着被攻击为海盗风险的人，当他们侵犯西班牙声称的海域领土时。

For whosoever claimed territorial rights over an entire region of the sea gave himself the right to impound any ship found in the region without requiring the permission of whoever exercised sovereign jurisdiction over the vessel, to confiscate its cargo and to pass sentence on its crew as pirates. There was no court in which the legality of such a procedure could be challenged; therefore, the publication of a claim to the dominion over a certain part of the world seas included the claim to decide what was right and wrong in that territory. Let us start out by following, if only very roughly, the carving up of the world’s seas in territories. This began in 1493 when Columbus and his crew returned from their first major voyage. It had started the great race for wealth overseas. Initially, only the Crowns of [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] seemed to have the prospect of competing successfully in this race. In order to not destabilise their rule in Europe, both powers turned to the Pope so that he could carve up the New World for them. The fact that the demarcation line chosen was changed again the following year shows clearly that negotiations prior to the conclusion of the treaty had been tough.8 Be that as it may, the ‘world’ outside Europe was split up between [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] on 7 June 1494 under the aegis of Pope Alexander vi in the Treaty of [REDACTED]. Whatever was to be found further than 370 nautical miles west of the Cape Verde Islands went to the Kingdom of [REDACTED], while everything to the east of this imaginary line belonged to the Kingdom of [REDACTED]. Since the end of the fifteenth century, the high sea between Europe and the Americas had thus been formally broken up into territories.9 To be precise, the Pope did not determine which part of the New World both kingdoms could rightly appropriate, but merely distributed territories in which they were allowed to do missionary work.10 Of course, this specific detail played no role in practice. Further demarcations followed. In 1526, the Treaty of [REDACTED] established how the Pacific was split up. The so-called Moluccas antemeridian corresponded to today’s 135th meridian. It is possible that these lines kept Portuguese and Spanish ships from entering each other’s territories in the high seas, as laid down in the treaty, but for the French corsairs and English ‘discoverers’ sailing the seas for booty from the sixteenth century onwards, these treaties only consisted of a risk if they were defeated on the seas. To reduce this risk and thereby enhance their chances of getting a share of said booty, the rulers of the new sea powers challenged the legitimacy of the lines and demanded that their subjects should have the right to sail through the sea regions claimed by [REDACTED] and [REDACTED].n In [REDACTED], negotiations were conducted for a peace treaty between [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] in 1559.12 It was said that there had been an additional, oral agreement amending the published text of the treaty. In any case, it was reported time and again that the peace treaty was limited to Europe and that armed conflicts beyond this ‘line of friendship’ would not be interpreted as a breach of the treaty. Although the issue of whether the treaty had this additional clause alongside the official version is still open to debate/3 it played a considerable role in academic debates over the past decades, triggered by a publication by [REDACTED] in 1950, which in turn referred to a publication by [REDACTED] from 1930. According to [REDACTED], bracketing out an area of combat outside Europe served war in Europe (1950, p. 66).14 More recent research on the treaty negotiations have shown that [REDACTED] offered to reduce its claim on territories, hitherto based on the Treaty of [REDACTED]. But ultimately, [REDACTED] did not give up its claims (Kempe 2010, p. 57). They continued to apply to everyone who continued to run the risk of being attacked as pirates when violating the maritime territory to which [REDACTED] laid claim.”

Some nutrients are missing in my diet so I drink a can of this nutrient drink every day. Since Jane has PKU and is affected by the disorder, we can assume that she is homozygous recessive for the PKU gene (pp). If her partner is a carrier, he would be heterozygous (Pp) for PKU. question: What are some common symptoms that Sam may experience because of his brain tumour. Choose three symptoms and explain why they would occur?
reference: Common symptoms that Sam may experience due to his brain tumor can vary depending on the tumor's location and size. However, here are three possible symptoms and explanations for their occurrence: 1. Headaches: Headaches are a prevalent symptom of brain tumors. The tumor can cause increased pressure within the skull, leading to chronic or worsening headaches. Tumors can also disrupt the normal flow of cerebrospinal fluid, leading to further pressure buildup and resulting in headaches. Additionally, as the tumor grows, it can compress or invade surrounding tissues, triggering pain signals. 2. Seizures: Brain tumors can irritate or disrupt the normal electrical activity in the brain, leading to seizures. Seizures occur when there is a sudden surge of abnormal electrical impulses in the brain. The presence of a tumor can disturb the normal functioning of brain cells and their communication, leading to these abnormal electrical discharges and subsequent seizures. 3. Cognitive and Behavioral Changes: Depending on the tumor's location, cognitive and behavioral changes may occur. Tumors in areas responsible for cognitive function, such as the frontal or temporal lobes, can affect memory, concentration, language skills, and problem-solving abilities. Tumors can also cause personality changes, mood swings, irritability, or depression due to the disruption of normal brain function and chemical imbalances caused by the tumor. It is important to note that these symptoms are not exclusive to brain tumors and can be caused by other conditions as well. If Sam experiences any of these symptoms, it is crucial for him to seek medical attention to undergo proper evaluation and receive an accurate diagnosis.

reference: Leica Biosystems is a global leader in workflow solutions and automation, integrating each step in the workflow from biopsy to diagnosis. Their focus is primarily on providing tools for pathology, histology, and cancer diagnostics. As of my knowledge cutoff in 2023, here's a rundown of the types of health tech and products developed by Leica Biosystems: 1. Tissue Processing Systems: These are designed to automate the preparation of tissue samples for analysis. This includes paraffin embedding and sectioning to prepare tissue for microscopic examination. 2. Microtomes: Microtomes are instruments used in laboratories to cut extremely thin slices of material, known as sections. Leica Biosystems offers a range of microtomes for different needs, including fully motorized and manual options. 3. Stainers: Stainers automatically apply specific stains to tissue sections to enhance the contrast of structures under a microscope, which is essential for accurate diagnosis. 4. Coverslippers: After staining, coverslippers are used to place a protective glass cover slip over the tissue sample on a slide. This is important for preserving the sample and for accurate viewing under a microscope. 5. Digital Pathology and Workflow Solutions: Leica Biosystems provides solutions for digitizing glass slides so that they can be viewed, analyzed, and shared electronically. Digital pathology enables remote diagnostics and consultations, which can significantly speed up the workflow. 6. Imaging Systems: Leica Biosystems offers a range of imaging solutions, including microscopes and cameras designed for different types of pathology and research applications. 7. Reagents and Consumables: They offer a variety of reagents and consumables necessary for tissue processing, staining, and examination including antibodies and probes utilized for immunohistochemistry (IHC). 8. Educational Software: Technologies like Aperio ePathology allow for educational collaboration where students and professionals can learn from digital slides. Leica Biosystems appears to stay at the forefront of technological innovation in their field, continually seeking to improve the efficiency and accuracy of diagnostics through advanced health tech tools and software. They are known to invest in R&D to keep up with the changing demands of pathology and laboratory medicine. question: write an article out of this press release: -- RELEASE EMBARGOED APRIL 28, 2023, AT 12 PM NOON-- Olympian clean seas activist Neil Agius attempts world-first open water swim. The 100 Mile Swim will be his greatest challenge yet. PALMA DE MALLORCA, SPAIN – On WEDNESDAY, April 27, 2023. Neil Agius, ultra-endurance athlete and world record holder, on Friday officially announced the 100 Mile Swim, a world-first record attempt in the longest non-stop, unassisted, current neutral, open water sea swim ever undertaken. The launch took place Friday, April 28, at 12:00 at the Palma International Boat Show & Superyacht Village, where Agius shared his vision for the challenge and his reasons for undertaking it. The 100 Mile Swim will see Agius attempt to swim from Mallorca around the west coast of Ibiza touching land on the eastern coast of Ibiza, covering approximately 160km, in open water. The swim will test Agius's endurance, strength, and mental resilience. A former Olympian and current world record holder in another category of swim, Agius is no stranger to pushing his limits. However, the 100 Mile Swim represents his most ambitious challenge yet. Speaking ahead of the launch, Agius said, "The 100 Mile Swim is not just about setting a world record. More importantly, it is about highlighting the problem of pollution and pollutants in the seas and oceans.” Media Contact: Ivan Martin <PRESIDIO_ANONYMIZED_EMAIL_ADDRESS> <PRESIDIO_ANONYMIZED_PHONE_NUMBER> The 100 Mile Swim will take place in the summer of 2023 during a brief weather window that begins at the end of June. Agius has been training intensively for months to prepare for the challenge. He is supported by a team of around 25 volunteers and professionals made up of medics, swim observers, navigators, skippers and crew, motivators, media, and a nutritionist, who will ensure that he remains safe and healthy throughout the swim. The launch of the 100 Mile Swim is expected to generate significant interest from the global media and supporters. Agius's previous successful world record attempts have been covered by major news outlets around the world, and the 100 Mile Swim is likely to attract even more attention. The swim will also raise awareness for ocean conservation and the urgent need to conserve our precious marine ecosystem, causes very close to Neil's heart. The 100 Mile swim is supported by the Mallorca Preservation Foundation as well as Neil's own NGO Wave of Change Malta, Ocibar Marinas and the Palma International Boat Show as well as being proudly sponsored by Atlas Insurance and Visit Malta. The Palma International Boat Show & Superyacht Village provides the perfect backdrop for the launch of the 100 Mile Swim. The event is one of the most prestigious boat shows in the world and attracts thousands of visitors each year. Agius will have the opportunity to speak to a global audience about his vision for the challenge and the impact he hopes it will have. The launch of the 100 Mile Swim is set to be a historic moment for endurance swimming and a significant milestone for Agius personally. With just a few months to go until the swim, Agius and his team are ready to take on this epic challenge and make history. question: first separate input: 'CHAPTER 1 INTRODUCTION In this chapter, we describe the research background with respect to hand kinematics analysis methods and state-of-art studies of hand and fingers tracking system, then we show the significance of researches for hand and fingers tracking technology in various fields (section 1.1). Next we state our research motivation (section 1.2), and we present overall contribution and innovations of the research (section 1.3). We finish up with the basic organization of the following of the thesis (section 1.4). 1.1 Research Background and Significance Recent researches have focused on developing hand and high-precision finger motion detection systems for a variety of applications based on tracking methods, such as robotics, virtual reality, and medicine Rehabilitation. Some of those applications are as follow: -Robotics: The most popular study field in robotics is the manufacture of prostherix hands. Researchers design prototype of an underactuated prosthetic hand, which improve the range of motion and dexterity of thumb and pinch and innovatively restore the capability of the thumb-index pinch [1]. -Virtual reality: Hand movement is the main means of interacting with the environment, so it is crucial in virtual reality (VR) applications. Although the existing inverse kinematics motion detection is sufficient for full body tracking (Fig.1.1) [2], it is difficult to locate small body parts such as fingers, and these parts are often blocked in the optical detection process. VR professionals need additional systems (such as inertial trackers) with low reliability [3]. -Medicine Rehabilitation: A 5-DOF hand rehabilitation robot is designed and developed using a synthetic method for generating natural curved finger tip motion using a 1-DOF mechanism (Fig.1.2). It’s practical in the diagnosis and treatment of hand injuries and diseases [4]. With the help of advanced sensors and computer vision methods, those system is able to capture and analyze finger movements. Machine learning algorithms are often used to interpret the data and provide real-time feedback to users [5,6] . These studies give us examples and inspires of the importance of hand-finger motion detection in different industries, and also show promise in improving the accuracy of the finger motion detection and tracking system. However, there are still challenges in developing a compact and comfortable system for users to wear and use for a long time, as well as its applicability in more application scenarios. 1.2 Motivation The existing research has done enough detail in measuring and tracking hand movements, and has derived many extensions and applications in various fields. However, the bending and extension of a single finger is different from the movement of the entire hand, and the detection of finger movement becomes very difficult when moving or rotating. In current finger motion detection technology, there are two distinct categories can be distinguished depending on the use of cameras or individual sensors. -Vision based: Use passive optical motion capture technology by setting cameras to capture the dynamic image of a specially designed glove with markers, then use the machine vision technique to process the images and correlate the local variation of image to the motion of fingers or change in the hand gesture [7,8]. The vision based hand tracking system has non-contact perception function, making hand motion detection convenient and efficient. Besides, machine vision and imaging analysis based on camara involve expensive components and complex algorithms [9], which are very expensive for ordinary users. The main advantage of a vision based system is its high tracking accuracy, but it has drawbacks such as sensitivity to light intensity fluctuations and occlusion issues, which may lead to tracking errors [10]. -Sensors based: The sensor-based systems directly detect the motion and bending of the fingers using various types of sensors such as accelerometers [4], gyroscopes, magnetic sensors, resistive sensors, and ElectroMyoGraphy (EMG) sensors [11] etc. To a certain it can help to mitigate the problem of vision-based system. Besides, the sensor-based systems are also in general more compact and inexpensive. However, acceleration or inertial sensors are generally susceptible to gravitational artifacts due to the rotation and vibration of arms or bodies. In our research, we intend to design and develop a magnetic sensors based device which is hihgly compact and have ability to detect finger motions real-time accurately. Because magnetic sensors have advantages over limitations of vision based systems which severely restricted the adoption of hand tracking in real-world applications (bulky tethered systems is impractical and line of sight or privacy concerns) [12]. Finger tips are significant marks of hand kinematics analysis, which have fewer amounts than joint angles of fingers and simpler structure. We intend to fix a magnetic sensor on each fingertips and a permanent magnet on the dorsal side of the hand to detect finger motions. Since the magnetic permeability of the human body is very similar to air, water and other non-ferromagnetic materials, it does not affect the static magnetic field [13]. The low-cost, compact, and accessible hand-finger motion tracking system is possible. 1.3 Contributions We propose a magnetic hand-finger motion tracking system which is simple, compact, low-cost, accurate and unobstructive for intelligent human-computer interface and various other applications involving hand gestures recognization. The core principle is relative fingertips position estimating with the use of magnetic sensors, then detect the hand gestures from the orientation and locations of the fingertips. The main contributions of our research are: 1. A intelligent finger motion tracking system using magnetic sensors is porposed. For sensors detecting part of the system, we choose the scheme that measure the orientations and locations of sensors in motion in a stationary magnetic field created by one permanent magnet. A permanent magnet is fixed on the dorsal side of the hand. Five 9-axis IMUs is settled on each of the fingertips, and one 6-axis IMU is fixed with the permanent magnet in order to achieve the attitude calibration and distance measurement between IMUs. After we get the result of finger motion by combining each 9-axis sensors’ orientations and locations (angular velocity on 3-axis, acceleration rate on 3-axis, and magnetic flux density on 3-axis), the next step is to adopt deep learning approaches to realize the real-time gesture recognization function. Various common gestures can be displayed as corresponding patterns when we make actual movements. 2. A set of algorithms for computing orientations and locations of sensors on the fingertips are proposed. First, we use EKF method for estimating the orientations of the 9-axis sensors on the fingertips to the 6-axis sensors on the dorsal side of the hand. After orthogonalization the coordinate system of two sensors through matrix operation, we apply L-M algorithm to calculate the linear distance between those two sensors to get the locations of 9-axis sensors. The L-M algorithm is based on a dipole model which approximate the magnet as a dipole under the research condition. Our experiments show the dipole model satisfied high approximation and accuracy within a certain range which is sufficient for finger motion tracking and gesture recognization. 3. A DNN method is adopted to achieve the real-time gesture recognization function. DNN map the features of existing spatial samples to another feature space through layer by layer feature mapping, in order to learn better feature representation for existing inputs. Firstly we maintain the posture of a specified gesture on the device and create positional data of the gesture in three-dimensional space through the movements and rotations of the hand and wrist. Then we cyclically group and train all data to obtain high accuracy in both training and testing sets. Finally, we use the wearable device to continuously make any gesture in the gesture library, the terminal can accurately display the corresponding gesture pattern. We develop our device prototype on a SBC: Raspberry pi 4b. It is also fixed on the dorsal side of hand aiming to read data and computing the orientations and locations of sensors. The data from 9-axis sensors are transmitted by I2C bus real-timely to the SBC for the next step of attitude calibration and distance calculation. Besides, we use our originally designed PCB to achieve improvements on stability and integration. Finally we fabricate prototype device on a left-hand glove, improve the compactness and comfort additionally. '

question: расскажи про PR-кампанию Coca-Cola “Share a Coke"
reference: Кампания "Share a Coke" была запущена Coca-Cola в 2011 году в Австралии и Новой Зеландии и быстро стала мировым хитом. Это была первая кампания, в рамках которой были заменены стандартные надписи на банках и бутылках Coca-Cola именами потребителей. Главная идея PR-кампании заключалась в том, чтобы способствовать более тесному общению между людьми. Coca-Cola считает, что этот напиток — не просто банальный продукт питания, он может объединять людей, поэтому в качестве etiltes предлагалась наладить общение с разными людьми, поделиться напитком и порадовать близких. Компания проводила рекламную кампанию в социальных сетях, печатных изданиях, телевидении, на сайте и в магазинах. Многие стали постить фотографии с банками Coca-Cola в социальных сетях с хэштегом #shareacoke, что способствовало еще большей популяризации кампании. Стоит отметить, что эта кампания оказалась беспрецедентно успешной и, по словам сотрудников Coca-Cola, превзошла все ожидания. Она получила международное признание и была запущена во многих странах мира. Бренд также продолжил кампанию вплоть до недавнего времени, добавив новые имена на банки и бутылки Coca-Cola и предложив потребителям напечатать свои имена и создать персонализированную банку.

question: Coastal restoration and rehabilitation offer great promise for vulnerable and marginalized groups in need of adaptation. However in Kenya, a critical research gap in evidence-based policy discussions demands immediate attention to advance these efforts towards building resilience for the most vulnerable segments of society. Presently, there is a lack of a dedicated community-led framework and relevant indicators that can effectively align coastal restoration and rehabilitation initiatives with the priorities of different social groups, especially those who are vulnerable and marginalized, such as women, children, indigenous communities, persons with disabilities, and minorities, all residing within the coastal regions. Additionally, there is a pressing need to establish methods for measuring and reporting the effectiveness of these restoration and rehabilitation efforts in addressing the intersectional vulnerabilities within these communities. Furthermore, linking the lessons learned from these initiatives to national adaptation plans and NDCs (Nationally Determined Contributions) is essential for ensuring a comprehensive approach to coastal resilience and safeguarding the interests of the vulnerable populations. The project aims to co-create locally led restoration indicators with the established community of practices and all the stakeholders through development of evidence based policy labs. Our project main goals: 1. To map out all stakeholders and establish a community of practice in coastal conservation and restoration. 2. To assess Policy, Institutional Framework and Knowledge gaps on coastal ecosystem restoration initiatives. 3. To assess the locally led restoration activities undertaken by different community groups. 4. To work with different local community groups to co-develop and agree on indicators that capture priority restoration actions and their expectations of impacts based on the assessed gaps 5. Co-development of impact learning and conservation framework: Based on the assessments, we will develop learning materials on restoration and conservation of coastal ecosystems and a conservation framework that targets the specific needs of coastal communities. 6. Establishment of multi stakeholder policy labs that will target all stakeholders and community of practice implementing restoration programs. These will be trained on Locally led restoration metrics co-production and development

question: summarise into bullet points: When I am emailed by pupils studying The Woman in Black for GCSE and A-level, many refer to it as "gothic", and indeed it forms part of a university course in gothic literature. But although the book has something in common with the pure gothic fiction of the 18th and 19th centuries, it is really only a distant cousin of the genre. It is a ghost story – not a horror story, not a thriller – and not a gothic novel; although the terms are often used very loosely, they are not by any means the same thing. I set out to write a ghost story in the classic 19th-century tradition, a full-length one. There have never been many, writers perhaps having felt the form would not stretch successfully. By the time I began mine, in the 1980s, full-length ghost stories seemed to have died out altogether. I read and studied the Jameses, Henry and MR, and Dickens, and I also had beside me the "bible" – Night Visitors by Julia Briggs (still the best study of the form). The list of ingredients included atmosphere, a ghost, a haunted house and other places, and weather. A footnote to "ghost" was a) of a human being; and b) with a purpose. There are dozens of little books of "true" ghost stories, usually sorted by geographical location, but almost without exception the ghosts have no purpose and so the stories are ultimately unsatisfying. A headless horseman rides by, a phantom coach clatters down a dark road, a veiled lady drifts up a staircase and through a wall, a pale and misty child's face is glimpsed at a window – and that is all. The ghosts are there and they apparently go through the same motions again and again. It is ultimately uninteresting. There has to be more to fiction than that. There also has to be more than an easy manipulation of the reader's superficial emotions – unless making someone jump out of their skin is the writer's only aim. Not that trying to induce a delicious thrill of fear is bad – it is another form of entertainment, and what is wrong with being an entertainer? Dickens certainly considered himself to be one. I knew my ghost story, like all my fiction, had to have a serious point and it was this that must sustain the length and underpin the sense of place, the creation of atmosphere and the events. But moral points come out of character, and I kept asking myself the question: "Why does a ghost return to this life?" Perhaps to give information that they have withheld in life – the whereabouts of a will, say, or the identity of a murderer, or to warn. reference: 1- As an inventory management employee at Shell Company, I would need to assess the overall business goals and objectives to determine if the inventory management strategy is aligned with them. This would involve evaluating factors such as customer demand, production capacity, cost efficiency, and profitability. By ensuring that the inventory management strategy is synchronized with the broader business goals, we can effectively balance supply and demand, minimize stockouts, reduce excess inventory, and optimize working capital utilization. 2- Inventory management plays a crucial role in meeting customer satisfaction levels. By maintaining appropriate inventory levels, we can ensure the availability of products when customers need them, reducing backorders or delays in delivery. Additionally, accurate inventory management enables efficient order fulfillment, minimizing errors and improving order accuracy. Properly managed inventory with real-time visibility can also enhance forecasting accuracy, enabling better predictability for customers and reducing unexpected supply chain disruptions. 3- There are always opportunities to improve supplier relationships and negotiate better terms. As an inventory management employee, I would continuously evaluate the performance of suppliers, considering aspects such as product quality, on-time delivery, and pricing. By identifying areas for improvement and working collaboratively with suppliers, we can enhance communication, optimize replenishment lead times, reduce costs, and negotiate favorable terms. Strengthening supplier relationships can lead to improved reliability, flexibility, and responsiveness in the supply chain, ultimately benefiting both Shell Company and its customers. 4- Process improvement and automation are areas of great potential for enhancing inventory management. Implementing advanced technologies, such as inventory management systems, can automate manual tasks, improve data accuracy, and provide real-time visibility into inventory levels and movements. Automation can enable more efficient demand forecasting, optimizing inventory replenishment and reducing the risk of stockouts or excess inventory. Furthermore, it can enable better coordination with suppliers, streamline order processing, and improve inventory turnover ratios. Investing in process improvement and automation can lead to higher productivity, reduced costs, improved accuracy, and enhanced decision-making capabilities for the inventory management team at Shell Company.

question: Ledbury Poetry (UK) has announced that Donegal poet Annemarie Ní Churreáin is among the poets shortlisted for the fourth Ledbury Hellens Poetry Prize for best second collection published in Britain or Ireland in 2021 or 2022. The prize aims to support and encourage poets at the mid-career stage, with a prize of £5000 for the winning second collection. Speaking of Ní Churreáin’s nominated work, judges Togara Muzanenhamo and Penelope Shuttle said: “Drawing inspiration from the concept of restorative justice – Annemarie Ní Churreáin’s The Poison Glen entwines legend from the Gaeltacht landscape with moments from history to depict the systematic mistreatment of unmarried or abandoned mothers and the children born to these women. Ní Churreáin revisits locations of state care institutions in Ireland over the past hundred years and beyond with an inquisitive lens that requires us to ask what the left-behind sites remember or what sense of the child remains after trauma. The Poison Glen stands as a literary monument to silenced voices”. ADVERTISEMENT - CONTINUE READING BELOW Originally from Cloich Cheann Fhaola, Ní Churreáin's books include Bloodroot, Doire Press, 2017, Town, The Salvage Press, 2018, and The Poison Glen, The Gallery Press, 2021. She is a recipient of the Irish Arts Council’s Next Generation Artist Award and a co-recipient of The Markievicz Award. She is Poetry Editor at The Stinging Fly Magazine. Her most recent literary project, a limited edition poetry pamphlet titled Ghostgirl, explores the Stranorlar Workhouse and Stranorlar County Home, also known as Stranorlar Mother and Baby Home. The project was a commission of the Donegal Archives Service as part of the Donegal Decade of Centenaries Programme. Co-judge Togara Muzanenhamo said: “The award is particularly special because it celebrates the accomplishment of what can be an artistic hurdle for some poets – compiling a second collection. There are numerous prizes for first collections and best collections but few focus on the pivotal role of a poets’ second book – a book that may highlight a poet’s maturing voice or solidify their career. I am excited at the prospect of reading work that will confidently explore and freely navigate language and introduce us to voices that will shape the future of poetry”. ADVERTISEMENT - CONTINUE READING BELOW The other collections and poets shortlisted for the prize are; Kaveh Akbar (Chatto) Pilgrim Bell; All the Names Given, Raymond Antrobus (Picador); A Blood Condition, Kayo Chingonyi (Chatto); England’s Green, Zaffar Kunial (Faber); Bloom, Sarah Westcott (Pavilion Poetry). The winner of the fourth Ledbury Hellens Poetry Prize will be announced on December 4 at 7pm at an online prize giving ceremony hosted by the Ledbury Centre.

question: Rewrite and improve this paragraph, adding examples that are very meaningful to children: Running your own cotton candy stand is no joke. Ralph, the enterprising owner of Ralph's Fairy Floss, just stress ate three bags of the stuff: he's got a big decision to make about the price of his cotton candy. The outcome of Ralph's decision will depend not only on the actions he takes but also on the actions of his only competitor, Regina. Both Ralph and Regina have two choices: lower their prices or keep their prices the same. Ralph would like to choose the action that will maximize his profits. But given the interdependencies of each competitor's actions, this decision is not so easy. Enter game theory, the formal study of decision-making in situations where one player's outcome depends on other players' decisions.

On the other hand, if he keeps his prices the same, he may not attract as many customers and miss out on potential profits. Ralph needs to strategize to find the perfect balance that maximizes his earnings while considering the actions of his competitor, Regina. This is where game theory comes into play: the scientific study of decision-making when a player's outcome relies on the decisions made by other players. By analyzing the choices of both players, Ralph can make an informed decision that will give him the best chance of achieving his goal. Perhaps Ralph and Regina could even engage in a fun and friendly competition to see who can sell the most cotton candy, adding an extra element of excitement and motivation for young readers. So, as Ralph ponders over his cotton candy pricing dilemma, he begins to think strategically and creatively, weighing the potential outcomes and considering the actions of his competitor. By using game theory, Ralph can increase his chances of success and bring childhood dreams, like owning a new bike, closer to reality.

question: Structure and optimize the following focus plan: Background: Aly has been with Amazon for 12 months, He joined VF team in July of 22’’ as city manager for West Cairo shortly before PEAK and showed high ownership and bias for action and was rated as an HV2. Shortly after PEAK, and starting in Jan 23’’, Aly faced a few health-related family issues that started to clearly affect his focus, performance and output. He requested multiple personal leaves, and the team offered support to cover for him. After things seemingly started to get better on the personal aspects, his performance never picked up, rather, it continued to slack. Performance Assessment: As a City manager Aly is responsible for all West Cairo sites, 5 of which are critical- high volume VF sites with Amazon AAs on ground. Aly is tasked with all on ground operations, IB control, stock control, AA performance, TPH, labor management and their development for all of his sites. On ground Ops: Aly has not been fully present on ground for the past couple of months and has been relying more on the on-ground supervisor to control operations hence multiple issues are not being identified on time and handled properly. In addition, a few instances occurred where even when he was present on ground he failed (or chose not to) to communicate high risk impactful issues to his superiors, pears or relevant stakeholders which led to tons of extra work on the team’s end and at times translated to actual misses impacting overall team metrics and performance. IB and stock Control: Continuous gaps have been found in both areas with multiple promises of remediation on his end with no appropriate output. Issues have not been brought to leadership attention on time, because of vague, incomplete or untrue answers to follow-up questions which resulted in a significant trust breach between Aly and the team. AA performance and TPH: Due to his lack of presence on ground, TPH has been dropping from its BAU value and AA’s performance has been slacking. Multiple instances occurred where items were poorly packed, lost, shipped without AWBs, etc.. A clear lack of control, follow up and proper training has been identified and communicated to Aly without proper actions taken on his end to fix it. Initial Performance Assessment Conclusion: Aly’s continuous drop in performance and irresponsiveness to feedback, along with serious concerns on earning trust has led the team to decide on putting him on focus to communicate the gaps more assertively and track performance progress very closely. Task, goals and actions should be communicated to him in details, with clear milestones, deliverables and deadlines in order to assess his progress properly. Development Areas; 1- Work on earning back team’s trust by communicating more clearly and truthfully in a timely manner. 2- Take back control of on ground ops, by being more present and DDing into all matters in question. 3- Work on better tracking AA’s performance & TPH, identify gaps and work in depth to develop and train AAs and optimize TPH. 4- Keep track of data and volumes to better manage and communicate labor needs, and optimize rooster. 5- Work on his communication skills with the team and relevant stakeholders to be able to callout critical issues on time. 6- Work on better understanding priorities, criticalities and time sensitivity of his tasks.
reference: Focus Plan: Objective: Improve performance and address development areas for Aly, the city manager for West Cairo. 1. Establish Trust and Communication: - Schedule a one-on-one meeting with Aly to discuss the concerns raised regarding trust and communication. - Clearly communicate the impact of his lack of transparency and timely communication on the team's performance and metrics. - Set expectations for open and honest communication, emphasizing the importance of timely updates on high-risk issues. - Provide specific examples of incidents where trust was breached and discuss the consequences on the team. - Regularly check-in to ensure Aly is making efforts to regain the team's trust. 2. On-Ground Operations Management: - Clearly define Aly's responsibilities as the city manager for all West Cairo sites, including on-ground operations, IB control, stock control, AA performance, TPH, labor management, and development. - Emphasize the importance of Aly being fully present on the ground and actively involved in operations. - Schedule regular on-site visits for Aly to monitor operations, identify issues, and provide support to the on-ground supervisor. - Implement a system for Aly to report and escalate high-risk issues promptly to superiors, peers, and relevant stakeholders. - Monitor Aly's presence and involvement in on-ground operations and provide feedback on improvements. 3. AA Performance and TPH Optimization: - Regularly review AA performance and TPH metrics with Aly. - Identify gaps in training and development for AAs and provide resources and support to address these gaps. - Set clear expectations for AA performance, proper packing, tracking, and follow-up processes. - Implement a performance tracking system to monitor improvements in TPH and AA performance. - Provide regular feedback and coaching to Aly on optimizing AA performance and TPH. 4. Labor Management and Optimization: - Work with Aly to establish a system to track data and volumes for better labor management. - Define clear goals and targets for labor optimization, including roster management. - Regularly review labor needs and align resources accordingly to avoid understaffing or overstaffing. - Provide training and support to Aly on labor management techniques and effective communication with relevant stakeholders. 5. Communication Skills Enhancement: - Offer communication skills training to Aly, focusing on effectively conveying critical issues and time sensitivity. - Provide resources and guidance on prioritization techniques to help Aly better understand and manage his tasks. - Encourage regular communication and feedback sessions to practice and improve communication skills. - Provide ongoing support and guidance to Aly in developing his communication skills with the team and relevant stakeholders. 6. Progress Tracking: - Establish regular progress check-ins with Aly to assess his progress in addressing the development areas. - Monitor and review milestones, deliverables, and deadlines to ensure progress is being made. - Provide constructive feedback and guidance on areas where improvement is still needed. - Celebrate and acknowledge achievements and improvements made by Aly. By implementing this focus plan, Aly will have clear goals and actions to work on, allowing for better performance assessment and improvement in his role as the city manager for West Cairo.

How are these findings important to specific audiences such as expectant mothers, families or married couples, young people who are exposed to stress and substances, and healthcare professionals. A., Blake, J., DeFrancesco, M. S., DeNicola, N., Martin Jr, J. N., ... & Giudice, L. C. (2015). International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics opinion on reproductive health impacts of exposure to toxic environmental chemicals. International Journal of Gynecology & Obstetrics, 131(3), 219-225.
reference: **Study Overview and Implications** The groundbreaking research conducted by Di Renzo et al. (2015) aimed to elucidate the reproductive health impacts of exposure to toxic environmental chemicals. The study meticulously outlined how various common environmental pollutants, such as pesticides, air pollutants, metals, and endocrine-disrupting chemicals, adversely affect the health of pregnant women, fetuses, and reproductive outcomes. One pivotal finding from this research is the discernible link between exposure to these chemicals and a range of adverse health outcomes, including preterm birth, low birth weight, and developmental defects. Expectant mothers stand as one of the primary audiences who can greatly benefit from these findings. The study not only raises awareness about the potential dangers these women face from environmental pollutants but also empowers them with knowledge, potentially guiding them in mitigating unnecessary exposures. Understanding this risk profile may encourage expectant mothers to advocate for safer environmental practices and regulations, seek out environments with better air quality, and be more vigilant about avoiding high-risk substances. Families and married couples planning for children could also utilize this information by adjusting lifestyle choices and domestic environments to foster healthier reproductive outcomes. Knowledge of toxic substances at play could transform the choices they make, influencing their residential decisions, consumer behavior, and even political engagement to support environmental reforms for safer communities. Young people exposed to stress and addictive substances are another significant group that could stand to gain knowledge from this research. Often on the cusp of their reproductive years, understanding the long-term implications of their exposure could inform better life decisions, aid in lobbying for healthier college campuses and work environments, and inspire engagement with public health initiatives that target environmental health. Healthcare professionals, as key interpreters and implementers of such research, can integrate these findings into their practice by increased screening for environmental exposures, offering advice for risk reduction, and continuing education to stay abreast of new research. They can also contribute to the broader dialogue on environmental health policy, bolstered by evidence-based understanding of these risks. **Limitations of the Study** Despite the valuable insights garnered from the study by Di Renzo et al. (2015), several limitations warrant consideration. Firstly, the global nature of this research brings variability in environmental laws, exposure levels, and health outcomes that may not apply uniformly across different populations. Hence, the transferability and applicability of the findings may require regional adaptation. Secondly, the mixed-method approaches of correlating reproductive outcomes with environmental exposures face challenges of causal inferences due to potential confounding factors. Lifestyle, genetic predispositions, and other environmental factors not wholly accounted for might skew the perceived impacts of toxic chemicals. Furthermore, the rapid evolution of manufacturing practices introduces new chemicals into environments faster than research can reliably assess their implications. This timing gap leaves practitioners and patients relying on incomplete information for making crucial health decisions. Lastly, the article targets only a slice of reproductive health, potentially overlooking broader systemic health impacts associated with environmental exposures that could also influence reproductive outcomes. **Next Steps** In light of these findings and limitations, the next logical step in research would be to conduct longitudinal and cross-sectional studies focusing on specific chemicals and their direct impact on reproductive health outcomes. These studies should prioritize establishing causal relationships and consider variables such as timing, dosage, and individual susceptibilities to exposure. Additionally, there would be value in increasing research into the effectiveness of different interventions at the personal, community, and policy levels to reduce harmful exposures. Participation in community and policy initiatives should also be investigated to understand the broader social effects. Moreover, exploring the epigenetic changes resulting from exposures and their potential to affect several generations could significantly extend the current research. Investigations into the long-term implications of these epigenetic modifications could help in developing better predictive models for individual risks. Finally, the development of advanced monitoring and diagnostic tools for early detection of environmental pollutant levels in human tissues would augment preventative approaches in healthcare and support more personalized patient guidance. **Conclusion** Di Renzo et al. (2015) have contributed significantly to the field of reproductive health and toxicology by highlighting the insidious threats posed by environmental chemicals. The implications of their study demand concerted attention from expectant mothers, families, young individuals, and healthcare professionals in forming a united front against environmental health hazards. While there are limitations to their findings, such as regional applicability and potential confounding variables, the importance of continued research in this area is unequivocal. The pursuit of deeper insights through more granular studies, interventions, and advanced technology informs the next frontier in safeguarding reproductive health against the backdrop of an increasingly polluted world. This ongoing effort not only has the potential to improve individual health outcomes but will also resonate through public policy, ultimately striving for healthier communities and environments.

question: prière de m'écrire une lettre de motivation pour le poste Ingénieur - Expert Navigabilité (F/H): Description du poste L'entreprise: AIA Bordeaux Le service industriel aéronautique (SIAé) du Ministère des Armées est en charge des actions de maintenance et de réparation des matériels aéronautiques. Rattaché à l’état-major de l’armée de l’air et de l’espace (EMAAE), il est composé d'une direction centrale et de 5 ateliers industriels aéronautiques (AIA) répartis sur 11 sites de production. L’AIA de Bordeaux a pour mission principale la maintenance et la réparation des moteurs, propulseurs ou turboréacteurs. Description du poste L’AIA de Bordeaux réalise des prestations de soutien technique en utilisation et d’ingénierie de maintenance afin de soutenir ses activités de MCO mais également afin d’améliorer la disponibilité globale des matériels. Ces activités de conception sont réalisées dans l’environnement réglementaire EMAR 21J. De plus, l’AIA de Bordeaux assure les responsabilités de Détention de Certificats de Type et en particulier de suivi de navigabilité pour plusieurs matériels certifiés par l’Autorité Technique militaire française. Le poste à pourvoir relève du Bureau Navigabilité qui exerce les prérogatives et privilèges associés à la Reconnaissance d’Aptitude à la Conception EMAR21J permettant d’approuver les activités d’ingénierie de maintenance, de conception et de suivi de navigabilité au sein de la sous-direction Technique. Le poste requiert la connaissance des règlements en matière de certification des systèmes aéronautiques (civils ou militaires) ainsi que la connaissance du domaine aéronautique et des activités de maintenance. Il nécessite également une bonne maitrise des analyses de risques et de fiabilité des systèmes. Son action s'exerce principalement sur : La définition technique, la gestion de configuration et le suivi de la navigabilité des produits dont le SIAé est détenteur du Certificat de Type en relation avec les concepteurs de ces produits, L’évolution de la définition technique applicable aux produits entretenus par l’AIA de Bordeaux ainsi que la maintenance associée à ces produits, La mise en œuvre, le maintien et l’évolution de la Reconnaissance d’Aptitude à la Conception EMAR 21J détenue par le SIAé en relation avec l’Autorité Technique. L’ingénieur navigabilité fait partie d’une équipe pluridisciplinaire pour laquelle il assure le pilotage : Des activités de collecte et d’analyses des événements en service, de la remonté des événements vers l’Autorité de Certification et de l’élaboration des dispositions de préservation, Des activités de certification des évolutions de la définition en relation avec les experts technique et l’Autorité de Certification, De veille réglementaire, que ce soit en matière d’exigences techniques (base de certification) ou bien en matière d’organisation de l’activité de conception en concertation avec le département qualité et la direction de service. L’ingénieur navigabilité assure également l’accompagnement des entités dans une démarche d’amélioration continu des processus associés à la Reconnaissance d’Aptitude à la Conception et réalise la formation des personnels aux activités relevant de la conception. Profil recherché De formation Bac +5 reconnue par l'Etat, vous disposez d’une expérience significative dans le domaine de la conception aéronautique, de la certification ou du suivi de navigabilité aéronautique, de préférence dans le secteur des turbomachines. La connaissance de la réglementation aéronautique civile PART 21 ou militaire EMAR 21 ainsi que la connaissance des exigences normatives en matière de conception (EN9100) est un plus. Curieux(se), rigoureux(se), autonome, doté(e) d’une bonne capacité de synthèse et d’aisance relationnelle, vous aimez évoluer dans un environnement complexe et vous confronter à des problématiques multiples et variées. Enfin vous êtes en mesure d’animer des réunions en français mais également en anglais. Le poste est basé à Bordeaux. Des déplacements ponctuels en France ou à l’étranger sont à envisager.
reference: Objet : Candidature au poste d'Ingénieur - Expert Navigabilité (F/H) Madame, Monsieur, Je souhaiterais vous proposer ma candidature au poste d'Ingénieur - Expert Navigabilité (F/H) que vous proposez au sein de votre entreprise, AIA Bordeaux. Votre entreprise, reconnue dans le secteur aéronautique pour sa qualité et son professionnalisme, est pour moi une référence en matière de performance et de savoir-faire. Travailler dans votre entreprise serait pour moi une chance de mettre en avant mes compétences et mes aptitudes. Forte de mes compétences et de mes expériences professionnelles en tant qu'ingénieur en aéronautique, j'ai développé une connaissance approfondie de la réglementation aéronautique et des activités de maintenance. Je suis en mesure d'effectuer une veille réglementaire effective pour suivre l'évolution des exigences techniques et l'organisation de l'activité de conception. Ma grande capacité à synthétiser les éléments et à travailler en équipe me permettra de m'intégrer facilement au sein de votre équipe pluridisciplinaire. Je suis également capable de piloter des activités de collecte et d'analyse d'événements en service, de certifier les évolutions de la définition en relation avec des experts techniques et avec l'Autorité de Certification. Je suis également très à l'aise avec la mise en place, la réalisation et l'évolution des Reconnaissances d'Aptitude à la Conception EMAR 21J permettant d'approuver les activités d'ingénierie de maintenance, de conception et de suivi de navigabilité. J'ai également une solide expérience en matière d'animation de réunions en français et en anglais. Enfin, je suis déterminée(e) à travailler dans un environnement complexe et à relever les défis en permanence. Ma curiosité, ma rigueur, mon autonomie et ma capacité à synthétiser les informations sont des atouts qu'il me faudra mettre en œuvre pour atteindre les objectifs que vous fixerez. Je souhaiterais vous rencontrer prochainement pour vous exposer de vive voix mes motivations et connaître les détails de l'offre en place. Je vous remercie pour votre attention et je reste disponible pour toute information supplémentaire. Cordialement, [Prénom et Nom]

question: Long-Only Value Investing: Size Doesn’t Matter! Please explain like I am a layperson: By Wesley Gray, PhD | Published On: June 15th, 2023 Categories: Research Insights, Factor Investing, Key Research, Value Investing Research Many factor investors are familiar with “small-cap value investing,” which is a reasonable allocation for long-term investors who can tolerate a lot of volatility. Why are there so many small-cap value investors? Small-cap value investors have been told that the value premium is higher, on average, in small stocks versus larger stocks. Unfortunately, this is not true if you are a long-only value investor.(1). Our own Jack Vogel recently published a paper called “Long-Only Value Investing: Does Size Matter?” which makes this point clear.(2) The fact large-cap value and small-cap value stocks earn similar returns may be shocking for investors who have been sold the idea that value investors have to invest in small-caps to capture the value premium. But we need to remember that data/evidence should drive decisions, not stories. A simple example will highlight the fragility of the result that small-cap value beats large-cap value. First, let’s look at a chart of equal-weight long-only portfolios sorted on book/market via the data from the paper.(3) The results are hypothetical results and are NOT an indicator of future results and do NOT represent returns that any investor actually attained. Indexes are unmanaged and do not reflect management or trading fees, and one cannot invest directly in an index. Key Result: Large-cap value stocks outperform small-cap value stocks on an absolute and risk-adjusted basis. Here are the detailed stats: The results are hypothetical results and are NOT an indicator of future results and do NOT represent returns that any investor actually attained. Indexes are unmanaged and do not reflect management or trading fees, and one cannot invest directly in an index. Wait a second! That can’t be true. All the research suggests value works better in small-caps. I tested it on Ken French’s website! Don’t worry, the date on Ken Fench’s website is correct, but the portfolios from that website are crafted in a different way… Below we look at the typical small-cap value and large-cap value chart, which compares value-weighted(4) large-cap and small-cap portfolios and looks at tercile sorts, not decile sorts. The results are hypothetical results and are NOT an indicator of future results and do NOT represent returns that any investor actually attained. Indexes are unmanaged and do not reflect management or trading fees, and one cannot invest directly in an index. Eureka! We can replicate the result generated from data on Ken French’s website. Here are the statistics: The results are hypothetical results and are NOT an indicator of future results and do NOT represent returns that any investor actually attained. Indexes are unmanaged and do not reflect management or trading fees, and one cannot invest directly in an index. What is the point of the exercise above? The point is that evidence-based investors want to invest on robust and reliable fact patterns, not results that can change dramatically via cherry-picked portfolio formations. Why are the portfolios above fragile? Simple: Size doesn’t matter when it comes to value investing. Valuation does. Let’s go for an intuitive example with low complexity. For example, if you can buy a portfolio with an average P/E of 5x and a market cap of $10B, this will, using historical datasets, outperform a portfolio with an average P/E of 8x and a market cap of $500mm. Why? Size doesn’t drive expected returns — valuation does.(5)(6) [/ref] The reason this result may be surprising to readers is that size and value investing have never really been explored in a simple-to-understand way for non-PhDs. Fortunately, Jack’s latest research paper solves this problem! Let’s dive into what I feel are the key points of Jack’s published paper. Point #1: Long-Only Value Investing is Different than Long-Short Value Investing As many readers know, academic research papers often study so-called zero investment long/short factor portfolios. But in the real world, most investors often don’t invest in these portfolio structures (outside of AQR and a few other providers)–they invest in long-only portfolios. Why does Jack bring this up? Well, many investors cite research that speaks to long/short portfolio analysis, and this analysis may not apply to their long-only portfolio decisions. This topic is addressed in more depth here. Bottom line: if you are investing in long-only factor portfolios, focus on research that studies long-only factor portfolios, not long-short factors. Point #2: Portfolio Formation Matters…a lot. At the outset of this post, we made it clear that how one forms a portfolio can significantly drive results. By manipulating several decision points — 1) equal-weight vs. value-weight and 2) decile vs. tercile sorts — we can tell a story that large-cap value dominates small-cap value, or we can tell a story that small-cap value dominates large-cap value (the story most often told). But the important thing to note is these are both “stories” because they cherry-pick aspects of the data to highlight a particular argument. Jack’s paper cuts through the stories told on size and value investing and conducts a robust study that looks at long-only portfolios with various valuation metrics, various portfolio formation techniques, and various geographies and sample time periods. Throughout the paper, Jack breaks the top 3000 largest companies into the biggest 1000 firms (“large caps”) and the next largest 2000 firms (“small caps”). This breakdown is done to reflect how practitioners think about the marketplace and should be more applicable to long-only investors than research that uses NYSE percentile breakpoints.(7) The breakdown of what percentage of the market resides in these respective buckets is in the chart below: In general, large caps represent the vast majority of the investment universe, but this varies over time. Important to note, that mega-caps, at times, can represent a large portion of a portfolio if the portfolio has “value-weight” construction versus equal-weight construction. Take a simple example. Let’s say you sort the universe of stocks on P/E and find Apple in your portfolio and then stock X, which has a $100 billion market cap — not exactly “small”.
