question: Make short post review for linkedin on this case Client A major European car manufacturer used Elinext to develop a B2B online payment system. Challenge The company used another developer to build a custom end-to-end payment application that would allow businesses to sell to customers online. For customers, it would be the same as paying via a card terminal in a store — but on the Internet. The application needed to process payment details safely and securely. The first version of the application lagged a lot and was difficult to use. The company decided to replace the developer team. They wanted a partner who could clear up the application’s architecture, make it more stable, and add new features. Someone in the company had already worked with Elinext and knew we had experience with building online payment software. So, we were referred to as a potential partner. We showed our expertise through several related case studies, and the company was convinced we knew what to do and we could execute as much. Process Our collaboration with the client was organized using the outstaffing model. This means we provided a team, and our team worked as a remote part of the client’s organization. We aligned the process with Agile methodology, using Jira to set up a workflow across four development environments with automatic deployments. The work was broken down into five one-week sprints, each of which was built around a particular phase: investigation, implementation, testing, bug fixing and delivery. In large part, the client planned the sprints on their own, consulting our lead developer. And the lead developer was instrumental to monitoring the progress through daily meetings, one with his team and one with the client. In addition to sprints, the entire project included four stages: refactoring, adding new features, developing version 2.0 and improving that version. And the most crucial of them was refactoring. Cleaning The original application we had to work with required quite a few improvements, especially its architecture: we had to rewrite it. We tackled the challenge by using domain-driven design (DDD). This approach allowed us to align the new architecture with the business’ needs and specifics. And the architecture we built as a result proved itself much cleaner, more stable and more load-resilient than the original. Six months from when we hopped on the project, the client had a clean, early version of the application. It included modules and entities that they and prospective businesses using the application could finally comprehend and work with. And no security risks or codebase issues were preventing further development. Taking It to the Next Level Once the application had a clean and efficient architecture, the client green-lighted further improvements. Over the following six months, we added new features and completed the first version of the application as it had been conceived. And we didn’t stop there. It took us one year to build the second version and a year-and-a-half to expand the application, enriching it with further features. Testing Throughout the development, we checked the software using various tests. But end-to-end (E2E) tests played the most important part by allowing us to monitor how new features performed. In the process, we applied a variety of tools to analyze the application and make sure features were delivered in a continuous, timely manner. Product Businesses can use the application to take payments online. Once it has been integrated with a company’s website or mobile app, our client will provide that company with a merchant account and a payment gateway. These will connect the customer’s bank or payment processor with that of the company. We enabled related data storage in DynamoDB, making it compliant with GDPR. The Widget A company can integrate the application with their website or mobile app by installing a widget. The widget supports payments in ten currencies, transferred via commonly used cards (e.g. Mastercard, Visa, Paypal) and custom solutions (e.g. Klarna, SEPA). We also enabled automated recurring payments. The system complies with Payment Card Industry (PCI) standards while not being required to follow the PCI Data Security Standard (DSS). What the widget looks like will depend on the company using it — you can easily customize its appearance. And it’s friendly to users speaking different languages. We set up a localization mechanism that automatically detects the user’s language, and presents the interface in one of ten languages available. We used Native.js with its event system to be managed by an internal state manager (e.g. Redux). This helped prevent potential integration conflicts. The Back End We used Amazon Web Services (AWS) to build the back-end application in the cloud so it can process more than two million requests daily. To streamline transactions, we used a set of technologies. Elastic Load Balancer automatically balances high loads, while Serverless Workflow Orchestrations is responsible for processing transactional mechanisms. Now, if a transaction fails, the payment value will automatically send funds back to the payment card or wallet. Failure reasons may include wrong request handling by third parties, lack of funds in case of automated recurring payments and others. We also applied lambdas for handling scheduled jobs and all possible events. Admin Portal To build the admin portal, we used React.js accompanied by Redux as a state manager and AWS Cognito as an authentication tool. The portal generates access tokens required for integrating the application with a company’s site or mobile app. Portal users can be assigned one of the three roles: Operator, Super Admin and Merchant. A Super Admin manages the application at all levels, assigning user roles, editing organization details, setting up default localizations and more. Operators can create business accounts, generate access tokens and manage a businesses localizations. Finally, Merchant accounts are reserved for businesses. They can manage their business details and use access tokens to integrate the widget with their site or mobile app. Results We completed the project on time, cleaning up the application’s architecture, adding new features and saving the client money by removing third-party tools. And the project overall had been instructive to us, as we improved our understanding of handling huge, highly-loaded payment systems. Today, the product is developing rapidly. And we are preparing for the next stage: refactoring the widget using React Framework.
reference: The collaboration between Elinext and a major European car manufacturer resulted in the creation of a B2B online payment system that enabled businesses to sell to customers online safely and securely. Elinext was referred to as a potential partner given their experience in building online payment software, and they did not disappoint. They used Agile methodology, Jira, and domain-driven design to organize the process, break down the work into sprints and improve the original architecture. Six months later, the company had a clean, early version of the application, and over the next year and a half, Elinext added new features and expanded it. The widget supports payments in ten currencies, is customizable, and operates in ten languages. The back-end application uses AWS technology and can already process over two million requests daily. Finally, the project improved their understanding of handling huge, highly-loaded payment systems, and resulted in savings for the client by removing third-party tools.

The purpose of implementing an ERP system is to integrate various business processes (including inventory management, accounting, sales, and human resources) into a single unified system. This system enhances efficiency, transparency, and data accuracy, which are essential for making informed decisions. For Toboggan Brewing Company, the following aspects should be considered in the comprehensive review: 1. **Microbrewery Inventory Management Best Practices**: - **Accurate Demand Forecasting**: Using historical sales data to forecast future demand and adjust inventory levels accordingly. - **Batch Tracking**: Ability to track ingredients and batches through the brewing process to manage quality and recall issues if needed. - **Seasonality Management**: Handling the ebb and flow of seasonal offerings by planning and adjusting inventory levels for raw materials and finished products. - **Supplier Management**: Developing strong relationships and agreements with suppliers for consistent supply and managing lead times effectively. 2. **Benchmarks**: - **Inventory Turnover Ratio**: Calculating how often inventory is sold and replaced over a certain period. A higher ratio indicates efficient inventory management. - **Carrying Cost of Inventory**: Understanding the total cost of holding inventory, including storage, insurance, and obsolescence. - **Order Accuracy**: Ensuring that orders are filled accurately, which speaks to effective inventory control. - **Days on Hand**: The number of days it takes to run out of stock, reflecting how well inventory matches demand. 3. **Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)**: - **Yield per Batch**: Amount of product produced per batch, indicating process efficiency. - **Waste Percentage**: The proportion of ingredients not converted to saleable product. - **Stockouts and Overstock**: Frequency of running out of stock or excess stock, indicating forecasting accuracy. - **Lead Time**: The time between placing an order and its delivery, which affects inventory restocking strategies. 4. **Types of ERP Systems for Microbrewery Industry**: - **Cloud-Based ERP**: Such systems offer on-demand access, lower upfront costs, and easy scalability which can be advantageous for a growing brewery. - **On-Premises ERP**: More traditional, this option might suit a brewery wanting full control over their system but involves higher initial investment and ongoing maintenance. - **Industry-Specific ERP**: There are ERP systems designed specifically for the brewing industry, with features tailored to its unique needs. - **Custom ERP Solutions**: Some breweries might consider building a custom ERP solution to meet their particular operational nuances. When selecting an ERP system, it's important for the Toboggan Brewing Company to consider factors such as cost, scalability, ease of use, customer support, and the ability of the system to integrate with existing software. Additionally, employee training and change management will be crucial for the successful implementation of a new ERP system.

question: Design Thinking in Action (C): Experimentation in Action at South Western Railway Covid-19 positive and negative impact on them.
reference: South Western Railway (SWR), like many other transportation companies, faced significant challenges and had to adapt rapidly due to the Covid-19 pandemic. To navigate through these uncertain times, SWR implemented design thinking principles and focused on experimentation to address both the positive and negative impacts of the pandemic on their operations. One positive impact was the decrease in passenger demand, which allowed SWR to experiment with new operational strategies. They used design thinking to identify opportunities to improve efficiency and customer experience. This led to the implementation of new contactless ticketing systems, allowing passengers to use mobile apps or smart cards to travel. This not only reduced the necessity for physical handling of tickets but also streamlined the boarding process and reduced queues, further enhancing passenger safety and satisfaction. Additionally, SWR experimented with different seating configurations and train layouts to maximize social distancing guidelines. Through iterative prototyping and feedback loops, they developed solutions that optimized available space while maintaining passenger comfort. By leveraging design thinking, SWR was able to quickly adapt to changing government regulations and ensure the safety of passengers. On the flip side, the pandemic also had negative impacts on SWR, such as reduced revenue and financial strain. Design thinking was crucial in identifying creative solutions to mitigate these challenges. SWR experimented with alternative revenue streams, such as repurposing train carriages for cargo transportation. By partnering with logistics companies, they were able to offset some of the revenue losses from reduced passenger demand. Furthermore, SWR utilized design thinking to explore cost-saving measures without compromising safety or service quality. They experimented with lean practices and process optimizations, identifying areas where resources could be allocated more effectively. This allowed them to reduce operational costs and ensure the financial viability of the company. Overall, design thinking and experimentation played a pivotal role in helping SWR navigate the positive and negative impacts of the Covid-19 pandemic. By adopting a human-centered approach, they were able to identify and address passenger needs, optimize operations, and find innovative solutions to financial challenges. These efforts not only helped SWR survive during the pandemic but also positioned them for future success in a rapidly evolving transportation landscape.

It is a leading manufacturer and supplier of petrochemical products, specializing in the production of a wide range of unsaturated polyester resins (UPR) and vinyl ester resins (VER). The company was established in 1993 as a joint venture between Japan’s Mitsubishi Corporation and Malaysia's PETRONAS Chemicals Group Berhad. With the support of advanced technology and expertise from Mitsubishi Corporation, PrefChem Johor has become one of the key players in the petrochemical industry in Malaysia. PrefChem Johor operates a state-of-the-art manufacturing facility located in Pasir Gudang, Johor. The facility is equipped with advanced production technologies and adheres to stringent quality control measures to ensure the production of high-quality resins. The company has a production capacity of over 50,000 metric tons per year. The primary products manufactured by PrefChem Johor are unsaturated polyester resins (UPR) and vinyl ester resins (VER). These resins are widely used in various industries such as automotive, construction, electrical, and marine. UPRs are commonly used in the production of fiberglass-reinforced plastics (FRP), while VERs are known for their high heat resistance and chemical resistance. PrefChem Johor is committed to delivering products that meet the highest quality standards. The company emphasizes research and development activities to continuously improve and develop new products to meet the evolving needs of its customers. Additionally, the company prioritizes environmental sustainability and operates in compliance with all relevant environmental regulations. Overall, PrefChem Johor is known for its expertise in petrochemical manufacturing and its commitment to delivering high-quality products. Its partnership with Mitsubishi Corporation and PETRONAS Chemicals Group Berhad has contributed significantly to its success in the industry.

PRefChem was formed primarily to develop, construct, and operate the Pengerang Integrated Complex (PIC) located in Pengerang, Johor, Malaysia. The PIC is a significant downstream oil and gas project that comprises two main components: the Refinery and the Petrochemical Integrated Development (RAPID) complex. The Refinery has a capacity of 300,000 barrels per day and processes a variety of crude oils to produce refined petroleum products such as gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel. On the other hand, the Petrochemical complex is designed to produce a wide range of petrochemical products, including polymers, glycols, synthetic rubber, and specialty chemicals. It has a production capacity of 3.3 million metric tonnes per year. This complex aims to strengthen Malaysia's position in the global petrochemical market and cater to the growing demand for these products in the region. The Pengerang Integrated Complex is strategically located in the southern part of Malaysia, near major shipping routes and close to regional markets. It is also supported by world-class infrastructure, including deepwater harbors, storage facilities, and pipelines for efficient transportation. PRefChem is committed to operating the PIC in an environmentally sustainable manner. It adheres to stringent safety and environmental standards, ensuring compliance with international regulations and best practices. The company focuses on minimizing its environmental impact, implementing effective waste management systems, and promoting resource conservation. The establishment of PRefChem and the development of the Pengerang Integrated Complex has brought significant economic benefits to Johor and Malaysia as a whole. It has created numerous job opportunities, attracted foreign investments, and contributed to the growth of the local economy. In summary, Pengerang Refining and Petrochemical (PRefChem) is a joint venture between PETRONAS and Saudi Aramco. It operates the Pengerang Integrated Complex, which consists of a Refinery and Petrochemical Integrated Development (RAPID) complex. PRefChem aims to produce refined petroleum products and a variety of petrochemicals while ensuring environmental sustainability and economic growth for Malaysia.

reference: I am thrilled to share with you our two distinct phases of product development - EVT (Engineering Validation Testing) and DVT (Design Validation Testing). These phases play a crucial role in ensuring that our products meet the highest standards of quality, functionality, and reliability. First, let's discuss the EVT phase. During this phase, our team, led by A, takes charge of bringing BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) and BMC (Baseboard Management Controller) to the table. Their primary focus is to validate the hardware functions and ensure that everything works seamlessly together. A's expertise in BIOS and BMC allows them to thoroughly test and fine-tune the hardware, ultimately paving the way for the successful execution of upcoming phases. Once the EVT phase is completed, we transition into the DVT phase. Here, the responsibility of BIOS and BMC development shifts to B, our skilled team member. B utilizes their extensive knowledge and experience to develop and enhance the BIOS and BMC systems. They work closely with the hardware team to refine these crucial components, ensuring optimal performance and compatibility. B's expertise and dedication contribute significantly to the success of our product design and validation. By dividing the responsibilities between EVT and DVT phases, we can streamline the development process and achieve the best possible outcomes. This division allows us to have a dedicated focus on hardware validation during EVT and a specialized approach to BIOS and BMC development in DVT. It also provides an opportunity for thorough testing and feedback incorporation, ensuring that the final product meets or exceeds our customers' expectations. question: Big Companies Are Embracing Analytics, But Most Still Don’t Have a Data-Driven Culture by Thomas H. Davenport and Randy Bean For six consecutive years NewVantage Partners has conducted an annual survey on how executives in large corporations view data. This year, results show nearly every firm is investing in some form of analytics, and most are seeing value. But only one-third say they have succeeded in creating a data-driven culture. And many fear disruption by firms better equipped to use AI. Almost four in five respondents said they feared disruption or displacement from firms like those in the fintech sector or firms specializing in big data. The technology judged most disruptive is AI — by far. Seventy-two percent chose it as the disruptive technology with the most impact — far more than cloud computing (13%) or blockchain (7%). For six consecutive years NewVantage Partners has conducted an annual survey on how executives in large corporations view data. Each year the response rate increases, and the reported urgency of making effective use of data increases as well. This year the results are both more encouraging and more worrisome than in the past. Six years ago, the primary focus of questions and answers in the survey was big data, which was relatively new on the business scene. In the 2018 survey, the primary attention has moved to artificial intelligence. AI is now a well-established focus at these large, sophisticated firms. There is both a stronger feeling that big data and AI projects deliver value and a greater concern that established firms will be disrupted by startups. The survey includes senior executives from 57 large corporations. The industry group with the most firms represented in the survey is one of the most data-intensive: financial services. Companies from the life sciences, manufacturing, telecom, and online industries also participated. The actual respondents are changing somewhat from the first surveys: It has always involved a high proportion of C-level executives responsible for data, but this year chief data officers are 56% of the respondents, up from 32% last year. Only 12% of firms in the 2012 survey had even appointed a chief data officer. While AI gets the headlines here and elsewhere in the world, the survey addresses both big data and AI. Terminology comes and goes, but the constant is a data explosion and the need to make sense of it. Big data and AI projects have become virtually indistinguishable, particularly given that machine learning is one of the most popular techniques for dealing with large volumes of fast-moving data. It’s also the case that statistical approaches to AI — deep learning, for example — are increasingly popular. Therefore, we view traditional data analytics, big data, and AI as being on a continuum. Virtually all of the respondents (97%) say they are investing in these types of projects. Perhaps the best news in this survey is that companies continue to believe they are getting value from their big data and AI projects. 73% of respondents said they have already received measurable value from these initiatives. That number is half again higher than in the 2017 survey, which suggests that more value is being achieved as companies grow familiar with the technologies. The types of value received are perhaps consistent with other previous types of technology. Consistent with our view that big data and AI are extensions of analytical capabilities, the most common objectives — and those most likely to achieve success — are “advanced analytics/better decisions.” Thirty-six percent had that as their top priority, and 69% of those had already achieved success with the objective. Better customer service and expense reduction are also common objectives. Just over one-quarter of firms (27%) are pursuing some combination of innovation and disruption, speed to market, or data monetization initiatives. Data monetization programs had the lowest priority and the lowest percentage of success (27%). One of the greatest issues for concern in the survey for large enterprises is the risk of disruption from new entrants. Almost four in five respondents said they feared disruption or displacement from firms like those in the fintech sector or firms specializing in big data. The technology judged most disruptive is AI — by far. Seventy-two percent chose it as the disruptive technology with the most impact — far more than cloud computing (13%) or blockchain (7%). Another important and continuing issue is the slow speed with which these established firms make the shift to a data-driven culture. Virtually all respondents (99%) say their firms are trying to move in that direction, but only about one-third have succeeded at this objective. This gap appears every year in the surveys, and the level of success hasn’t improved much over time. Clearly firms need more-concerted programs to achieve data-related cultural change. Many startups have created data-driven cultures from their beginning, which is a key reason why large, established firms fear disruption from them. One of the approaches that firms have established to deal with data-driven disruption and change is to establish new management roles. However, there is still a lack of clarity about how different data-oriented roles (chief information officer, chief data officer, chief digital officer, chief analytics officer, etc.) relate to each other. With respect to the chief data officer role, there is substantial disagreement about the major responsibilities of the role and what types of backgrounds are appropriate for CDO jobs. Thirty-nine percent say their CDO has primary responsibility for data strategy and results, but 37% assign that responsibility to other C-level executives, and 24% say there is no single point of accountability for it. In terms of backgrounds, 34% of respondents believe the CDO should be a change agent from outside the company, while 32% believe the person should be a company veteran from inside the firm. Role clarity in senior data-related roles is critical for both leading AI/big data projects and accomplishing cultural change. And while all respondents believed it important, the majority of firms still lack an enterprise data strategy. This continuing rise in the importance and challenges of big data is one of the most important features of contemporary economy and society. The survey results over time provide interesting and useful documentation of this revolution. The rise of AI is only exacerbating this trend. The keys to success are to determine how your firm should respond, assign clear responsibilities for data strategy and results, and then move ahead to execute the needed changes in a systematic and effective fashion. 翻译成中文
reference: 大公司正在采纳数据分析，但大多数仍未形成数据驱动的文化 托马斯·H·达文波特和兰迪·比恩著 六年来，NewVantage Partners连续进行了关于大型企业高管如何看待数据的年度调查。今年的结果显示，几乎每家公司都在某种形式的数据分析上有所投入，大多数公司认为数据分析很有价值。但只有三分之一的公司表示他们成功地创建了一个数据驱动的文化。许多人担心，那些更擅长使用人工智能的公司会对他们造成颠覆。近五分之四的受访者表示，他们担心会被金融科技领域的公司或专注于大数据的公司颠覆或取代。被认为最具颠覆性的技术是人工智能——远远领先。72%的人选择它作为最具影响力的颠覆技术——远远超过云计算（13%）或区块链（7%）。六年来，NewVantage Partners每年都在进行这项调查，每年的响应率都在增加，对有效使用数据的紧迫性也在增加。今年的结果比以往既更令人鼓舞又更令人担忧。 六年前，调查中的主要问题和回答集中在大数据上，这对商业界来说是相对较新的领域。在2018年的调查中，主要的注意力已转移到人工智能上。人工智能现在已经成为这些大型、成熟公司的一个重要焦点。人们越来越觉得大数据和AI项目能够提供价值，并且越来越担心成熟的公司会被初创公司颠覆。 这项调查包括了来自57家大型公司的高级执行官。在调查中代表最多的行业群体之一是最注重数据的：金融服务业。生命科学、制造业、电信和在线行业的公司也参与了调查。实际回应者在从第一次调查至今有所变化：它一直涉及负责数据的C级高管的高比例，但今年的首席数据官占了回应者的56%，而去年是32%。2012年的调查中，只有12%的公司任命了首席数据官。 虽然人工智能在这里和世界其他地方都占据了头条，但调查既包括大数据也包括人工智能。术语来来去去，但不变的是数据爆炸和理解这些数据的需求。大数据和AI项目已经变得几乎无法区分，特别是考虑到机器学习是处理大量快速移动数据的最受欢迎的技术之一。统计方法对于AI也越来越受欢迎——例如深度学习。因此，我们认为传统数据分析、大数据和人工智能处于一个连续体上。几乎所有的受访者（97%）都表示他们正在这些类型的项目上投资。 调查中最好的消息是，公司继续相信他们从大数据和人工智能项目中获得了价值。73%的受访者表示，他们已经从这些计划中获得了可衡量的价值。这个数字比2017年调查中的数字高出了一半，这表明随着公司对技术的熟悉，获得的价值在增加。 获得的价值类型或许与其他以前的技术类型一致。与我们认为大数据和人工智能是分析能力扩展的观点一致，最普遍的目标——也是最有可能成功的目标——是“高级分析/更好的决策”。36%的人将其作为他们的首要任务，其中69%的人已经成功实现了这个目标。更好的客户服务和费用减少也是常见的目标。略超过四分之一的公司（27%）正在追求某种结合创新和颠覆、市场速度或数据货币化计划的目标。数据货币化项目的优先级最低，成功百分比也最低（27%）。 对于大型企业来说，调查中最大的担忧之一是来自新进入者的颠覆风险。近五分之四的受访者表示，他们担心会被金融科技领域的公司或专注于大数据的公司颠覆或取代。被认为最具颠覆性的技术是AI——远远领先。72%的人选择它作为最具影响力的颠覆技术——远远超过云计算（13%）或区块链（7%）。 另一个重要且持续的问题是这些成立公司以多快的速度转型为数据驱动的文化。几乎所有的回应者（99%）都表示他们的公司正试图朝这个方向转型，但是只有大约三分之一成功实现了这个目标。每年的调查中都会出现这个差距，而且随着时间的推移，成功的水平并没有多大提高。显然，公司需要更加集中的项目来实现与数据相关的文化变革。许多初创公司从一开始就创建了数据驱动的文化，这是大型成熟公司害怕被它们颠覆的一个主要原因。 公司建立新的管理角色是处理数据驱动的颠覆和变革的方法之一。然而，不同的数据导向角色（首席信息官、首席数据官、首席数字官、首席分析官等）之间的关系仍然缺乏清晰性。 关于首席数据官角色，对于这个角色的主要职责以及CDO职位适合什么样的背景存在显著分歧。39%的人表示他们的CDO主要负责数据战略和结果，但有37%的人将这一责任分配给其他C级高管，还有24%的人表示没有一个单一的责任点对其负责。在背景方面，34%的回应者认为CDO应该是来自公司外部的变革推动者，而32%的人认为这个人应该是来自公司内部的企业老手。对于高层数据相关角色的角色清晰度对于领导AI/大数据项目和实现文化变革都至关重要。尽管所有的回应者都认为这一点很重要，但大多数公司仍然缺乏一个企业数据战略。 大数据的重要性和挑战的持续上升是当代经济和社会最重要的特征之一。随着时间的推移，调查结果提供了这场革命的有趣和有用的记录。人工智能的崛起只是加剧了这一趋势。成功的关键是确定你的公司应该如何应对，明确分配数据战略和结果的责任，然后着手以系统和有效的方式实施所需的改变。

That number is half again higher than in the 2017 survey, which suggests that more value is being achieved as companies grow familiar with the technologies. The types of value received are perhaps consistent with other previous types of technology. Consistent with our view that big data and AI are extensions of analytical capabilities, the most common objectives — and those most likely to achieve success — are “advanced analytics/better decisions.” Thirty-six percent had that as their top priority, and 69% of those had already achieved success with the objective. Better customer service and expense reduction are also common objectives. Just over one-quarter of firms (27%) are pursuing some combination of innovation and disruption, speed to market, or data monetization initiatives. Data monetization programs had the lowest priority and the lowest percentage of success (27%). One of the greatest issues for concern in the survey for large enterprises is the risk of disruption from new entrants. Almost four in five respondents said they feared disruption or displacement from firms like those in the fintech sector or firms specializing in big data. The technology judged most disruptive is AI — by far. Seventy-two percent chose it as the disruptive technology with the most impact — far more than cloud computing (13%) or blockchain (7%). Another important and continuing issue is the slow speed with which these established firms make the shift to a data-driven culture. Virtually all respondents (99%) say their firms are trying to move in that direction, but only about one-third have succeeded at this objective. This gap appears every year in the surveys, and the level of success hasn’t improved much over time. Clearly firms need more-concerted programs to achieve data-related cultural change. Many startups have created data-driven cultures from their beginning, which is a key reason why large, established firms fear disruption from them. One of the approaches that firms have established to deal with data-driven disruption and change is to establish new management roles. However, there is still a lack of clarity about how different data-oriented roles (chief information officer, chief data officer, chief digital officer, chief analytics officer, etc.) relate to each other. With respect to the chief data officer role, there is substantial disagreement about the major responsibilities of the role and what types of backgrounds are appropriate for CDO jobs. Thirty-nine percent say their CDO has primary responsibility for data strategy and results, but 37% assign that responsibility to other C-level executives, and 24% say there is no single point of accountability for it. In terms of backgrounds, 34% of respondents believe the CDO should be a change agent from outside the company, while 32% believe the person should be a company veteran from inside the firm. Role clarity in senior data-related roles is critical for both leading AI/big data projects and accomplishing cultural change. And while all respondents believed it important, the majority of firms still lack an enterprise data strategy. This continuing rise in the importance and challenges of big data is one of the most important features of contemporary economy and society. The survey results over time provide interesting and useful documentation of this revolution. The rise of AI is only exacerbating this trend. The keys to success are to determine how your firm should respond, assign clear responsibilities for data strategy and results, and then move ahead to execute the needed changes in a systematic and effective fashion.

question: "Sarah: I think you need a reality check, don't you think it's time to do an actual research? Beverly: No! You're hitting too close to home!" Explain please and make it a detailed explanation with the structure, fragments, components of the sentences
reference: The conversation between Sarah and Beverly is centered around a moment where Sarah is suggesting (perhaps critically) that Beverly should consider doing "actual research," implying that Beverly might not have been thorough or accurate in her previous efforts, if any. Beverly's response indicates that Sarah's comment has touched on a sensitive subject or area of personal insecurity. Let's break down the conversation component by component: 1. **Sarah: "I think you need a reality check, don't you think it's time to do an actual research?"** - **"I think you need a reality check,"** is the first clause of Sarah's sentence, serving as an independent clause. It suggests that Sarah believes Beverly needs to reassess her perspective or understanding of the situation. The phrase "reality check" implies that Beverly's current view is distorted or not based on facts. - **"don't you think it's time to do an actual research?"** This part is a tag question, which typically follows a statement to invite confirmation or denial from the listener. The structure consists of the negated auxiliary verb "don't," the subject "you," the verb "think," and the infinitive phrase "it's time to do an actual research." The phrase "actual research" emphasizes the need for genuine, thorough investigation. Note that in standard English, "research" is an uncountable noun, so the more grammatically correct phrase would be "to do actual research" without the article "an." 2. **Beverly: "No! You're hitting too close to home!"** - **"No!"** Beverly begins with a strong, definitive negation, rejecting Sarah's suggestion or implication outright. - **"You're hitting too close to home!"** This is an idiomatic expression used to convey that someone's words or actions have touched upon something very personal, sensitive, or discomforting to the listener -- in this case, Beverly. Here, "You're" is a contraction of "you are," forming the present continuous tense with the verb "hitting." The phrase "too close to home" is figuratively used to mean the comments or actions are affecting a matter that is intimately personal or sensitive. - The entire sentence is notable for its exclamation mark, indicating strong emotion or surprise. From a structural perspective, both parts of the conversation are composed of complex sentences that convey nuanced feelings and suggestions. Sarah's sentence suggests a corrective action, while Beverly's response illustrates personal affront or vulnerability. This interaction encapsulates a moment of conflict or tension where advice is perceived not as helpful guidance but as a critical or painful reminder of a personal issue or failure.

reference: Title: The Dilapidated Remnants of Riki Published on 13th March 2013 Glasgow, Scotland - The once iconic Riki store on Sauchiehall Street continues to deteriorate, with the dilapidated building now a haunt for vandals and a bittersweet reminder of a beloved children's shop. The image of a crying Krash the Rabbit, once a symbol of joy and adventure, is left untouched on a faded sign that greets passersby. Since its closure in 2007, the former Riki store has become a shadow of its former self. Windows are shattered, and graffiti covers the walls, a somber reflection of the changing retail landscape. The closure of Riki was a blow to many, as the shop held a special place in the hearts of both children and adults alike. Despite its abandoned state, the remnants of Riki are not forgotten. The CITV channel continues to air the KikoRiki cartoon, providing a nostalgic link to the store's heyday. The cartoon has managed to withstand programming changes, remaining a firm favorite with millions of viewers. Local residents and fans of the show have expressed their sadness at the state of the former store, with one passerby commenting, "It's such a shame to see the place like this. Riki brought joy to so many people, and now it's just a shell of its former self." Efforts to repurpose the space that once housed Riki have been met with opposition. Plans to create a new studio for CITV's Toonattik show were rejected due to concerns from local broadcaster STV, who feared that the move would contribute to the marginalized presence of Scottish media. As a result, the building remains in a state of decay, a stark reminder of lost opportunities. The closure of Riki and the decline of its physical presence have sparked nostalgia among the community. Many are left wondering if there will ever be another shop as unique and beloved as Riki, where children could immerse themselves in the whimsical world of KikoRiki. As the years pass, the memories of Riki and the joy it brought continue to fade. Yet, the image of Krash the Rabbit shedding tears remains as a poignant reminder of a time when laughter and play filled the very walls that now stand deserted. Although Riki may be forgotten by many, its impact on the Glasgow community still lingers, stirring emotions of loss and nostalgia for a beloved children's shop that brought such delight and happiness.

A computational integrative approach was proposed here to tackle the problem by integrating Hi-C data with other genomic data. A novel hyperparameter tuning method facilitating network clustering is developed to identify valid intra-chromosomal communities at different interaction resolutions. The approach was first trained on Hi-C data and other epigenetic data in an untreated and one hour estrogen (E2)- treated tamoxifen-sensitive (TS) breast cancer cell line, MCF7, and revealed two major types of valid intra-chromosomal communities - active/repressive compartments, respectively, which resembles the properties of open/closed chromatin domains. It was further tested on MCF7 and tamoxifen-resistant (TR) breast cancer cell line, MCF7TR, and identified 515 differential interacting and differentially expressed genes (DIEGs) within intra-chromosomal community interactions. Further analysis of these DIEGs revealed that endocrine resistance is among the top biological pathways, suggesting a looping-mediated mechanism in regulating breast cancer tamoxifen resistance. This novel computational approach may have a broader application in many other biological systems for identifying a biological-specific differential community interaction. 3 Introduction Over the past decade, the advancement of both genomic profiling and computational analysis has revolutionized the field of three-dimensional (3D) chromatin architecture[1-7]. The human genome is now understood to function as a complex hierarchy of folded high-order chromatin units, such as chromosomal territories, compartments, topologically associating domains (TADs), and chromatin loops[5, 8]. Chromatin or DNA looping is recognized as one of the basic principles of gene regulation[9, 10]. We and others have demonstrated that although chromatin interaction domains are conserved at one Mb size among different cell types, hundreds of Kb-size subdomains are usually diverse and dynamically changed[11-15]. These highly dynamically changed domains may underlie mechanistic and functional consequences, and computationally identified looping genes can be used as prognostic signatures for measuring the outcome of the endocrine treatment[16]. Current computational methods still mainly focus on constructing or inferring global topological domains and detecting long-range interacting loops[16-21]. However, many challenges, especially in the aspect of computational modeling and analysis remain. For example, how to computationally integrate Hi-C data with many other epigenetic modification data to classify cell type-specific intra-chromosomal community interactions from multiple cell types or at different time points upon an environmental or cellular stimulus? What are the resulted biological functions associated with differential intra-chromosomal community interactions between cell types? Despite many computational tools for processing Hi-C data, no computational tools are currently available for systematically integrating Hi-C data with epigenetic modification data from multiple cell types or at different time points upon an environmental or cellular stimulus. In this study, we will develop an integrative data analysis approach for investigating intra- chromosomal community interactions (Figure 1), which includes 1) constructing genomic 4 feature matrices by mapping multi-omics datasets to adjacency matrices obtained from Hi-C data, 2) identifying valid community structures based on both the network clustering and the optimized parameter determination methods, 3) evaluating enrichment of genomic features in intra-chromosomal community interaction with a permutation test, and 4) screening for significant gene loci and corresponding sub-network by comparing genomic and network topological features through differential intra-chromosomal community interaction analysis. Finally, we apply the computational approach on an ERα+ breast cancer model system, i.e., untreated tamoxifen-sensitive (TS) cell line MCF7, one hour estrogen (E2)-treated MCF7 cell line, as well as tamoxifen-resistant (TR) cell line MCF7TR. Our goal is to identify distinct types of TS- and TR-intra-chromosomal community interactions and to gain insights into the functional role of these TR-intra-chromosomal community interactions in contributing to breast cancer tamoxifen resistance. Moreover, we anticipate that applying and validating our novel bioinformatics tools in an ERα+ breast cancer model system will make it broader application in many other biological systems for identifying a biological-specific differential community interaction. Material and Methods Multi-omics Data Hi-C data in untreated and one hour of E2-treated MCF7 cells, and MCF7TR cells were obtained from our previous publication[11]. Preprocessing of raw Hi-C data was performed by HiCUP[22] (e.g., map reads to HG19 human reference genome et al). Aligned BAM files of Hi-C experiments were further processed by either in-house python scripts (e.g., normalization[23] and transformation of Hi-C interaction data to Z-scores[24]) or HOMER[25] for selecting significant chromosomal interactions. Then, intra-chromosomal interactions were studied in 500 kb, 100kb, and 50kb resolution, respectively. Microarray expression profiles of 5 genes in zero and one hour of E2 treated MCF7 cells, as well as RNA-Seq data in tamoxifen- resistant MCF7TR cells were retrieved from earlier paper[26, 27], which were quantile normalized[28] before transforming them to Z-scores. ChIP-Seq experiments of markers for enhancer (H3K27ac and H3K4me1), promoter (H3K4me3), repressor (H3K27me3 and H3K9me3), nucleosome density (DNase-seq and ATAC-Seq), and insulator (CTCF) in the same MCF7 cells were downloaded from published work[11, 27] and ENCODE project[29]. Preprocessing of these ChIP-Seq and ATAC-Seq experiments was done similarly as published works[11, 24, 30]: for example, raw reads were mapped to HG19 human reference genome by bowtie2[31], narrow (e.g., in CTCF, H3K27ac and H3K4me3) and broad (e.g., DNase, H3K27me3, H3K4me1 and H3K9me3) peaks were called by MACS2[32], and problematic regions for high throughput sequencing in human genome were removed according to ENCODE Black List[33]. Then, BEDTools[34] were used to estimate the read counts in a 200 bp window size for called peaks which were quantile normalized across all markers[35] before log-transforming and converting them to Z-scores. Building adjacency matrices with predefined resolution for Hi-C interactions If a chromosome length is L (e.g., 22 human chromosomes and an X chromosome), then the number of window bins 𝑛 𝑏 𝑖𝑛 of this chromosome based on a predefined window bin size or interaction resolution (e.g., bin=500kb) is 𝑛 𝑏 𝑖𝑛 = ⌈ 𝐿 𝑏 𝑖𝑛⌉, where ⌈𝑥⌉ is a ceiling function, returning an integer greater than or equal to 𝑥 . Then, the i-th interval (or window bin) of a chromosome is 𝑤 𝑖 : [(𝑖 − 1) ∙ 𝑏 𝑖𝑛, min(𝑖 ∙ 𝑏 𝑖𝑛, 𝐿)), 𝑖 ∈ {1,2, ⋯ , 𝑛 𝑏 𝑖𝑛 }. 6 For a set of 𝐻 (ℎ 1 , ⋯ , ℎ 𝐾 ) 𝑇 with K Hi-C intra-chromosomal interactions (e.g., significant interactions identified by HOMER), each pair of interactions ℎ 𝑘 (𝑥 𝑘 , 𝑦 𝑘 ) will be mapped to a pair of window bins ℎ 𝑘 (𝑥 𝑘 , 𝑦 𝑘 ) → 𝑤 𝑖𝑗 (𝑤 𝑖 , 𝑤 𝑗 ), where 𝑥 𝑘 and 𝑦 𝑘 are the positions of a pair of Hi-C interactions in intervals (or window bins) 𝑤 𝑖 and 𝑤 𝑗 , respectively, and 𝑤 𝑖𝑗 is an interaction between window 𝑤 𝑖 and 𝑤 𝑗 . Thus, some 𝑤 𝑖𝑗 might contain several pairs of Hi-C interactions while others might have none. Subsequently, an adjacency matrix A for intra-chromosomal interactions can be obtained 𝐴 𝑖𝑗 = Ι {𝑤 𝑖𝑗 ∪ 𝑤 𝑗𝑖 ≠∅} , 𝑖, 𝑗 ∈ {1,2, ⋯ , 𝑛 𝑏 𝑖𝑛 }, where 𝐴 𝑖𝑗 = 1 if the union ( ∪ ) of 𝑤 𝑖𝑗 and 𝑤 𝑗𝑖 is not empty ( ∅ ), otherwise 𝐴 𝑖𝑗 = 0 . In this way, intra-chromosomal Hi-C interactions are transformed to a binary adjacency matrix A with 𝐴 𝑖𝑗 = 𝐴 𝑗𝑖 . Here, if different window bin sizes (e.g., bin size = 500kb, 100kb, or 50kb) are used to map Hi-C interactions, then intra-chromosomal interaction networks with different resolutions will be obtained. Generating genomic feature matrices based on multi-omics data for Hi-C interactions First, Z-scores of intra-chromosomal interactions obtained from Hi-C data are mapped to the aforementioned adjacency matrix (e.g., bin size=500kb), as the edge weights of intra- chromosomal interactions (e.g., 22 human chromosomes and an X chromosome) for untreated, one hours E2-treated MCF7 cells, and MCF7TR cells, respectively. Then, genomic features (e.g., nucleosome density, histone modifications, and gene expressions) are mapped to the same adjacency matrix for generating genomic feature matrices, respectively. For example, 𝐻 (𝑔) (ℎ 1(𝑔) , ⋯ , ℎ 𝑀(𝑔) ) 𝑇 is genomic feature g with M data points, where each ℎ 𝑚(𝑔) (𝑥 𝑚 , 𝑧 𝑚 ) contains position information 𝑥 𝑚 and Z-score 𝑧 𝑚 of feature g in the loci. For a set of genomic features 𝑊 𝑖 in a window bin 𝑤 𝑖 7 𝑊 𝑖 = {𝑧 𝑚 |𝑥 𝑚 ∩ 𝑤 𝑖 ≠ ∅, 𝑚 ∈ {1,2, ⋯ , 𝑀 }}, if loci 𝑥 𝑚 intersects with bin 𝑤 𝑖 (e.g., 𝑥 𝑚 ∩ 𝑤 𝑖 ≠ ∅ ), then feature 𝑧 𝑚 will be included in this bin. Otherwise, the feature 𝑧 𝑚 will not be considered because loci 𝑥 𝑚 is not in bin 𝑤 𝑖 (e.g., 𝑥 𝑚 ∩ 𝑤 𝑖 = ∅ ). Since there may be multiple (or none) 𝑧 𝑚 in the same bin 𝑤 𝑖 , a genomic feature Z-score for the bin 𝑤 𝑖 is 𝑍 𝑖 = {𝑊 𝑖 ̅̅̅, 𝑊𝑖 ≠ ∅ 0, 𝑊𝑖 = ∅ . where 𝑊 𝑖 ̅̅̅ is the mean of these 𝑧 𝑚 . Subsequently, a feature matrix 𝐹 (𝑔) can be built for each genomic feature g based on the adjacency matrix A of Hi-C intra-chromosomal interactions. For instance, if there is an interaction between the window bins 𝑤 𝑖 and 𝑤 𝑗 (e.g., 𝐴 𝑖𝑗 = 1 ), then an edge weight 𝐹 𝑖𝑗(𝑔) of the interaction 𝑤 𝑖𝑗 at feature matrix F is assigned by equation 𝐹 𝑖𝑗(𝑔) = max(0, 𝑍 𝑖 + 𝑍 𝑗 ) It indicates the edge weight of feature matrix 𝐹 (𝑔) is determined by the Z-scores of a pair of interacting bins (e.g., 𝑤 𝑖 and 𝑤 𝑗 ). Such edge weight assignment (e.g., a weighted edge approach) for a network graph is adopted from a previous work [36], which is used here to build genomic feature matrices 𝐹 (𝑔) for adjacency matrix A. In order words, if there is an interaction in A, then the available genomic features will be considered correspondingly for building genomic features matrices 𝐹 (𝑔) . After converting multi-omics datasets 𝐻 (𝑔) to genomic feature matrices 𝐹 (𝑔) , based on the intra-chromosomal interactions A derived from Hi-C experiments (e.g., in untreated, one hours E2-treated MCF7 cells, and MCF7TR cells, respectively), information from diverse sources is comparable and integrable through the intra- chromosomal interactions. Identifying significant intra-chromosomal interactions from Hi-C interactions 8 For removing unreliable or biased intra-chromosomal interactions from Hi-C data, two approaches are used to screen significant chromosomal interactions. One is the filtering of the weakest 0, 5, 10, 20, or 60 percentages of intra-chromosomal interactions from observed Hi-C interactions. And the other is applying HOMER[25] directly on the aligned BAM files of Hi- C data, to obtain significant interacting fragments[37] such as using “makeTagDirectory” and “analyzeHiC” with significant P-value < 0.1. The screened significant intra-chromosomal interactions are converted to adjacency matrices A (or intra-chromosomal interaction matrices) with a predefined window bin size. Both filtering approaches were applied for screening observed intra-chromosomal interactions (e.g., window bin size=500kb) in untreated and one hours E2-treated MCF7 cells, respectively. The aim is to evaluate the robustness of predicted intra-chromosomal community interactions (e.g., the network modularity scores, the number of network edges, and the number of valid communities or network clusters) based on different filtering criteria. Since identified significant chromosomal interactions (e.g., adjacency matrices of intra- chromosomal interactions) at different interaction resolutions (e.g., window bin size = 500kb, 100kb, or 50kb) are frequently affected by the program parameters (e.g., HOMER), it is essential to find a solution for selecting optimal parameters accordingly. Though a higher interaction resolution (or a smaller window bin size) may yield more accurate network structure, it cannot be increased infinitely. For instance, the significant interactions identified by HOMER are dependent on two major parameters: window resolution – bin size, and its super resolution – range of signal averaging. To find optimal parameters for identifying significant intra-chromosomal interactions by HOMER, a new approach is designed to evaluate the associations between the number of identified interactions and the distance of interactions, when different window bin sizes are used in analysis. This new statistical method can minimize 9 the impact of window bin sizes (e.g., bin=500kb, 100b, or 50kb) on building adjacency matrices, when applying HOMER on Hi-C interactions. In the end, the significant intra- chromosomal interactions identified by HOMER with optimized parameters will be used further in differential network analysis. Predicting intra-chromosomal community interactions Applying modularity function to find communities in intra-chromosomal interaction network An intra-chromosomal interaction matrix from Hi-C experiments is represented by an adjacency matrix in graph theory, where intra-chromosomal interactions are treated as an undirected network. It is interesting to see whether there are intra-chromosomal community interactions in the network or not. For example, a smart local moving (SLM) algorithm [38] can be applied on the Hi-C intra-chromosomal interactions (e.g., an adjacency matrix), to find community structure of intra-chromosomal interactions. The SLM method is based on a modularity function [39] for detecting communities in a large network. The modularity function was proposed by Newman and Girvan[39] for evaluating the whether the division of a network into communities is good or bad. Let 𝐴 𝑖𝑗 be a node in an adjacency matrix A of the network, equivalent to a window bin in a Hi-C intra-chromosomal interaction matrix, if 𝐴 𝑖𝑗 = 1 then two nodes (or window bins 𝑤 𝑖 and 𝑤 𝑗 ) are connected, otherwise 𝐴 𝑖𝑗 = 0 . Currently, only unweighted networks are considered in building the network communities. The fraction of edges that assigned to communities (e.g., a node i belong to community 𝑐 𝑖 ) is 𝐹𝐸 = ∑ 𝐴𝑖𝑗 (𝑐𝑖, 𝑐𝑗) 𝑖𝑗 ∑ 𝐴𝑖𝑗 𝑖𝑗 = 1 2𝑚 ∑ 𝐴 𝑖𝑗 (𝑐 𝑖 , 𝑐 𝑗 ) 𝑖𝑗 where  (𝑐 𝑖 , 𝑐 𝑗 ) = 1 if 𝑐 𝑖 = 𝑐 𝑗 and 0 otherwise, and m is the total number of edges in the graph. The expected fraction of edges assigned to communities in a randomized network is 𝐸 = 1 2𝑚 ∑ 𝑘 𝑖 𝑘 𝑗 2𝑚  (𝑐 𝑖 , 𝑐 𝑗 ) 𝑖𝑗 10 where 𝑘 𝑖 = ∑ 𝐴 𝑖𝑗 𝑗 is the degree of node i in a network. Subsequently, a modularity function 𝑄 = 𝐹𝐸 − 𝐸 [38] to evaluate the division of the network can be obtained. If the FE is close to E, except in the case of randomized network, then the modularity score Q will be close to zero. In order words, a higher value from modularity function Q indicates a better division of community structure in a network. Usually, a modularity score Q above 0.3 may suggest of significant community structure in a network[39]. To search for optimized community structure of a big network based on the modularity function, SLM algorithm[38] (a procedure of the local moving heuristic) is used: to repeatedly move one node from one community to another that increasing the modularity score Q. After many iterations, the final assignment of nodes to communities will be reached if no nodes can be moved further to increase the Q. Please refer to previous publications [38-40] for more detailed descriptions of SLM algorithm in large network structure study. Determining the minimum size of valid communities Here, a new method is developed to estimate the minimum size of valid communities following a specific window bin size or interaction resolution. For example, a minimum size of valid communities (or network clusters) is determined by the predicted communities of intra- chromosomal interactions at a predefined resolution (e.g., window bin size=500kb). First, the communities with only one node are removed, and the number of identified communities in a chromosome r is defined as 𝐶 𝑟 . Then, the number of edges in a community (or network cluster) j for chromosome r is defined as 𝑒 𝑟𝑗 , where 𝑟 ∈ {1,2, ⋯ ,23} , and 𝑗 ∈ {1,2, ⋯ , 𝐶 𝑟 } . Since both the number of edges and the size of communities are dependent on the nodes number of a network, which are further determined by the resolution of network (e.g., the choice of window bin size), the number of edges 𝑒 𝑟𝑗 may not reflect the real-world scale of a network when different network resolution is used (e.g., window bin size = 500kb, 100kb, or 50kb). Thus, 11 𝑒 𝑟𝑗 needs to be normalized against a specific window bin size (or network resolution) by equation 𝑝 𝑟𝑗 = 𝑒 𝑟𝑗 𝑒 𝑗 ̅ , where 𝑒 𝑗 ̅ = ∑ 𝑒𝑟𝑗 𝑟,𝑗 ∑ 𝐶𝑟 𝑟 is the average number of edges of all chromosomes at the same network resolution. Subsequently, a predefined percentage value p (e.g., 𝑝 = 0.02 ) can be set to find communities with at least p percentage (e.g., 2% in this work) of the average number of edges based on equation 𝑝 ∗ = 𝑎 𝑟 𝑔𝑚𝑖𝑛 𝑝𝑟𝑗 |𝑝 𝑟𝑗 − 𝑝|, where the closest value 𝑝 ∗ to 𝑝 is identified and the corresponding number of expected edges 𝑒 ∗ is calculated by 𝑒 ∗ = 𝑝 ∗ 𝑒 𝑗 ̅, which is the expected minimum size (or number of edges) of valid communities in a network at the chosen interaction resolution. Based on the predefined threshold value p, the expected minimum size of valid communities in a community interaction network can be determined by 𝑒 ∗ (e.g., the number of edges for valid communities > 𝑒 ∗ ) and estimated automatically for different Hi-C interaction networks at different resolutions (or window bin size). Please note that the edges of intercommunity interactions are not considered in the calculation. Thus, the number of identified total communities of chromosome r will be reduced from 𝐶 𝑟 to 𝑉 𝑟 after filtering communities that do not reach the minimum size (or the number of edges) of valid ones. Inferring communities and genomic feature matrices based on intra-chromosomal interactions First, an intra-chromosomal interaction matrix H (e.g., a normalized Hi-C contact count or Z- score matrix) is converted to an adjacency matrix A based on a predefined resolution (e.g., 12 window bin size = 500Kb). Then, multi-omics datasets 𝐻 (1) , ⋯ , 𝐻 (𝐺 ) from various genomic features are used to build genomic feature matrices 𝐹 (1) , ⋯ , 𝐹 (𝐺 ) follow the adjacency matrix A, where G is the number of genomic features (e.g., gene expressions, nucleosome density/DNase-seq, histone modifications for enhancer “H3K4me1 and H3K27ac”, promoter “H3K4me3”, repressor “H3K9me3 and H3K27me3”, or insulator “CTCF”). The weights of genomic features are assigned to the edges of feature matrix F based on intra-chromosomal interactions in adjacency matrix A. Subsequently, SLM algorithm is applied on the unweighted adjacency matrix A (e.g., with a window bin size=500kb) to predict intra-chromosomal community interactions. After determining the minimum size (or number of edges) of valid communities, the valid communities V (or network clusters) are used in further data analysis such as the genomic feature enrichment and the differential network analysis. Evaluating genomic feature enrichment in intra-chromosomal interaction communities Based on the community network, an enrichment of various genomic features in valid intra- chromosomal communities can be evaluated. For instance, to evaluate the difference of genomic feature l between the inside community ( 𝐹 𝑣(𝑙) ) and the outside community ( 𝐹 𝑣′(𝑙) ), a two-sample T-test is applied on each valid community (or a network cluster), such as the T- value of feature l is 𝑇 𝑖(𝑙) = 𝑇 𝑡 𝑒𝑠𝑡 (𝐹 𝑣(𝑙) , 𝐹 𝑣′(𝑙) ), where 𝐹 𝑣(𝑙) represents the observed genomic feature l within the valid community v, while 𝐹 𝑣′(𝑙) is the expected genomic feature from randomly selected intra-chromosomal interactions (e.g., drawn from outside community v but with the same size as 𝐹 𝑣(𝑙) ). Meanwhile, the P-value (e.g., 𝑃 𝑖(𝑙) ) of the corresponding 𝑇 𝑖(𝑙) indicates whether there is a significant enrichment of genomic feature l at the community in sampling i or not (e.g., a significance level 𝛼 = 0.01 ). To obtain 13 an expected P-value ( 𝑃 (𝑙) ) for the enrichment of genomic feature l in a community, the random permutation test is repeated N times (e.g., resampling 1000 times) then calculate 𝑃 (𝑙) = ∑ Ι {𝑃𝑖(𝑙)<𝛼} 𝑁 𝑖=1 𝑁 , a small 𝑃 (𝑙) indicates a significant feature enrichment in the community when it is compared against randomly drew samples outside the community. Subsequently, an expected T-value for the enrichment of genomic feature l in a community is 𝑇 (𝑙) = ∑ 𝑇 𝑖(𝑙) 𝑁 𝑖=1 𝑁 The permutation test is performed at each genomic feature l to access its overall enrichment in a community (or network cluster), respectively. question: translate the following to arabic : ( Case example ‘It’s an itchy bottom,’ Lucy’s mum says. Lucy Godfrey (4), a bit shy, hides her head in mum’s arm. Her younger brother sits unconcernedly kicking his heels in his little chair. ‘Oh dear’ you say. ‘Can you tell me a bit more?’ ‘Well it’s been going on for a bit’ says her mother Lisa Godfrey. ‘She’s had it for about 2 months, before that she was fine. She’s been itchy during the day but for the last few nights she’s been waking up screaming and I’ve even had to get her up and wash her bottom before she settles. It’s been quite awful actually.’ ‘Is there anything to see?’ you ask. Her mum shakes her head. ‘Just a bit pink around the, you know, back bottom.’ ‘Any pets at home?’ you ask. ‘Or does Lucy suck her thumb or bite her nails at all?’ ‘No pets. But she does suck her fingers at night. She has done since she was small.’ Lucy holds up the first two fingers of her left hand and demonstrates unnecessarily. ‘Because I’m thinking of worms,’ you say. ‘Oh,’ says the mum. ‘Well, there are other things that cause an itchy bottom. In fact, it’s so common it’s got a special name: pruritis ani. Hygiene is the first to mention because sometimes children this age have difficulty wiping their bottoms properly and any poo left behind is a great irritant to the skin and can cause itching.’ You glance at the mum who nods slowly and says ‘Lucy’s not too bad for that.’ You continue, ‘OK. Another common cause is a thrush infection, which can be easily treated with Canesten. There are other conditions related to eczema like something called lichen sclerosis but that’s more common in adults, not really children. But the reason I’m thinking of worms rather than hygiene or eczema is because worms come out of the back passage at night to lay their eggs and that’s when the bottom is itchiest. It fits best with your description of what has been happening with Lucy.’ Lisa Godfrey is nodding. ‘Ok. I had worms once as a child. It was disgusting but I grew up on a farm.’ ‘Because Lucy sucks her fingers it means if she does have a threadworm infection and scratches her bottom she can get the eggs under her nails and then re-ingest them. That’s how people get an infestation of worms. Apparently a lot of us have a threadworm infection quite often but if we don’t re-ingest the eggs it’s just one worm and it eventually dies. It’s very easily treated,’ you add. ‘But you have to treat the whole family, all at the same time. It’s a one-off treatment; a liquid that you swallow.’ ‘Can we test for it?’ Lucy’s mum asks. ‘We can send off a stool sample, and the classic test is to go in at night with a torch and check the child’s bottom to see if there are any worms there.’ Mrs Godfrey grimaces. ‘Or other people put 38 Gastrointestinal Sellotape over the bottom to capture the worm or eggs that way . . . Or we could just swab and then treat. Can I have a look at Lucy’s bottom?’ Lucy is not keen but her mum convinces her to stand on her lap and lowers her pants. Her younger brother wanders around the room ignoring the commotion. You put on some gloves and pause. This examination position is not ideal. ‘Let’s get you over here on my special bed,’ you suggest to Lucy. Her mum carries Lucy over objecting strenuously. ‘If you just lie on your side and tuck your legs up,’ you request. Lucy curls up her legs firmly together. You keep mum at Lucy’s head end cuddling her, and say ‘Now I’m just going to look at your bottom. I’ll be very quick.’ Lucy’s anus is a normal colour, it is clean, there is no surrounding redness or lesions, and no obvious threadworm. Threadworm eggs are too small to see except under a microscope. You take a plain swab (no gel in the base) and moisten it with saline from a saline pod. ‘I’m just going to take the swab,’ you say to Mrs Godfrey and then to Lucy, ‘I’m just going to take a swab with this special cotton wool on a stick. You might feel a tickly feeling on your bottom,’ and quickly but gently wipe the swab around and over the anus to pick up any possible eggs present before Lucy has time to wriggle too much. ‘All done,’ you say. ‘That looks fine, no thrush, nice and clean . . . What shall we do then?’ you ask the mum who is pulling up Lucy’s things. Lucy jumps down and joins her brother. ‘Can you give enough treatment for the four of us?’ asks Mrs Godfrey. You nod and also print off a leaflet and circle the paragraphs about nail cleaning, washing in the morning, and also on hand washing before food preparation and cleaning the bedding. ‘Here’s the prescription. It’s for a liquid called mebendazole. Get everyone to take it tonight and then again in a week’s time.’ Lisa Godfrey is reading the leaflet as you speak and looks up and nods, folding it to look at properly later. ‘Ok, thank you. If we have any other problems we’ll get back in touch.’ One week later you receive confirmation from the laboratory that threadworm ova were present on the swab. )

"حسنًا. لقد كانت لدي ديدان مرة واحدة عندما كنت طفلة. كانت مقرفة ولكن نشأت على مزرعة." تقول: "لأن لوسي تمتص أصابعها، إذا كان لديها عدوى بديدان الأمعاء وتحكّ في مؤخرتها، يمكن أن تحصل على بيوض الديدان تحت أظافرها وتبتلعها مرة أخرى. هذا كيف يحدث انتشار الديدان. على ما يبدو أن الكثير منا يُصاب بعدوى ديدان الأمعاء كثيرًا ولكن إذا لم نبتلع البيوض مرة أخرى ، سيكون هناك ديدان فقط وفي النهاية ستموت. علاجها سهل جدًا،" تضيف "ولكن يجب علاج العائلة بأكملها في نفس الوقت. إنه علاج مرة واحدة ؛ سائل يتم ابتلاعه." تسأل أم لوسي: "هل يمكننا إجراء اختبار لذلك؟" تجيب: "يمكننا إرسال عينة براز والاختبار التقليدي هو الذهاب في الليل بمصباح يدوي وفحص مؤخرة الطفل لمعرفة ما إذا كان هناك أي ديدان هناك." تعبّر السيدة جودفري عن استياءها. "أو يمكن للآخرين أن يضعوا شريطة لاصقة على المؤخرة لالتقاط الديدان أو البيض بهذه الطريقة... أو يمكننا ببساطة أن نأخذ عينة ونعالج. هل يمكنني أن أرى مؤخرة لوسي؟" لوسي ليست حريصة ولكن أمها تقنعها بأن تقف على ركبتيها وتخفض سروالها. يتجول أخوها الأصغر في الغرفة يتجاهل الضجة. تضع قفازات وتتوقف. هذا الموقف الفحص ليس مثاليًا. "لنذهب إلى السرير الخاص بي هنا" ، تقترح لوسي. تحمل أمها لوسي معارضة بشدة. "إذا فقط اضطجعي هنا على جانبك وارفعي ساقيك" ، تطلب. تثني لوسي ساقيها محكمة معًا. تحتفظ أنت بأمها بجوار رأس لوسي وتقول: "الآن سأنظر إلى مؤخرتك. سأكون سريعة جدًا." مؤخرة لوسي ذات لون طبيعي، نظيفة، لا يوجد احمرار حولها أو طفح جلدي ولا وجود واضح لديدان. بيض الديدان صغيرة جدًا لا يمكن رؤيتها إلا تحت الميكروسكوب. تأخذ عينة عادية (بدون جل في القاع) وتبللها بمحلول ملحي من كبسولة محلول ملحي. "سأأخذ العينة فقط" تقول للسيدة جودفري وبعد ذلك للوسي: "سأأخذ عينة بواسطة قطنة خاصة على عصا. قد تشعرين بشعور مقزز على مؤخرتك" ثم تمسح العينة بسرعة ولكن بلطف حول وفوق فتحة الشرج لالتقاط أي بيوض ممكنة قبل أن يتمكن لوسي من التحرك كثيرًا. تقول: "انتهينا. يبدو ذلك على ما يرام، لا يوجد تدرن، نظيف بشكل جيد... ماذا علينا أن نفعل إذن؟" تسأل الأم التي ترفع ملابس لوسي. تنزلق لوسي وتنضم إلى أخيها. تسمح ليزا جودفري بالإيضاح: "هل يمكنك توفير العلاج الكافي لأربعة منا؟" توافق برأسه وتطبع أيضًا نشرة وتحيط بفقرات التنظيف الأظافر، وغسل في الصباح، وكذلك غسل اليدين قبل إعداد الطعام وتنظيف الفراش. Date: [25/06/2023] Time: 11:27-11: 54 Location: Bathroom Reporter: Students Let the teachers (Mam Yolanda) know and Mam Lebogang Channe wrote the incident form for the injured learner. Incident Details: On 25/05/2023 Nkazimulo Zulu, a learner in 4C, went to the bathroom with some of his friends during break time. While inside the bathroom, he slipped and fell, resulting in an injury. The incident was first reported to Teacher Yolanda Mouton who was in the building Corridor, who was on duty monitoring the hallway just outside the bathroom. Teacher Yolanda immediately alerted the break duty teachers, Teacher Lebo and Rosa, who referred the learner to the first aiders. After a thorough assessment, the first aiders found that Nkazimulo Zulu had pain on her hand although they could not pick up where the learner had sustained a sprain/fracture. They provided him with immediate first aid assessment, which included asking her to elevate her arm and also applying some minimal pressure on the hand which the learner had pointed as the affected area. Although they could not ascertain the severity of the injury the first aiders advised that Nkazimulo Zulu be taken to the school sick room so that her parents be notified of the incident. Conclusion: In conclusion, Nkazimulo Zulu, a learner in grade 4C got injured during break time, sustaining a hand injury. The incident was reported to teacher Yolanda, who immediately alerted the break duty teachers, Teacher Lebo and Rosa. The first aiders, Mam Nthabiseng and Mr Mhlanga, assessed the child for injuries and provided immediate first aid treatment. Nkazimulo Zulu was advised to be taken to the school sick room for notification of her parents about the incident.
reference: Additionally, investigations were conducted on the footage from the bathroom to determine the cause of the injury. However, no evidence indicating foul play was found on the footage. Students who were in the bathroom at the time of the incident were also asked to provide any information they knew about the incident. None of the students indicated that they had seen anything that could have caused the injury. The incident report was submitted to the school's administration for review and to ensure that appropriate measures are taken to prevent similar incidents from occurring in the future. The school will also provide support to Nkazimulo Zulu and their family as they recover from the injury.
